evaluation_layout.scope: Physical numbering is shared across editions. Some labels have multiple panels. Twenty-six of the 29 evaluation folio numbers also occur on separate training sides or panels. The public partitions do not represent 29 independent held-out physical leaves.

fixed_block_design.blocks: Rank distinct numbered physical folios in canonical ZL first-observed order, and assign rank i to quartile floor(4*i/N). Analyze the four quartiles independently in each practice partition, keeping page panels of a folio together. Evaluation is primary. Training quartiles are descriptive because these pages set the common period. The ZL/IT results are alternative readings of the same loci, not independent cohorts.
fixed_block_design.calibration: Check vectorized spectral power against the published direct Fourier code on the same exact observed stream to numerical tolerance. Confirm the original injected periodic glyph in the exact replay of #515, and separate each new null's scope from that reconstruction.

layout.continuous_1024: administrative quartile stream with 1,024-position nonoverlapping Hann windows
layout.within_folio_512: 512-position windows taken only within one physical folio; omit each folio's residual tail

fixed_block_design.null: Use 99 shuffles from each endpoint-preserving folio-interior and line-interior permutation. Within a quartile and edition, feed identical permuted glyph streams into all window modes. Use seed 692615 plus 1000 for the line null. Preserve comparison boundaries and count ties against a positive upper-tail excess. Report supports, unavailable quartile geometry, and descriptive p-values. Give combined evidence only when the same prespecified broad or maximum statistic is positive in both editions of a fixed public evaluation block; otherwise no positive criterion is proposed. Do not recenter based on a measured peak.
fixed_block_design.scope: Public practice only. Keep the exact strict paired loci and raw spaceless EVA representation from #515. Keep its already published period of 44. The 0.90–1.10 center band and shoulder factors 0.65–0.80 and 1.25–1.50 are fixed.
fixed_block_design.scored_prefix_sensitivity: Before observing results, add a within-folio 512 null that shuffles only the retained prefix interior slots of each folio. This avoids changing the scored glyph stock by exchanging with a truncated folio tail. It preserves original line endpoints even when a 512-window boundary falls inside a line. Use 99 draws and seed 695615.
fixed_block_design.spectrum: Compare wide band mean, the nearest center Fourier bin selected before observations (lower bin on a tie), and maximum over the entire fixed center band. Divide each by the mean of the two shoulder means. For nearest-bin sensitivity also report fixed center bins closest to periods 0.95, 1.00 and 1.05 times 44, ranked against their own permutations. Use the simultaneous maximum of the center bins for an arbitrary narrow spike anywhere in the band.

findings: All registered training, evaluation, pulse and geometry figures match exactly.
The pulse avoided altering line-edge positions after a global glyph shuffle. It therefore keeps the endpoints of the randomized background, rather than restoring the original manuscript glyphs.

The exact original folio-interior null preserves the complete folio’s stock. It exchanges characters with the omitted tail of a truncated scored prefix. Independent seed checks verified the original endpoint and full-stock invariants in both views.

reproduction.usage: Extract the two exact scripts from the original experiment to one directory, and save the new block_sensitivity.py beside them. detail.statement: The two original public scripts reproduce #515 exactly, including the detected 44.52-character pulse. Four fixed physical folio blocks show no nominal p at or below .05 for the broad band, nearest bin, or center-band maximum in either continuous window size under the two endpoint-preserving nulls. Restricting 512-character windows to each folio gives one local paired excess, the f53–f85 block, where line-interior shuffling gives broad-band p values .02 in ZL and .05 in Takahashi, and nearest-bin .02 and .04. The broad-band ranks are .04 and .07 under folio-interior shuffling, including when scored glyph stock is exactly fixed. There is no positive criterion that is replicated across these tested nulls and layouts.

The first prints one line per key and must reproduce the four paired savings values, verdicts and coverage ranges recorded here on commit 20dd02a; the second lists every registered result on the Claston v101 transliteration with its scoring time and whether it predates the fix. Both read only the public practice partition and only frozen registered submissions - no key is edited and no held-out page is touched. The open decision stays with the scorer: whether the eight pre-fix v101 rows need a corrected held-out run. Our reading is that the two Hannig keys do not need an emergency re-score (the shift is at most 0.011 savings and the verdict is unchanged), while the seven search keys with empty uppercase maps are the ones whose registered input the fix actually rewrites, and the project should state explicitly whether an undefined uppercase v101 glyph is a null or a lowercase alias.

findings: Paired public reruns on the same 34 practice evaluation pages (commit 20dd02a, frozen registered submissions, no key edited). Savings with case preserved, then with the old coercion re-applied, then the difference: K-hebrew-substitution-002 (PR #185) -0.23668 / -0.23036 / -0.00632; K-hebrew-substitution-004 (PR #560) -0.23990 / -0.22893 / -0.01097; K-english-substitution-004 -0.11055 / -0.08568 / -0.02487; K-latin-substitution-006 -0.10408 / -0.08545 / -0.01863. The sign is the same for all four: the coercion made the registered numbers look better than the fixed parser produces.

No verdict changes. All four keys fail the same five criteria in both modes - a_compresses, b_reads, kill_tests, c_pictures and d_not_illusion - so the fix does not rescue or sink any of these submissions.

Lexicon-coverage ranges over judged sections move with the input, not monotonically. K-hebrew-002 is unchanged at 0.36-0.48; K-hebrew-004 goes 0.2633-0.4313 (case preserved) against 0.24-0.4293 (coerced); K-english-004 0.3167-0.35 against 0.3095-0.35; K-latin-006 0.4467-0.5013 against 0.3967-0.4553. Dropping uppercase glyphs can raise coverage because the words that lose a letter also stop contributing junk.

The affected input is large. In the pinned Claston v101 parse, 6,418 of 40,174 word tokens (15.98 per cent) contain at least one uppercase glyph - 5,479 of 33,862 on the practice training side and 939 of 6,312 on the 34 evaluation pages - spread over 25 distinct uppercase forms, with C alone appearing 2,826 times. On the evaluation pages the two search keys change the decode of 939 words, K-hebrew-004 of 441 words, and K-hebrew-002 of 71 words.

Only one uppercase pair in the Hannig table actually disagrees: N maps to final pe while n maps to pe. The other seven uppercase entries (A, F, G, H, J, K, U) repeat their lowercase value, so for those the coercion was harmless. The Hannig keys define 8 uppercase forms, leaving 17 of the 25 forms undefined.

Seven of the nine registered v101 results have no uppercase entry at all in their key map. Before the fix every uppercase glyph silently took its lowercase value; after the fix the same glyph is a null, because vs/families/substitution.py documents a glyph missing from the key as a null and decode_word returns m.get(g, ""). So the merged fix is a decoder-behaviour change for those keys, not only a case correction.

Eight of the nine registered v101 results predate the fix (PR #510 merged 2026-11-26T17:23:14Z, commit e89497e): the seven search keys at 2026-11-25T05:42:08Z through 05:48:59Z and K-hebrew-substitution-002 at 2026-11-25T08:39:22Z. Only K-hebrew-substitution-004 (2026-11-26T18:59:51Z) was scored on the fixed parser. All nine are FAIL.
detail.interpretation: For the two Hannig keys the practical answer to PR #185's question is small: the coercion flattered the registered practice number by 0.006-0.011 savings and changed no verdict, so no emergency held-out re-score is implied. The reason it is small is that the Hannig key happens to define most of the uppercase forms it meets, and only one of them differs from its lowercase twin. The general problem is bigger than that case. Roughly one v101 word in six carries an uppercase glyph, and a key that does not define one used to fall back on the lowercase letter by accident rather than by decision. Seven registered search keys sit in that situation, and the measured shift for two of them (0.019-0.025 savings, plus a coverage range that moves by up to 5 points) is larger than the Hannig shift. Whether those rows should be re-scored is a scorer decision, and it depends on a policy question the project has not answered in writing: is an undefined uppercase v101 glyph a null, or does it inherit the lowercase reading? The fix chose null; the registered history assumed inheritance.
limits: Only four of the nine registered v101 results were re-scored; the other five search keys are listed with their scoring times and empty uppercase maps but no paired number was measured for them.
The practice evaluation split is 34 pages; the held-out pages that produce the authoritative verdict were not touched, so these deltas say nothing about the registered hidden-split numbers.
Lowercasing the parsed words emulates the removed coercion; it is equivalent for these keys but was not produced by reverting the parser itself.
Savings is one of five criteria and all four keys fail every criterion in both modes, so the measured shift cannot by itself change any verdict.
The uppercase-glyph counts are counts of parsed v101 tokens, not a claim about how the manuscript's capitalisation should be read.
detail.methods: The registered submissions are read back frozen from the registry (submitted['key.json']) and scored with the pinned judge on the practice split exactly as the scorer does: views.apply is applied to the submission's own scope before judge.evaluate, so the baseline model and the decoys see the same text as the candidate. The old behaviour is emulated by lowercasing the parsed words of both partitions before scoring, which is equivalent to the removed clean_text coercion because that coercion ran on the whole transcription before any consumer saw it. Case preservation is the tree's current behaviour, selected by the '#=IVTFF v101 ' header that the pinned Claston file carries, so the 'case preserved' column is a real run of the current code rather than an emulation. Affected-glyph tables count uppercase characters in the parsed evaluation words and compare key[g] with key[g.lower()]. Nothing is fitted, tuned or selected against the evaluation pages; the keys are frozen and the only variable is the coercion.

reproducibility.instructions: Extract the two embedded scripts to one temporary directory under the names listed. From the repository root, with the pinned Claston text fetched, run PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/l1004.py (about 4 minutes, eight judge runs) and PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/l1004_registered.py. Both only read the public practice partition and the registry; neither writes to the repository.

scripts.l1004.py:
"""P-L1-004: paired public reproduction of registered Claston-v101 keys with and without the
case coercion that PR #510 removed.

Old behaviour: vs/ivtff.clean_text lowercased every input, including Claston v101, so an
uppercase glyph entered the decoder as its lowercase form (and an unmapped uppercase form
silently acquired the lowercase mapping). New behaviour: case is preserved when the file
header starts with '#=IVTFF v101 '. Emulated here by re-parsing the same pages with the
coercion re-applied (equivalently: page words lowercased after parsing), which also puts the
coercion into the baseline model and the decoys, exactly as the old code did.
"""
import copy, hashlib, json, os, subprocess, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
from collections import Counter
from vs import corpus, judge, registry, views
from vs.models import scoped

REPO = os.getcwd()

def load_registered(item_id):
    from vs import registry
    return registry.get(item_id)["submitted"]["key.json"]

KEYS = {
    "K-hebrew-substitution-002 (PR #185, Hannig table, fleet-corpora)":
        ("registered", "K-hebrew-substitution-002"),
    "K-hebrew-substitution-004 (PR #560, Hannig table, mtx-light)":
        ("registered", "K-hebrew-substitution-004"),
    "K-english-substitution-004 (gc raw, glyphs reversed)":
        ("registered", "K-english-substitution-004"),
    "K-latin-substitution-006 (gc raw, words reversed)":
        ("registered", "K-latin-substitution-006"),
}

def lower_pages(pages):
    out = []
    for p in pages:
        q = copy.deepcopy(p)
        for ln in q.lines:
            ln.words = [w.lower() for w in ln.words]
        out.append(q)
    return out

def run(sub, train, ev):
    tr, ee = views.apply(scoped(train, sub.get("scope")), sub), views.apply(scoped(ev, sub.get("scope")), sub)
    return judge.evaluate(sub, tr, ee, "practice")

def sha(obj):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()

commit = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
train, ev = corpus.split_pages("practice", "gc")
train_c, ev_c = lower_pages(train), lower_pages(ev)

def glyph_table(sub, pages):
    m = sub["key"]["map"]
    cnt = Counter(ch for p in pages for ln in p.lines for w in ln.words for ch in w if ch.isupper())
    return [{"glyph": g, "occurrences": cnt[g], "case_preserved": m.get(g, ""), "coerced_to": m.get(g.lower(), "")}
            for g in sorted(cnt, key=lambda g: (-cnt[g], g)) if m.get(g, "") != m.get(g.lower(), "")]

out = {"commit": commit, "split": "practice", "pages_evaluated": len(ev),
       "coercion_emulation": "clean_text's lowercase coercion re-applied: page words lowercased after parsing, so the baseline model and the decoys see the coerced text too",
       "results": []}
for name, (_kind, item_id) in KEYS.items():
    sub = load_registered(item_id)
    a = run(sub, train, ev)
    b = run(sub, train_c, ev_c)
    cov = lambda r: [v["coverage"] for v in r["b_reads"]["sections"].values() if v.get("judged")]
    row = {"key": name, "item": item_id, "key_sha256": sha(sub),
           "transliteration": sub.get("transliteration", "zl"),
           "scored_at": str(registry.get(item_id)["provenance"].get("at")),
           "case_preserved": {"savings": a["a_compresses"]["savings"], "verdict": a["verdict"],
                              "failed": a["failed"], "coverage_min": round(min(cov(a)), 4),
                              "coverage_max": round(max(cov(a)), 4)},
           "coerced": {"savings": b["a_compresses"]["savings"], "verdict": b["verdict"],
                       "failed": b["failed"], "coverage_min": round(min(cov(b)), 4),
                       "coverage_max": round(max(cov(b)), 4)},
           "savings_delta": round(a["a_compresses"]["savings"] - b["a_compresses"]["savings"], 5),
           "verdict_changed": a["verdict"] != b["verdict"],
           "uppercase_glyphs_affected": glyph_table(sub, ev)}
    out["results"].append(row)
    print(row["key"], "| delta", row["savings_delta"], "| verdict", a["verdict"], "->", b["verdict"],
          "| affected glyphs", len(row["uppercase_glyphs_affected"]), flush=True)

json.dump(out, open('/tmp/l1004_results.json', 'w'), indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
print("WROTE /tmp/l1004_results.json")

"""P-L1-004: enumerate every registered result whose submission reads the Claston v101
transliteration, and mark which of them were scored before PR #510 removed the case coercion.

The fix was merged as commit e89497e at 2026-11-26T17:23:14Z; anything scored before that

detail.statement: PR #185 asked for the same Hannig key to be scored with and without the single case coercion that vs/ivtff.clean_text applied to every input, including Claston v101. PR #510 has since merged the parser half of that step: clean_text now takes preserve_case, and parse() turns it on for a file whose first line starts with '#=IVTFF v101 ', with a fixture that separates N from n. This submission closes the remaining half - the paired public reproduction - by re-scoring the frozen registered submissions on the same 34 public practice evaluation pages twice: once as the tree scores them today (case preserved), and once with the coercion re-applied after parsing, which puts the coerced text into the baseline model and the decoys exactly as the old code did. Four keys were measured: the two Hannig keys named in PR #185 and PR #560, and two search keys on the same Claston v101 transliteration whose key maps contain no uppercase entry at all. In all four cases the old coercion flattered the result - savings became less negative by 0.00632, 0.01097, 0.02487 and 0.01863 - and no verdict changed: all four still fail a_compresses, b_reads, kill_tests, c_pictures and d_not_illusion. The wider finding is the size of the affected input. 6,418 of 40,174 parsed v101 word tokens (15.98 per cent) contain at least one of 25 uppercase forms, so the coercion was not a corner case: it silently replaced the decoder input for about one word in six. Because a glyph missing from a key is a null, the fix is not only a case change - an uppercase form that no key defines now decodes to nothing instead of quietly borrowing its lowercase letter's value. Eight of the nine registered v101 results were scored before the fix merged, and seven of those eight have no uppercase entry in their key map, so their registered numbers all rest on the borrowed-lowercase behaviour.

experiment.json.summary: Paired public reruns of four frozen Claston-v101 keys show the removed case coercion flattered savings by 0.006-0.025 and flipped no verdict, while 16 per cent of v101 word tokens carry an uppercase glyph and eight registered v101 results predate the fix.

step.json.check: From the repository root with the pinned texts fetched, extract the two scripts below to one temporary directory and run them with PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/l1004.py and PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/l1004_registered.py. The first prints one line per key and must reproduce the four paired savings values, verdicts and coverage ranges recorded here on commit 20dd02a; the second lists every registered result on the Claston v101 transliteration with its scoring time and whether it predates the fix. Both read only the public practice partition and only frozen registered submissions - no key is edited and no held-out page is touched. The open decision stays with the scorer: whether the eight pre-fix v101 rows need a corrected held-out run. Our reading is that the two Hannig keys do not need an emergency re-score (the shift is at most 0.011 savings and the verdict is unchanged), while the seven search keys with empty uppercase maps are the ones whose registered input the fix actually rewrites, and the project should state explicitly whether an undefined uppercase v101 glyph is a null or a lowercase alias.
findings: Paired public reruns on the same 34 practice evaluation pages (commit 20dd02a, frozen registered submissions, no key edited). Savings with case preserved, then with the old coercion re-applied, then the difference: K-hebrew-substitution-002 (PR #185) -0.23668 / -0.23036 / -0.00632; K-hebrew-substitution-004 (PR #560) -0.23990 / -0.22893 / -0.01097; K-english-substitution-004 -0.11055 / -0.08568 / -0.02487; K-latin-substitution-006 -0.10408 / -0.08545 / -0.01863. The sign is the same for all four: the coercion made the registered numbers look better than the fixed parser produces.

No verdict changes. All four keys fail the same five criteria in both modes - a_compresses, b_reads, kill_tests, c_pictures and d_not_illusion - so the fix does not rescue or sink any of these submissions.

Lexicon-coverage ranges over judged sections move with the input, not monotonically. K-hebrew-002 is unchanged at 0.36-0.48; K-hebrew-004 goes 0.2633-0.4313 (case preserved) against 0.24-0.4293 (coerced); K-english-004 0.3167-0.35 against 0.3095-0.35; K-latin-006 0.4467-0.5013 against 0.3967-0.4553. Dropping uppercase glyphs can raise coverage because the words that lose a letter also stop contributing junk.

The affected input is large. In the pinned Claston v101 parse, 6,418 of 40,174 word tokens (15.98 per cent) contain at least one uppercase glyph - 5,479 of 33,862 on the practice training side and 939 of 6,312 on the 34 evaluation pages - spread over 25 distinct uppercase forms, with C alone appearing 2,826 times. On the evaluation pages the two search keys change the decode of 939 words, K-hebrew-004 of 441 words, and K-hebrew-002 of 71 words.

Only one uppercase pair in the Hannig table actually disagrees: N maps to final pe while n maps to pe. The other seven uppercase entries (A, F, G, H, J, K, U) repeat their lowercase value, so for those the coercion was harmless. The Hannig keys define 8 uppercase forms, leaving 17 of the 25 forms undefined.

Seven of the nine registered v101 results have no uppercase entry at all in their key map. Before the fix every uppercase glyph silently took its lowercase value; after the fix the same glyph is a null, because vs/families/substitution.py documents a glyph missing from the key as a null and decode_word returns m.get(g, ""). So the merged fix is a decoder-behaviour change for those keys, not only a case correction.

Eight of the nine registered v101 results predate the fix (PR #510 merged 2026-11-26T17:23:14Z, commit e89497e): the seven search keys at 2026-11-25T05:42:08Z through 05:48:59Z and K-hebrew-substitution-002 at 2026-11-25T08:39:22Z. Only K-hebrew-substitution-004 (2026-11-26T18:59:51Z) was scored on the fixed parser. All nine are FAIL.
step.json.interpretation: For the two Hannig keys the practical answer to PR #185's question is small: the coercion flattered the registered practice number by 0.006-0.011 savings and changed no verdict, so no emergency held-out re-score is implied. The reason it is small is that the Hannig key happens to define most of the uppercase forms it meets, and only one of them differs from its lowercase twin. The general problem is bigger than that case. Roughly one v101 word in six carries an uppercase glyph, and a key that does not define one used to fall back on the lowercase letter by accident rather than by decision. Seven registered search keys sit in that situation, and the measured shift for two of them (0.019-0.025 savings, plus a coverage range that moves by up to 5 points) is larger than the Hannig shift. Whether those rows should be re-scored is a scorer decision, and it depends on a policy question the project has not answered in writing: is an undefined uppercase v101 glyph a null, or does it inherit the lowercase reading? The fix chose null; the registered history assumed inheritance.
limits: Only four of the nine registered v101 results were re-scored; the other five search keys are listed with their scoring times and empty uppercase maps but no paired number was measured for them.
The practice evaluation split is 34 pages; the held-out pages that produce the authoritative verdict were not touched, so these deltas say nothing about the registered hidden-split numbers.
Lowercasing the parsed words emulates the removed coercion; it is equivalent for these keys but was not produced by reverting the parser itself.
Savings is one of five criteria and all four keys fail every criterion in both modes, so the measured shift cannot by itself change any verdict.
The uppercase-glyph counts are counts of parsed v101 tokens, not a claim about how the manuscript's capitalisation should be read.
step.json.methods: The registered submissions are read back frozen from the registry (submitted['key.json']) and scored with the pinned judge on the practice split exactly as the scorer does: views.apply is applied to the submission's own scope before judge.evaluate, so the baseline model and the decoys see the same text as the candidate. The old behaviour is emulated by lowercasing the parsed words of both partitions before scoring, which is equivalent to the removed clean_text coercion because that coercion ran on the whole transcription before any consumer saw it. Case preservation is the tree's current behaviour, selected by the '#=IVTFF v101 ' header that the pinned Claston file carries, so the 'case preserved' column is a real run of the current code rather than an emulation. Affected-glyph tables count uppercase characters in the parsed evaluation words and compare key[g] with key[g.lower()]. Nothing is fitted, tuned or selected against the evaluation pages; the keys are frozen and the only variable is the coercion.

reproducibility.instructions: Extract the two embedded scripts to one temporary directory under the names listed. From the repository root, with the pinned Claston text fetched, run PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/l1004.py (about 4 minutes, eight judge runs) and PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/l1004_registered.py. Both only read the public practice partition and the registry; neither writes to the repository.

case coercion that PR #510 removed.

uppercase glyph entered the decoder as its lowercase form (and an unmapped uppercase form
silently acquired the lowercase mapping). New behaviour: case is preserved when the file
header starts with '#=IVTFF v101 '. Emulated here by re-parsing the same pages with the
coercion re-applied (equivalently: page words lowercased after parsing), which also puts the
coercion into the baseline model and the decoys, exactly as the old code did.
"""

    return [{"glyph": g, "occurrences": cnt[g], "case_preserved": m.get(g, ""), "coerced_to": m.get(g.lower(), "")}
            for g in sorted(cnt, key=lambda g: (-cnt[g], g)) if m.get(g, "") != m.get(g.lower(), "")]

check: Compare all eight planted final rates under 0%, 50%, 90% and 100% fixed line endings. Confirm the baseline result matches the merged pilot, report per-seed power and uncertainty, and verify that 100% fixation produces no rejections by construction.

detail.check: Compare all eight planted final rates under 0%, 50%, 90% and 100% fixed line endings. Confirm the baseline result matches the merged pilot, report per-seed power and uncertainty, and verify that 100% fixation produces no rejections by construction.
detail.findings: The unchanged base plan reproduced every stored pilot rejection count and interval. Across the three new layout/mask/simulation seeds, at a 5% final rate and 1% interior rate, mean rejection probability was 0.713 (range 0.703–0.721) with no endpoints fixed, 0.370 (0.364–0.381) with half fixed, 0.037 (0.037–0.039) with 90% fixed, and 0 at full fixation. At a 10% final rate the corresponding means were 0.997, 0.889, 0.185 and 0. At the 1% null the mean rejection rate remained below alpha in every condition; fully fixed endpoints yielded zero rejections. The direction and scale of the power loss persisted across the three independent public layouts and masks.
detail.interpretation: The pilot conclusion is robust over these sampled public layouts: endpoint-fixing nulls can sharply reduce power to detect a terminal effect. detail.statement: I checked the Yale f100r scan at full-page and detail scales, the actual illustrated article, the pinned ZL label locus, and a within-manuscript comparator. The inset on printed page 72 of the publisher's full HerbalGram 100 PDF directly reproduces this exact object and its label, so the authors' plant No. 8 is securely located beside ZL f100r.8 soity; the inference from plant No. 4 is unnecessary. I agree with that location and with N-011's warning of uncertainty. I dissent from confirming the named lexical anchor: a flattened green outline with marginal projections and a few interior marks is compatible with a cactus pad but does not distinguish one from a leaf-like object in this drawing style. On the same page, marginal teeth occur on other drawings. The leaves on f26r provide a closer documented control for this inference: several have an oval-to-obovate outline with stout marginal projections, attached by long petioles to slender axes bearing terminal clusters. This does not prove they are the same plant as f100r.8; it demonstrates that this outline is not diagnostic of an Opuntia pad. I cannot resolve an organized areole/glochid pattern, a pad joint, or a distinctive fruit apex in f100r.8 at the scan scale reviewed. Those are unobserved details, not proof that a stylized drawing could not represent a cactus. Modern botanical guidance also cautions against two easy exclusions: O. ficus-indica can lack large spines, and detached stem fragments can root. Thus the narrow base/root and sparse spines are not decisive counterarguments. The reviewed literature supplies one proposed identification and its proposed Nahuatl reading, not two independent published identifications of this drawing. Agreement with a label's position does not independently verify its meaning. Keep the Opuntia/nochtli/nashtli association disputed pending diagnostic comparative evidence and an independently justified reading; do not replace it with an invented alternative taxon.

Report all attempted and accepted pairs, joint readable denominator, broad curl-family versus other agreement, exact agreement, agreement with v101 (N maps to A, n maps to B), undecided rates, and whether relative stroke count is smaller, tied, larger, or unresolved for N versus n in the matching pair. Report by hand descriptively. Leave human rereading and inference about separate letters outside the measured claim.

plan.selection: Use the case-sensitive pinned v101 reading. Restrict to certain paragraph words of length at least three ending in n or N with identical preceding strings on the same page. Take one pair per physical folio and at most three folios per hand for hands 1, 2, 3. Rank by absolute line-number distance, then absolute within-line ordinal difference, canonical page order, uppercase line and ordinal, and lowercase line and ordinal. Inspect the first three per hand or all where fewer than three exist. Keep failures to match the scan visible. Read only complete pairs in the primary comparison.

"""Make two randomly ordered masked panels using unchanged Yale crop pixels."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
from random import Random
import sys

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

work = Path(sys.argv[1])
old = work.parent / 'voynich-v101-scan-work'
source = Path('experiments/K-010-open-1/mubadala777/step.json')
new = json.loads((work / 'selected-crops.json').read_text())
old_rows = json.loads(source.read_text())['results']['trials']
controls = [row for row in old_rows if row['v101_shape'] in ('C','D')]
rows = [{'locus': row['locus'], 'word_ordinal': row['word_ordinal'], 'v101': row['v101'],
         'xyxy': row['xyxy'], 'scan_crop': row['scan_crop'], 'source': 'control', 'expected': row['v101_shape']}
        for row in controls]
rows += [dict(row, source='new', expected={'N':'A','n':'B'}[row['v101'][-1]]) for row in new]
rows.sort(key=lambda row:(row['locus'],row['word_ordinal']))
rng = Random(374201)
labels = rng.sample(range(100, 1000), len(rows))
for label, row in zip(labels, rows):
    row['tile'] = f'Q{label:03d}'
(work / 'sealed-key.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + '\n')

font = ImageFont.truetype('/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf', 18)
columns, width, height = 3, 320, 140
for reader, seed in [('a',49741),('b',92651)]:
    shuffled = list(rows)
    Random(seed).shuffle(shuffled)
    panel = Image.new('RGB', (columns * width, ((len(rows)+columns-1)//columns)*height), 'white')
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(panel)
    for i,row in enumerate(shuffled):
        page = row['locus'].partition('.')[0]
        image_path = (old if row['source']=='control' else work) / f'{page}.jpg'
        with Image.open(image_path) as image:
            letter = image.crop(tuple(row['xyxy']))
        scale = min(1.5, 290 / letter.width, 104 / letter.height)
        letter = letter.resize((round(letter.width * scale),round(letter.height * scale)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)

scripts.panels.py:
"""Make two randomly ordered masked panels using unchanged Yale crop pixels."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
from random import Random
import sys

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

work = Path(sys.argv[1])
old = work.parent / 'voynich-v101-scan-work'
source = Path('experiments/K-010-open-1/mubadala777/step.json')
new = json.loads((work / 'selected-crops.json').read_text())
old_rows = json.loads(source.read_text())['results']['trials']
controls = [row for row in old_rows if row['v101_shape'] in ('C','D')]
rows = [{'locus': row['locus'], 'word_ordinal': row['word_ordinal'], 'v101': row['v101'],
         'xyxy': row['xyxy'], 'scan_crop': row['scan_crop'], 'source': 'control', 'expected': row['v101_shape']}
        for row in controls]
rows += [dict(row, source='new', expected={'N':'A','n':'B'}[row['v101'][-1]]) for row in new]
rows.sort(key=lambda row:(row['locus'],row['word_ordinal']))
rng = Random(374201)
labels = rng.sample(range(100, 1000), len(rows))
for label, row in zip(labels, rows):
    row['tile'] = f'Q{label:03d}'
(work / 'sealed-key.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + '\n')

font = ImageFont.truetype('/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf', 18)
columns, width, height = 3, 320, 140
for reader, seed in [('a',49741),('b',92651)]:
    shuffled = list(rows)
    Random(seed).shuffle(shuffled)
    panel = Image.new('RGB', (columns * width, ((len(rows)+columns-1)//columns)*height), 'white')
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(panel)
    for i,row in enumerate(shuffled):
        page = row['locus'].partition('.')[0]
        image_path = (old if row['source']=='control' else work) / f'{page}.jpg'
        with Image.open(image_path) as image:
            letter = image.crop(tuple(row['xyxy']))
        scale = min(1.5, 290 / letter.width, 104 / letter.height)
        letter = letter.resize((round(letter.width * scale),round(letter.height * scale)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
        x,y = (i % columns)*width,(i // columns)*height
        draw.text((x+8,y+3),row['tile'],font=font,fill='black')
        panel.paste(letter,(x+(width-letter.width)//2,y+29+(104-letter.height)//2))
        draw.rectangle((x,y,x+width-1,y+height-1),outline='#d4d4d4')
    panel.save(work/f'masked-panel-{reader}.png')

statement: The scribe keeps, for each (section, Currier language) group, a stack of word slips built from the group's training words in the order they were first met, a word met often contributing more slips than one met rarely. A pointer walks that stack a slip or two per page and a tray holds the last 200 slips it passed, so pages near each other in the book draw on nearly the same slips while pages far apart do not. The word written is chosen by where it stands: the opening glyph is read from a fitted table (paragraph-opening line first word, line first word, rest of a paragraph-opening line, mid-line, where the mid-line table is that of the last glyph of the word just written on the line, so a line's words are linked edge to edge and the link breaks at a line break); the scribe then takes a tray slip that BEGINS with that glyph and, at the end of a line, that also ENDS with a glyph the line-final table offers, writing the slip unchanged. When no slip fits, the word is composed glyph by glyph from a 5-glyph chain fitted on the group and backing off to the whole book, then opened and closed by the same tables. A word may instead be copied from the last 16 words of the page and changed in exactly one place, the copy being finished for its position first so a line-final m-word cannot carry its m into the middle of a line. Word length follows the fitted mean length of the position class, and the tables are read at a sharpness of 0.55 so the commoner entry is likelier. Fitted on the practice training pages only, written onto every page of the book in order.

public_advisory_rehearsal.scope: The declared selection is pooled and includes single-word and two-word lines, which have a final but no strict interior slot. The full whole-line null moves every word, including the original first word and uncertain tokens. Its treatment of certainty is part of the frozen specification. The separate exact diagnostic holds the initial and uncertain slots fixed and requires one certain final and at least one certain interior. The fixed-width control uses one glyph of space and a specified independent length mixture. Results concern that simplified wrap and this type of short-word abundance. public_advisory_rehearsal.summary: Practice evaluation ratios are 1.15745 in ZL, 1.31530 in Takahashi and 1.11877 in RF. The first two pass the fixed upper-tail whole-line test at p=.0025 and RF gives p=.0425. The 3–5 word diagnostic is at or below one in all three editions. At six or more words the ratios are 1.22159, 1.39140 and 1.17846. Keeping initial and uncertain positions fixed in a separate exact conditional test yields p=.00423, .00000135 and .05934 in the same order. Exchangeable and long-initial-only controls pass 0 of 16 each; adding a fixed terminal short-word preference passes 16 of 16. Greedy wraps of independent lengths in widths 40, 50 and 60 pass 0 of 10 each, with median final-to-interior ratios below 0.94.

"""Frozen production-model comparison, with synthetic sensitivity controls first."""
from collections import Counter
import copy
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from random import Random
import subprocess
import sys

here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
repo = here / "voynich-swarm"
os.chdir(repo)
sys.path.insert(0, str(repo))
from vs import corpus, models
from vs.fetch import verify
from vs.ivtff import Line, Page

directory = repo / "experiments/M-G/Pavlenko77"
frozen = json.loads((directory / "model.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
envelope = json.loads((directory / "experiment.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
canonical = lambda d: json.dumps(d, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
frozen_hash = hashlib.sha256(canonical(frozen)).hexdigest()
report = {"source_commit": subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], encoding="utf-8").strip(),
          "model_canonical_sha256": frozen_hash, "protocol": envelope["protocol"], "controls": {}, "practice": {}}


def save():
    (here / "hand2_context_results.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def pages(kind, count, seed, prefix):
    rng = Random(seed)
    result = []
    for index in range(count):
        pid = prefix + str(index)
        p = Page(pid, index, {"I": "H", "L": "B", "H": "2"})
        prev = rng.choice("ao")
        for ln in range(50):
            words = []
            for pos in range(8):
                if kind == "boundary":
                    first = prev
                else:
                    first = "a" if pos == 0 else "o" if pos == 7 else rng.choice("ao")
                w = first + rng.choice("lr") + rng.choice("lr") + rng.choice("ao")
                words.append(w)
                prev = w[-1]
            p.lines.append(Line(f"{pid}.{ln}", pid, ln, "P", "0", words, ln == 0, False))
        result.append(p)
    return result


def shuffled(pages, seed):
    rng = Random(seed)
    result = copy.deepcopy(pages)
    for original, p in zip(pages, result):
        words = [w for line in p.lines for w in line.words]
        original_counts = Counter(words)
        rng.shuffle(words)
        index = 0
        for line in p.lines:
            n = len(line.words)
            line.words = words[index:index+n]
            index += n
        assert Counter(w for line in p.lines for w in line.words) == original_counts
        assert [len(line.words) for line in p.lines] == [len(line.words) for line in original.lines]
    return result


def control(kind):
    tr = pages(kind, 10, 14040, "synthetic-train-")
    ev = pages(kind, 4, 14041, "synthetic-eval-")
    plain = {"components": [{"type": "letters", "order": 3}], "weights": "fit"}
    contextual = {"components": plain["components"] + [{"type": kind + "_letters", "order": 3}], "weights": "fit"}
    result = {}
    for label, train, evaluation in (("planted", tr, ev),
                                      ("matched_null", shuffled(tr, 14042), shuffled(ev, 14043))):
        baseline = models.evaluate(plain, train, evaluation)
        candidate = models.evaluate(contextual, train, evaluation)
        result[label] = {"baseline": baseline, "contextual": candidate,
                         "gain_bits_per_word": round(baseline["bits_per_word"] - candidate["bits_per_word"], 4)}
    return result


verify()
for kind in ("boundary", "position"):
    result = control(kind)
    report["controls"][kind] = result
    save()
    print(json.dumps({"control": kind, "results": result}), flush=True)
    threshold = .4 if kind == "boundary" else .05
    if result["planted"]["gain_bits_per_word"] < threshold or result["matched_null"]["gain_bits_per_word"] > .05:
        raise SystemExit("A frozen illustrative control failed; manuscript comparison not started.")

print("Synthetic controls passed; running the official full-model practice advisory.", flush=True)
completed = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-X", "utf8", "-m", "vs", "experiment", str(directory)],
                           cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", check=True)
print(completed.stdout, end="", flush=True)
full, _ = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(completed.stdout.lstrip())
report["practice"]["full"] = full
report["official_advisory_stdout"] = completed.stdout
assert hashlib.sha256(canonical(json.loads((directory / "model.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")))).hexdigest() == frozen_hash
save()

train, evaluation = corpus.split_pages("practice")
report["scope"] = {"hand": "2", "training_pages": len(models.scoped(train, frozen["scope"])),
                   "evaluation_pages": len(models.scoped(evaluation, frozen["scope"]))}
for label, removed in (("without_boundary_letters", {"boundary_letters"}),
                       ("without_position_letters", {"position_letters"}),
                       ("without_both_context_spellers", {"boundary_letters", "position_letters"})):
    ablated = copy.deepcopy(frozen)
    ablated["components"] = [c for c in frozen["components"] if c["type"] not in removed]
    result = models.evaluate(ablated, train, evaluation)
    report["practice"][label] = result
    save()
    print(json.dumps({"ablation": label, "results": result}), flush=True)
print("All frozen variants completed; the submitted full model remains unchanged.", flush=True)

statement: Fit a pooled distribution of certain paragraph word lengths and line capacities on the public ZL training pages. To fill each synthetic paragraph line, draw independently from the pooled word lengths that fit in its remaining capacity, counting one separator between words. Stop when the remaining room admits no positive-length word. This same conditional draw is used at every position and never names the final position or the one-to-three-glyph threshold. The ordinary capacity is 60 units, the training 75th percentile, and paragraph-end capacities come from the clean training paragraph ends capped at 60. Encode each sampled length as a nonlinguistic artificial word. Supply 5,225 lines for the whole book. Freeze seed 643701 for submission. On public practice all five capacity-fit draws pass F-023; controls using independent original slot counts or greedy wrap with an overflow carried to the next line pass zero of five each. The first capacity-fit ratio is 2.249192 with p=.0025, while the same measurement is 1.157454 on the public manuscript evaluation. This is a sufficiency test for the direction of a feature under one geometric model; The imposed filling policy makes the effect larger than on the public manuscript. EVA-basic units serve as a proxy for physical width.

plan.fit: Measure certain paragraph word lengths as eva-basic glyph counts pooled on public ZL practice training only. Ordinary width is the nearest-rank 75th percentile of the observed glyph counts plus inter-word spaces for non-paragraph-ending training rows. At a paragraph-ending line, draw a width from the empirical training distribution of clean paragraph endings, capped by the ordinary width. Empty input lines consume no text. plan.primary_mechanism: A word-table writer observes a fixed line capacity and repeatedly draws an independent word from the pooled length profile conditional on fitting in the remaining space. Every position uses the same rule, and no final-position category is queried. Stop when no positive-length word can fit. Use whole-book line mapping.

"""Public practice reproduction of the official short-final-word fact attack."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

from measure import flags_from_groups, group_toks, test
from write_book import Writer
from vs import corpus, dsl, ivtff, redteam, registry


def practice_pages(lines):
    _, selected = corpus.split_pages('practice')
    selected_ids={p.id for p in selected}
    stream=iter(lines)
    output=[]
    for page in corpus.pages():
        obj=ivtff.Page(page.id,page.order,dict(page.meta))
        for line in page.lines:
            words=next(stream) if line.words else []
            obj.lines.append(ivtff.Line(line.id,line.page,line.n,line.unit,line.subtype,words,line.para_start,line.para_end))
        if obj.id in selected_ids:
            output.append(obj)
    assert next(stream,None) is None
    return output


def main():
    work=Path(sys.argv[1]); entry=json.loads((work/'frozen.json').read_text()); cfg,shape=entry['settings'],entry['layout']
    seeds=range(643701,643706)
    results={}
    for mode in ('fixed_slots','greedy','capacity_fit'):
        results[mode]=[]
        for seed in seeds:
            lines=list(Writer(cfg,seed).rows(shape,mode))
            sample=practice_pages(lines)
            result=test(flags_from_groups(group_toks(sample)),399)
            if mode=='capacity_fit' and seed==643701:
                assert lines==json.loads((work/'primary-lines.json').read_text())
                official=redteam.fact_attack('F-023',lines,'practice',cut='book')
                assert 'refused' not in official
                assert official['synthetic']['value']==round(result['value'],6)
                assert official['synthetic']['pass']==result['pass']
                exact=dsl.evaluate(registry.get('F-023')['detail']['spec'],sample)
                assert exact['detail']['shuffle_within_line']['p']==round(result['p_upper'],4)
            results[mode].append({'seed':seed,'book_words':sum(map(len,lines)),**result})
    print(json.dumps({'official_primary':official,'public_runs':results},indent=2))


if __name__=='__main__':
    main()

"""Reconcile Table 2 treatment choices in radiocarbon BP, without calendar recalibration."""
from fractions import Fraction
import itertools
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path

ROWS = [
    {"sample": "AA84050", "leaf": 8, "extracted": True, "age_bp": 490, "sigma": 37},
    {"sample": "AA84049", "leaf": 26, "extracted": True, "age_bp": 514, "sigma": 35},
    {"sample": "AA84048", "leaf": 47, "extracted": True, "age_bp": 506, "sigma": 35},
    {"sample": "AA84047", "leaf": 68, "extracted": True, "age_bp": 550, "sigma": 35},
    {"sample": "AA84047", "leaf": 68, "extracted": False, "age_bp": 488, "sigma": 35},
]


def estimate(rows):
    weights = [Fraction(1, r["sigma"] ** 2) for r in rows]
    total = sum(weights)
    mean = sum(w * r["age_bp"] for w, r in zip(weights, rows)) / total
    variance = 1 / total
    # Independent floating implementation of the printed formula.
    float_weights = [1 / r["sigma"] ** 2 for r in rows]
    float_mean = sum(w * r["age_bp"] for w, r in zip(float_weights, rows)) / sum(float_weights)
    assert math.isclose(float(mean), float_mean, rel_tol=0, abs_tol=1e-10)
    assert math.isclose(float(variance), 1 / sum(float_weights), rel_tol=0, abs_tol=1e-10)
    # The rational weighted least-squares first derivative is exactly zero.
    assert sum(w * (r["age_bp"] - mean) for w, r in zip(weights, rows)) == 0
    sigma = math.sqrt(float(variance))
    return {"n_determinations": len(rows), "physical_leaves": [r["leaf"] for r in rows],
            "ages_bp": [r["age_bp"] for r in rows], "sigmas": [r["sigma"] for r in rows],
            "mean_bp": float(mean), "standard_error_bp": sigma,
            "mean_exact_fraction": str(mean), "variance_exact_fraction": str(variance),
            "rounded_mean_bp": round(float(mean)), "rounded_standard_error_bp": round(sigma),
            "matches_reported_516_plusminus_18_after_rounding": round(float(mean)) == 516 and round(sigma) == 18,
            "independent_error_formula": True}


def controls():
    equal_sigma = [{"age_bp": x, "sigma": 10, "leaf": i} for i, x in enumerate((100, 200, 300, 400))]
    result = estimate(equal_sigma)
    assert result["mean_bp"] == 250 and result["standard_error_bp"] == 5
    known = [{"age_bp": 516, "sigma": 36, "leaf": i} for i in range(4)]
    assert estimate(known)["mean_bp"] == 516 and estimate(known)["standard_error_bp"] == 18
    before = estimate(ROWS[:4])
    shifted = [dict(r, age_bp=r["age_bp"] + 1000) for r in ROWS[:4]]
    assert math.isclose(estimate(shifted)["mean_bp"] - before["mean_bp"], 1000, abs_tol=1e-10)
    assert estimate(shifted)["standard_error_bp"] == before["standard_error_bp"]
    assert estimate(list(reversed(ROWS[:4]))) == dict(before, physical_leaves=list(reversed(before["physical_leaves"])),
                                                      ages_bp=list(reversed(before["ages_bp"])), sigmas=list(reversed(before["sigmas"])))
    return {"equal_error_arithmetic_mean": True, "known_516_plusminus_18": True,
            "translation_invariance": True, "row_order_invariance": True,
            "rational_and_float_agree": True, "weighted_least_squares_derivative_zero": True}


def run():
    candidates = []
    # Every four-row choice is shown. Only two contain all four physical leaves once.
    for rows in itertools.combinations(ROWS, 4):
        estimate_row = estimate(rows)
        estimate_row["each_of_four_leaves_once"] = len({r["leaf"] for r in rows}) == 4
        estimate_row["leaf68_extraction_flags"] = [r["extracted"] for r in rows if r["leaf"] == 68]
        candidates.append(estimate_row)
    result = {"source": "https://voynich.nu/papers/Carbon_GH_2009.pdf",
              "table": "Table 2", "reported_mean_bp": 516, "reported_standard_error_bp": 18,
              "reported_n": 4, "input_rows": ROWS, "controls": controls(), "all_four_row_choices": candidates,
              "all_four_extracted": estimate(ROWS[:4]),
              "replace_extracted_leaf68_with_unextracted": estimate(ROWS[:3] + [ROWS[4]]),
              "omit_both_leaf68_measurements": estimate(ROWS[:3]),
              "all_five_diagnostic_only": estimate(ROWS)}
    result["mean_shift_if_unextracted_replaces_extracted_bp"] = (
        result["replace_extracted_leaf68_with_unextracted"]["mean_bp"] - result["all_four_extracted"]["mean_bp"])
    valid = [r for r in candidates if r["each_of_four_leaves_once"]]
    assert len(valid) == 2
    assert sum(r["matches_reported_516_plusminus_18_after_rounding"] for r in valid) == 1
    out = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "parchment_mean_results.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps({k: result[k] for k in ("all_four_extracted", "replace_extracted_leaf68_with_unextracted",
                                           "omit_both_leaf68_measurements", "all_five_diagnostic_only",
                                           "mean_shift_if_unextracted_replaces_extracted_bp", "controls")}, indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

                                                      ages_bp=list(reversed(before["ages_bp"])), sigmas=list(reversed(before["sigmas"])))
    return {"equal_error_arithmetic_mean": True, "known_516_plusminus_18": True,
            "translation_invariance": True, "row_order_invariance": True,
            "rational_and_float_agree": True, "weighted_least_squares_derivative_zero": True}


def run():
    candidates = []
    # Every four-row choice is shown. Only two contain all four physical leaves once.
    for rows in itertools.combinations(ROWS, 4):
        estimate_row = estimate(rows)
        estimate_row["each_of_four_leaves_once"] = len({r["leaf"] for r in rows}) == 4
        estimate_row["leaf68_extraction_flags"] = [r["extracted"] for r in rows if r["leaf"] == 68]
        candidates.append(estimate_row)
    result = {"source": "https://voynich.nu/papers/Carbon_GH_2009.pdf",
              "table": "Table 2", "reported_mean_bp": 516, "reported_standard_error_bp": 18,
              "reported_n": 4, "input_rows": ROWS, "controls": controls(), "all_four_row_choices": candidates,
              "all_four_extracted": estimate(ROWS[:4]),
              "replace_extracted_leaf68_with_unextracted": estimate(ROWS[:3] + [ROWS[4]]),
              "omit_both_leaf68_measurements": estimate(ROWS[:3]),
              "all_five_diagnostic_only": estimate(ROWS)}
    result["mean_shift_if_unextracted_replaces_extracted_bp"] = (
        result["replace_extracted_leaf68_with_unextracted"]["mean_bp"] - result["all_four_extracted"]["mean_bp"])
    valid = [r for r in candidates if r["each_of_four_leaves_once"]]
    assert len(valid) == 2
    assert sum(r["matches_reported_516_plusminus_18_after_rounding"] for r in valid) == 1
    out = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "parchment_mean_results.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps({k: result[k] for k in ("all_four_extracted", "replace_extracted_leaf68_with_unextracted",
                                           "omit_both_leaf68_measurements", "all_five_diagnostic_only",
                                           "mean_shift_if_unextracted_replaces_extracted_bp", "controls")}, indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

source: Tests the claim Timm (2014, https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6639) makes in passing, that repeated sequences longer than five words are missing from the manuscript, and gives it a layout-matched comparison it did not have. Uses the pinned repeat_ngram statistic at n=3, which no established fact uses: F-012, F-015, F-017 and F-022 all measure repetition at the single-word or one-edit level, so the multi-word level was open. Reference tokens keep the order they have in sampled calibration blocks and are poured into the selected Voynich word slots, so token count and line layout match while genre and vocabulary frequency are left free to differ. Public practice: manuscript 0.00290 against a reference range of 0.00532 (chinese, the lowest) to 0.15080 (breton), so the manuscript sits below all 48; on the IT2a and RF1b transliterations the value is 0.00098 and 0.00129 against minima of 0.00440 and 0.00517, so the direction does not depend on the transcription. At n=2 the manuscript (0.10634) is NOT below all references (chinese 0.01626 is lower), so the effect is specific to the longer sequence and is not an artefact of the layout. This is the expected footprint of a procedure that never writes a long run twice, and it is the mirror image of F-007 and F-021, which record that SIMILAR words do gather on the line above. The practice comparison is advisory; only the hidden pages decide.

statement: The pinned self-citation procedure (after Timm & Schinner 2020), fitted on the practice training pages only and then writing the shape of every page of the book: each word copies a word written recently on the same page and changes it by 0 to 2 glyph edits drawn from the training glyph inventory. Nothing in the procedure knows what a word means, and nothing counts, avoids or targets repeated sequences: the low three-word repetition falls out of the mechanism itself, because a copy is never an exact copy of a long run. F-024 holds on this text, so it is not evidence that the manuscript was produced by something with language behind it. The same held for all four pinned generators at cut 'lines' (table-cipher 0.00239, self-citation 0.0, grille 0.0, line-chain 0.0, against the manuscript's 0.0029), so F-024 is reproduced by every meaningless procedure on the record, not by one lucky fit.

source: Closes the generator half of P-G-001, whose fact half fleet-fable filed as F-010. F-010 states the within-minus-across gap for the manuscript as a whole; this submission asks whether it survives being split by dialect, which matters because a generator that mixes the two could pass the pooled claim while getting each dialect wrong. It does survive: on the practice split the gap is 0.1328 in Currier A (1898 tokens) and 0.2058 in Currier B (3336 tokens), both clearing the 0.08 bar and both at p=0.005 against 199 within-page shuffles. The split is also a sharper test of generators than the pooled claim. At the evaluation pages' shape, G-line-chain reproduces the gap in both dialects (A 0.1729, B 0.1546) and is the only pinned generator that does; G-grille reproduces it in A (0.0975) but not in B (-0.0212), which the pooled F-010 threshold lets it pass; G-table-cipher (-0.0416 / -0.0121) and G-self-citation (-0.0870 / -0.0253) reproduce it in neither. So the pooled claim is weaker than it looks: one of the four pinned generators passes it by doing the right thing in one dialect only, and the dialect split catches that. The substantive reading is that the mechanism which resets a line's glyph context is a property of each scribe's practice, not an artefact of pooling two hands. Scope by language rather than by hand, since Currier A and B are the split the manuscript itself offers and hand labels are missing on some pages. The practice comparison is advisory; only the hidden pages decide.
statement: In certain paragraph tokens of Currier A, and again in those of Currier B taken on their own, the dependence between a word's last glyph and the next word's first glyph exceeds the same dependence across a line break by at least 0.08 bits, after subtracting the value on each page's shuffled words.

fact.json.source: Closes the generator half of P-G-001, whose fact half fleet-fable filed as F-010. F-010 states the within-minus-across gap for the manuscript as a whole; this submission asks whether it survives being split by dialect, which matters because a generator that mixes the two could pass the pooled claim while getting each dialect wrong. It does survive: on the practice split the gap is 0.1328 in Currier A (1898 tokens) and 0.2058 in Currier B (3336 tokens), both clearing the 0.08 bar and both at p=0.005 against 199 within-page shuffles. The split is also a sharper test of generators than the pooled claim. At the evaluation pages' shape, G-line-chain reproduces the gap in both dialects (A 0.1729, B 0.1546) and is the only pinned generator that does; G-grille reproduces it in A (0.0975) but not in B (-0.0212), which the pooled F-010 threshold lets it pass; G-table-cipher (-0.0416 / -0.0121) and G-self-citation (-0.0870 / -0.0253) reproduce it in neither. So the pooled claim is weaker than it looks: one of the four pinned generators passes it by doing the right thing in one dialect only, and the dialect split catches that. The substantive reading is that the mechanism which resets a line's glyph context is a property of each scribe's practice, not an artefact of pooling two hands. Scope by language rather than by hand, since Currier A and B are the split the manuscript itself offers and hand labels are missing on some pages. The practice comparison is advisory; only the hidden pages decide.
fact.json.statement: In certain paragraph tokens of Currier A, and again in those of Currier B taken on their own, the dependence between a word's last glyph and the next word's first glyph exceeds the same dependence across a line break by at least 0.08 bits, after subtracting the value on each page's shuffled words.

statement:
ONE PROCEDURE. A scribe writes a whole book, page by page, carrying three things and nothing else: a letter jig, a word tray, and a quire packet. No meaning, no morphology, no phrase, no word list outside his own working stock.

THE LETTER JIG. An order-2 chain over strokes. Its alphabet is the strokes of the manuscript's own transcription (EVA-basic, 31 of them) plus three marks: a word end; a line end, which is written as one mark, so that a word ending a line ends with the line; and the paragraph mark that stands before an opening line. Every place is looked up in eight tables at once and they are blended -- the two strokes before, in this setting (an ordinary line, or the opening line of a paragraph, which he sets up before writing), at a line end or not, in this part of the book in this hand; then the same with the hand dropped, then the part of the book, then the line-end setting, then one stroke of history. Each table takes the weight n/(n+8) where n is how often it has seen the place, and what the closer tables leave is left to the whole-book table, so no probability is lost. The jig holds the pen: at every stroke it is asked whether the word ends here, and on a line end only the line-end mark may close it.

THE WORD TRAY. Before the jig writes a word he may take a slip he has already written. Sixteen times in a hundred he lifts one from the tray of the last ten words, the nearer ones lying on top (a geometric reach, tau 3 words), and alters one stroke in it: the stroke is drawn from the jig at that place, must fit the stroke that follows it in the word, and may not be the stroke standing there already. Sixteen times in a hundred he takes a whole slip from the pile of the page, and twelve times in a hundred one from the packet. A slip is lifted with a weight for how the jig would take it up -- the fitted probability of its first stroke in this place -- because he lifts the word his pen is already set for.

THE QUIRE PACKET. Every 12 pages he stocks a packet of 420 slips from the working stock of the part of the book he is in, in the hand that writes it, and does not restock it mid-quire. A page's stock is 35 per cent drawn from the packet and the rest afresh from the same working stock.

THE LINE IS WRITTEN TO THE MARGIN. He draws the width of the line from the fitted distribution of line widths -- strokes, with one space between words, mean 45.4 on the public pages -- lays word after word while the next one fits, and where the room left is too small for the word he has just written he tries up to three more forms and takes one that fits if one comes; if none does, the line ends where it stands. A form he rejects is not written and does not enter his tray. The word that stands at the line's end gets the closing stroke of his line-end habit: the jig, at that place with the line-end setting on, is asked which stroke closes a word there, and the last stroke is drawn again from that answer.

FITTED ON PUBLIC PAGES ONLY. Every table, rate and distribution above is fitted on the 192 training pages of the public practice split, the complement of the 34 pages the practice evaluation scores; those 34 are never read. The book's layout -- page order, which lines open a paragraph, which part of the book each page belongs to, which hand writes it -- is the codicological record rather than the text, and the scorer lays the lines onto it page by page as a scribe's lines go onto a quire. The text itself is meaningless and knows nothing of the pages it is laid on.

WHAT IT DOES TO F-023. On the held-out practice pages the share of certain words of at most three units is 0.4403 at line ends against 0.3440 on the same lines away from the ends: ratio 1.2681, against the manuscript's own 0.3701 against 0.3079, ratio 1.1575. It beats the within-line shuffle null at p = 0.0025 on 399 permutations, which is the floor of the test. Nothing in the procedure mentions word length, or line ends, or a ratio between them. The shortness of line-endings falls out of filling a ruled line to the margin: when the room left is small, the forms that fit are the short ones.

CONTROLS, same generator, same fit, measured on public 40-page samples (ratio of the at-most-three share at line ends to mid-line; the manuscript's own value on the public training pages is 1.115). Margin-filling with three shorter forms tried: 1.24. With one form tried: 1.13. With none -- the line simply stops when the next word will not fit: 0.98, the fact is gone. So it is the ruled margin, not the line-end habit and not the letter jig, that carries F-023. The number of attempts, 3, was set on the public training pages by that comparison before the held-out pages were read; the band, the null and the held-out pages were used to choose nothing.

IT IS NOT A LUCKY SEED. Seeds 11, 12, 13, 14 give 1.2681, 1.2533, 1.3192, 1.2916 on the held-out practice pages, every one passing at p = 0.0025.

A FINDING ABOUT THE FACT ITSELF, from the public pages only. On 20 random 34-page subsets of the 192 public training pages, the manuscript's OWN value of this ratio ranges 0.935 to 1.289 (median 1.120) and falls below the fact's threshold of 1 on 1 subset of 20. The threshold is inside the sampling noise of the quantity it states: a draw of 34 pages of the manuscript itself can fail the first half of F-023. This text is above 1 on 20 of 20 such subsets (1.214 to 1.398, median 1.331), so its pass is not the same kind of pass the manuscript's own value would be on an unlucky draw.

WHAT ELSE THE SAME TEXT REPRODUCES. It was not aimed at any other fact, and on the same held-out practice pages it reproduces 15 of the 21 established ones: F-002, F-003, F-004, F-005, F-007, F-008, F-009, F-013, F-016, F-017, F-018, F-019, F-021, F-022, F-023. It does not reproduce F-001 (line-final m in Currier B), F-006 (line-opening words longer than within-line shuffle), F-010 (edge dependence breaking at line ends), F-011 (nearby pages sharing words), F-014 (two types in three occurring once) or F-020 (pages of one Currier language sharing words).

GUARDS. 4,487 ordinary lines and 738 paragraph-opening lines, exactly the manuscript's own counts, so the text fills every page of the book; 43,870 tokens, 8,663 distinct, mean length 4.38 units; 0 four-word runs of the manuscript; 0 uncertainty markers.

WHAT IT WOULD SHOW, if it holds on the hidden pages: that a text with no language in it, written by a hand that only knows how strokes follow strokes, what his pen is set for, and where the margin is, can carry the elevation of short words at line ends. The fact would then be a statement about ruled pages and justification, not about meaning or about the shape of a vocabulary. WHAT IT WOULD NOT SHOW: that the manuscript was written by such a scribe -- only that this fact cannot tell the two apart. ASSUMPTION THAT COULD FAIL ON THE HIDDEN PAGES: the hidden pages are one draw of 34, and on public draws of that size this text's ratio ranges 1.21 to 1.40 and the null's floor is p = 0.0025, so a failure would mean the hidden pages are unlike any public draw; the section and hand mix of the hidden pages also enters, since the jig and the stock are kept per part of the book and per hand.

detail.statement: P-G-020 asks for label_in_page_text and feature_label_share to be registered as facts before further invented languages are designed. None of the three picture_label tests can be evaluated today, for three independent reasons, each checked on the pinned record. (1) pictures() picks the wrong AGREED annotation. On f72v1 two seats filed an AGREED annotation with the same agreement 0.833: V-026 carries label null on all 32 objects, V-043 carries 30 real ZL label loci (f72v1.2 through f72v1.32, all present as unit L lines in ZL3b). pictures() keeps the first seen at equal agreement, so it returns V-026 and _picture_objects() finds 0 labelled objects on any page. (2) Even when V-043 is forced, the statistic is still undefined: f72v1 is not among the practice evaluation pages, so the value on the practice split is 0 labelled objects, and a fact scored on the hidden pages would depend on a folio the split does not sample. (3) On the whole book V-043 yields 30 labelled objects, but all are human_figure on one folio and they are near-identical: the first two agree on 9 of 10 features. feature_label_share therefore receives 435 alike pairs and 0 not-alike, and _rate_diff returns NaN because it needs at least 5 in each group; same_object_label compares across folios only, so with one folio it has 0 pairs by construction. Fix each in that order and the label facts become measurable; until then P-G-020 and P-G-006 have no discriminating target.

detail.check: Run the embedded script from the repository root with data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt fetched; it prints the ring inventory, the clock-aligned run and the same-ring-only run.
findings: The rings rebuild exactly as the step describes: 21 rings and rows of figure labels (unit L, subtype z, each carrying a clock marker) on the twelve zodiac pages, holding 265 labels, with sizes 20, 19, 18, 18, 16, 16, 15, 12, 12, 12, 11, ten 10s, 9 and 7 - the same multiset the step lists (19 and 10; 10 on each of four pages; 15 and 9; 12, 11 and 7; 18 and 12 twice; 20 and 10; 16 and 10 twice).

Clock-aligned run: 2415 comparisons, 2 exact agreements, null mean 4.3 over 400 random turnings, p = 0.94. The comparison count and the exact-agreement count reproduce the step's 2415 and 2 exactly, and so does its p = 0.94.

Same-ring-only run (rings classed by size within their page, largest as outer - twelve, one per sign - and the rest as inner - nine; outer with outer and inner with inner, the two inner rings of f72r3 compared with each other): 1239 comparisons, 0 exact agreements, null mean 2.4, p = 1.00. The comparison count and the exact count reproduce the addendum's 1239 and 0.

Within one glyph: 36 observed against a null mean of 28.3 (p = 0.07) for the clock-aligned run, and 15 against 13.0 (p = 0.32) for the same-ring-only run. The observed counts sit at or just below the step's 37 and 15; the nulls come out lower than its 33.7 and 16.0.
detail.interpretation: The step's conclusion stands under an independent rebuild: with the alignment fixed by the page itself and no freedom to search a rotation, a label at a given place in the wheel is no more likely to recur at the same place on another sign than under a random turning (2 in 2415 against 4.3 expected). The declared same-ring-only variant, which is what a roster split by ring would actually predict, is weaker still: no exact agreement in 1239 comparisons. The one-glyph nulls differ from the step's by about five counts in the same direction in both runs, which is a difference in how the turned ring is sampled, not in the observed text: the observed one-glyph counts match (15 exactly, 36 against 37). Nothing here reopens the roster question in the labels' favour.
limits: One transliteration (ZL3b), as in the step; the labels are short and the file gives clock positions only to the nearest quarter or half hour, coarser than the figure spacing in the larger rings, so nearest-position pairing is off by a figure fairly often.

The one-glyph nulls come out lower than the step's (28.3 against 33.7, and 13.0 against 16.0). The step does not state how the turning angle is sampled; this run draws it continuously and independently per ring pair, which makes the turned pairing closer to a random pairing. The observed one-glyph counts are not affected, and the exact-agreement nulls agree closely (4.3 against 4.1, 2.4 against 2.0).
Rings are rebuilt from consecutive line numbers; the step's own listing is reproduced exactly, so this is not an independent segmentation claim, only an independent rebuild.
No hidden pages were read: every label used is on the public pages.
detail.methods: The clock position of every figure-label line is read from the raw pinned file's <!hh:mm> comment (the parser strips comments, so the marker is taken before parsing); the labels themselves come from vs/ivtff.parse, first word only, uncertain readings stripped to their first alternative. Rings are maximal runs of consecutive label line numbers within a page, kept at seven or more. Rings stand in manuscript page order (Page.order), so for each pair of rings on different pages 'the first' is the earlier page - this is what makes the comparison count come out at 2415 rather than the 2406 of a page-id ordering or the 5045 of ordered pairs. For every label of the first ring, the partner is the label of the second whose clock position is nearest on the circle. The null turns the second ring by an angle drawn uniformly from 0 to 360 degrees, independently for every ring pair, 400 times, seed 408. One glyph apart means edit distance one: one substitution at equal length, or one insertion or deletion at lengths differing by one.

reproducibility.instructions: Save the embedded script as pl4028.py in the repository root and run `python3 pl4028.py` with data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt fetched. It prints the ring inventory, the clock-aligned run and the same-ring-only run. The run takes about two minutes on one core.

"""P-L4-028 reproduction: zodiac figure labels (unit L, subtype z) paired across signs by the clock
position of their figure, alignment fixed by the page, no rotation free.

As the step declares it: the rings and rows of figure labels on the twelve zodiac pages that hold
seven or more labels; for every pair of rings on different pages and every label of the first, the
label of the second whose clock position is nearest; first word of the label only, uncertain
readings taken at their first alternative. Rings stand in manuscript page order, so "the first" is
the earlier page. Null: the second ring turned by a random angle, 400 times.
Addendum variant: rings classed by size within their page, the largest as outer (twelve, one per
sign) and the rest as inner (nine); only outer with outer and inner with inner are compared, the two
inner rings of f72r3 thereby compared with each other.
"""
import re, sys, random, collections
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from vs import ivtff

RAW = "data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt"
HEAD = re.compile(r"^<(f\d+[rv]\d*)\.(\d+),([@+*=&~\-])(\w+)>")
CLOCK = re.compile(r"<!\s*(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*>")

clock = {}
for raw in open(RAW, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
    m = HEAD.match(raw)
    if not m or m.group(4) != "Lz":
        continue
    cm = CLOCK.search(raw)
    if cm:
        clock[(m.group(1), int(m.group(2)))] = (int(cm.group(1)) * 60 + int(cm.group(2))) / 1440 * 360.0

rings = collections.defaultdict(list)
order = {}
for pg in ivtff.parse(RAW):
    order[pg.id] = pg.order
    for ln in pg.lines:
        if ln.unit != "L" or ln.subtype != "z":
            continue
        d = clock.get((pg.id, ln.n))
        if d is None or not ln.words:
            continue
        w = ln.words[0].strip("?*")
        if w:
            rings[pg.id].append((ln.n, d, w))

groups = []
for p, rows in sorted(rings.items(), key=lambda kv: order[kv[0]]):
    rows.sort()
    cur = [rows[0]]
    for r in rows[1:]:
        if r[0] == cur[-1][0] + 1:
            cur.append(r)
        else:
            groups.append((p, cur))
            cur = [r]
    groups.append((p, cur))
groups = [(p, g) for p, g in groups if len(g) >= 7]
print("rings of seven or more:", len(groups), "on", len({p for p, _ in groups}), "pages;",
      "labels:", sum(len(g) for _, g in groups),
      "; sizes:", sorted((len(g) for _, g in groups), reverse=True))

    d = abs(a - b) % 360
    return min(d, 360 - d)


def one_glyph(a, b):
    if a == b or abs(len(a) - len(b)) > 1:
        return False
    if len(a) == len(b):
        return sum(x != y for x, y in zip(a, b)) == 1
    lo, hi = (a, b) if len(a) < len(b) else (b, a)
    i = 0
    while i < len(lo) and lo[i] == hi[i]:
        i += 1
    return lo[i:] == hi[i + 1:]


def measure(pairs, turns=400, seed=408):
    def once(rot_of):
        e = n2 = 0
        for i, j in pairs:
            rot = rot_of()
            for _n, d, t in groups[i][1]:
                b = min(groups[j][1], key=lambda r: cdist(d + rot, r[1]))
                if b[2] == t:
                    e += 1
                elif one_glyph(t, b[2]):
                    n2 += 1
        return e, n2
    obs_e, obs_n = once(lambda: 0.0)
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    null = [once(lambda: rng.uniform(0, 360)) for _ in range(turns)]
    me = sum(x[0] for x in null) / turns
    mn = sum(x[1] for x in null) / turns
    pe = (sum(1 for x in null if x[0] >= obs_e) + 1) / (turns + 1)
    pn = (sum(1 for x in null if x[1] >= obs_n) + 1) / (turns + 1)
    return sum(len(groups[i][1]) for i, j in pairs), obs_e, me, pe, obs_n, mn, pn


pairs = [(i, j) for i in range(len(groups)) for j in range(i + 1, len(groups))
         if groups[i][0] != groups[j][0]]
c, e, me, pe, n2, mn, pn = measure(pairs)
print(f"every ring with every other: comparisons={c} exact={e} (null {me:.1f}, p={pe:.2f}); "
      f"within one glyph {n2} (null {mn:.1f}, p={pn:.2f})")

outer, inner = [], []
for idx, (p, g) in enumerate(groups):
    on_page = [k for k, (_p, _g) in enumerate(groups) if _p == p]
    on_page.sort(key=lambda k: -len(groups[k][1]))

        for j in a:

                continue

print(f"same-ring-only (outer with outer, inner with inner; {len(outer)} outer, {len(inner)} inner rings): "
      f"comparisons={c2} exact={e2} (null {me2:.1f}, p={pe2:.2f}); within one glyph {n3} (null {mn2:.1f}, p={pn2:.2f})")
