step.json.check: Run the embedded script from the repository root with data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt fetched; it prints the ring inventory, the clock-aligned run and the same-ring-only run.
findings: The rings rebuild exactly as the step describes: 21 rings and rows of figure labels (unit L, subtype z, each carrying a clock marker) on the twelve zodiac pages, holding 265 labels, with sizes 20, 19, 18, 18, 16, 16, 15, 12, 12, 12, 11, ten 10s, 9 and 7 - the same multiset the step lists (19 and 10; 10 on each of four pages; 15 and 9; 12, 11 and 7; 18 and 12 twice; 20 and 10; 16 and 10 twice).

Clock-aligned run: 2415 comparisons, 2 exact agreements, null mean 4.3 over 400 random turnings, p = 0.94. The comparison count and the exact-agreement count reproduce the step's 2415 and 2 exactly, and so does its p = 0.94.

Same-ring-only run (rings classed by size within their page, largest as outer - twelve, one per sign - and the rest as inner - nine; outer with outer and inner with inner, the two inner rings of f72r3 compared with each other): 1239 comparisons, 0 exact agreements, null mean 2.4, p = 1.00. The comparison count and the exact count reproduce the addendum's 1239 and 0.

Within one glyph: 36 observed against a null mean of 28.3 (p = 0.07) for the clock-aligned run, and 15 against 13.0 (p = 0.32) for the same-ring-only run. The observed counts sit at or just below the step's 37 and 15; the nulls come out lower than its 33.7 and 16.0.
step.json.interpretation: The step's conclusion stands under an independent rebuild: with the alignment fixed by the page itself and no freedom to search a rotation, a label at a given place in the wheel is no more likely to recur at the same place on another sign than under a random turning (2 in 2415 against 4.3 expected). The declared same-ring-only variant, which is what a roster split by ring would actually predict, is weaker still: no exact agreement in 1239 comparisons. The one-glyph nulls differ from the step's by about five counts in the same direction in both runs, which is a difference in how the turned ring is sampled, not in the observed text: the observed one-glyph counts match (15 exactly, 36 against 37). Nothing here reopens the roster question in the labels' favour.
limits: One transliteration (ZL3b), as in the step; the labels are short and the file gives clock positions only to the nearest quarter or half hour, coarser than the figure spacing in the larger rings, so nearest-position pairing is off by a figure fairly often.

The one-glyph nulls come out lower than the step's (28.3 against 33.7, and 13.0 against 16.0). The step does not state how the turning angle is sampled; this run draws it continuously and independently per ring pair, which makes the turned pairing closer to a random pairing. The observed one-glyph counts are not affected, and the exact-agreement nulls agree closely (4.3 against 4.1, 2.4 against 2.0).
Rings are rebuilt from consecutive line numbers; the step's own listing is reproduced exactly, so this is not an independent segmentation claim, only an independent rebuild.
No hidden pages were read: every label used is on the public pages.
step.json.methods: The clock position of every figure-label line is read from the raw pinned file's <!hh:mm> comment (the parser strips comments, so the marker is taken before parsing); the labels themselves come from vs/ivtff.parse, first word only, uncertain readings stripped to their first alternative. Rings are maximal runs of consecutive label line numbers within a page, kept at seven or more. Rings stand in manuscript page order (Page.order), so for each pair of rings on different pages 'the first' is the earlier page - this is what makes the comparison count come out at 2415 rather than the 2406 of a page-id ordering or the 5045 of ordered pairs. For every label of the first ring, the partner is the label of the second whose clock position is nearest on the circle. The null turns the second ring by an angle drawn uniformly from 0 to 360 degrees, independently for every ring pair, 400 times, seed 408. One glyph apart means edit distance one: one substitution at equal length, or one insertion or deletion at lengths differing by one.

check: Run a held-apart, source-context-matched comparison on these cleaned work pairs. Choose the source context order by blocked validation within each training work, then freeze it. For the inter-letter versions compare a forward character model with a model reaching the same number of preceding source symbols, using the actual pad alignment. Report the known-rule inverse benchmark and bill any alignment information unavailable to a decoder. Evaluate each fixed choice once on the independent work. Also compare the constant suffix with an explicit, decoder-computable word-boundary state on the unexpanded source.

limits: Finite-order predictive code lengths depend on the representation, reconstructed vocabulary, amount of training and disjoint-work distribution shift. A reversible transform preserves joint source information when its rule is known.
Minima describe the tested grid on these evaluation works. An out-of-sample claim for the choice of order requires choosing the order using training only.
The chosen pairings compare genres as well as words within a language. Identical normalized evaluation input for all transforms within each pair is the primary control.

methods.audit: Exact inversion and word/space/block boundaries verified for all transforms in both splits. Exact encoded random streams reconstructed from original and ordered pads. Train and test marker histograms are identical for the deterministic and random two-marker controls on each work separately, and so are output lengths. All work pairs have distinct IDs, no shared complete normalized blocks, and no common exact 12-word windows in the trimmed spans. All order-normalization identities and substitution equalities checked. Independently hand-checked the model on ab/ba training and ab evaluation.

comparators.addB: append B after every nonspace source letter
comparators.matched_deterministic: append B or D according to the parity of the zero-based source letter index in the alphabet
comparators.matched_random: uniformly permute that exact B/D multiset once per complete work split, using independent experimental train and evaluation seeds 40801 and 40802
comparators.suffix_B: append B at the end of every source word

methods.denominators: Original normalized letters plus literal spaces and transformed letters plus literal spaces and insertions, respectively. The block separator is never modeled or counted. Symbols, not UTF-8 bytes, are the units.
methods.empirical_entropy: Conditional plug-in entropy computed on evaluation only, for orders 0–8 using shorter available contexts at block starts. Also report first-order entropy per actual adjacent transition, with no transitions across blocks. These are descriptive statistics, separate from held-apart predictive code lengths.
methods.held_apart_codelength: For each code and order 0–8, model ASCII letters and literal spaces plus that code’s pad alphabet. Fit counts on the training work only. Order zero uses one-half count per symbol. Each extra order interpolates context counts and the shorter order probability with prior mass 2. Reset at original work-block boundaries. Predict every symbol, using the available shorter context at block starts. Aggregate negative base-2 log probability over evaluation blocks, with probabilities fixed from training.
methods.inverse_aware: A decoder given the transform rules first decodes the original work with the same order model. All deterministic output symbols are recoverable from that source. For the random control the decoder must also recover the ordered B/D pad sequence. The source determines its exact histogram, and under the uniform-permutation model that sequence adds log2 binomial(N, number of B pads) bits once per work split. The random realization and PRNG seed are not given to that decoder. The recipe and shared training tables are conditioned on in all comparisons.
methods.selection: First 64 complete blocks after trimming the six independent source works. The boundaries are the existing project normalizer’s roughly 400-character blocks, not historical folio or line breaks. No manuscript text enters this calculation.

prior.paper: Claire Bowern and Daniel Gaskell, Enciphered after all? Word-level text metrics are compatible with some types of encipherment.

scripts.transforms.py:
"""Boundary-preserving transforms for normalized lowercase ASCII work blocks.

Spaces remain word separators. Newlines can join a work's blocks for a single
matched shuffle while remaining available for model resets. The source and
marker alphabets below exclude those block separators.
"""

from itertools import repeat
from math import comb, log2
from random import Random
import re
from string import ascii_lowercase


SOURCE_ALPHABET = ascii_lowercase + " "
MARKER_ALPHABETS = {
    "identity": "",
    "substitution": "",
    "addB": "B",
    "matched_deterministic": "BD",
    "matched_random": "BD",
    "suffix_B": "B",
}
KINDS = tuple(MARKER_ALPHABETS)
DEFAULT_SEED = 408

_BOUNDARIES = frozenset(" \n")
_SOURCE_SYMBOLS = frozenset(SOURCE_ALPHABET) | _BOUNDARIES
_PARITY_PAD = {letter: "DB"[i % 2] for i, letter in enumerate(ascii_lowercase)}
_WORD = re.compile(r"[a-z]+")
_RANDOM_PADDING = re.compile(r"(?:[a-z][BD]|[ \n])*")
_STRIP_PADDING = str.maketrans("", "", "BD")

_substitution = list(ascii_lowercase)
Random(408).shuffle(_substitution)
_FORWARD = str.maketrans(ascii_lowercase, "".join(_substitution))
_BACKWARD = str.maketrans("".join(_substitution), ascii_lowercase)


def _check_source(text: str, kind: str) -> None:
    if kind not in MARKER_ALPHABETS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown transform {kind!r}")
    if not _SOURCE_SYMBOLS.issuperset(text):
        raise ValueError("source must contain only lowercase ASCII letters, spaces, and newlines")


def encode(text: str, kind: str, seed: int = DEFAULT_SEED) -> str:
    """Transform a block or newline-joined work without changing its separators.

    Matched deterministic markers follow zero-based letter-index parity, with
    even indices producing D and odd indices producing B. Matched random uses a
    uniform shuffle of that exact marker multiset across the input's letters.
    The call's seed affects only the shuffle. Substitution uses a fixed key.
    """
    _check_source(text, kind)
    if kind == "identity":
        return text
    if kind == "substitution":
        return text.translate(_FORWARD)
    if kind == "suffix_B":
        return _WORD.sub(lambda word: word.group() + "B", text)

    if kind == "addB":
        markers = repeat("B")
    else:
        pads = [_PARITY_PAD[letter] for letter in text if letter not in _BOUNDARIES]
        if kind == "matched_random":
            Random(seed).shuffle(pads)
        markers = iter(pads)
    return "".join(c if c in _BOUNDARIES else c + next(markers) for c in text)


def decode(text: str, kind: str) -> str:
    """Recover the original source. Reject misplaced or mismatched markers."""
    if kind in ("identity", "substitution"):
        _check_source(text, kind)
        return text.translate(_BACKWARD) if kind == "substitution" else text

    source = text.translate(_STRIP_PADDING)
    _check_source(source, kind)
    if kind == "matched_random":
        expected_b = sum(_PARITY_PAD.get(c) == "B" for c in source)
        valid = _RANDOM_PADDING.fullmatch(text) is not None and text.count("B") == expected_b
    else:
        valid = encode(source, kind) == text
    if not valid:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid {kind} markers")
    return source


def side_bits(source: str, kind: str) -> float:
    """Conditional marker-code length for a source block or joined work.

    The source determines the number of marker locations n and B markers k.
    In matched random, all C(n,k) arrangements are equiprobable, so the ideal
    code length is log2(C(n,k)). Deterministic markers need zero side bits.
    """
    _check_source(source, kind)
    if kind != "matched_random":
        return 0.0
    n = sum(c not in _BOUNDARIES for c in source)
    k = sum(_PARITY_PAD.get(c) == "B" for c in source)
    return log2(comb(n, k))

detail.statement: Repeat the public P-J-011 calculation on editorially trimmed Latin, Italian and Middle High German works, using separate train and evaluation works. Every fixed substitution gives the identical code length at every order. At order eight, constant letter padding lowers the forward rate per output symbol and raises it per original symbol in all three pairs. The order-eight Latin rates are 3.838 for identity, 2.307 per output and 4.266 per original symbol after constant letter padding. Some intermediate orders give a smaller per-source estimate after deterministic padding. The word suffix also has a smaller descriptive minimum in all three pairs. These are finite-context coding effects. An exact work-matched random permutation of deterministic pad symbols costs extra bits even with a known inverse.

step.json.check: Run a held-apart, source-context-matched comparison on these cleaned work pairs. Choose the source context order by blocked validation within each training work, then freeze it. For the inter-letter versions compare a forward character model with a model reaching the same number of preceding source symbols, using the actual pad alignment. Report the known-rule inverse benchmark and bill any alignment information unavailable to a decoder. Evaluate each fixed choice once on the independent work. Also compare the constant suffix with an explicit, decoder-computable word-boundary state on the unexpanded source.
limits: Finite-order predictive code lengths depend on the representation, reconstructed vocabulary, amount of training and disjoint-work distribution shift. A reversible transform preserves joint source information when its rule is known.
Minima describe the tested grid on these evaluation works. An out-of-sample claim for the choice of order requires choosing the order using training only.
The chosen pairings compare genres as well as words within a language. Identical normalized evaluation input for all transforms within each pair is the primary control.

methods.audit: Exact inversion and word/space/block boundaries verified for all transforms in both splits. Exact encoded random streams reconstructed from original and ordered pads. Train and test marker histograms are identical for the deterministic and random two-marker controls on each work separately, and so are output lengths. All work pairs have distinct IDs, no shared complete normalized blocks, and no common exact 12-word windows in the trimmed spans. All order-normalization identities and substitution equalities checked. Independently hand-checked the model on ab/ba training and ab evaluation.

comparators.addB: append B after every nonspace source letter
comparators.matched_deterministic: append B or D according to the parity of the zero-based source letter index in the alphabet
comparators.matched_random: uniformly permute that exact B/D multiset once per complete work split, using independent experimental train and evaluation seeds 40801 and 40802
comparators.suffix_B: append B at the end of every source word

methods.denominators: Original normalized letters plus literal spaces and transformed letters plus literal spaces and insertions, respectively. The block separator is never modeled or counted. Symbols, not UTF-8 bytes, are the units.
methods.empirical_entropy: Conditional plug-in entropy computed on evaluation only, for orders 0–8 using shorter available contexts at block starts. Also report first-order entropy per actual adjacent transition, with no transitions across blocks. These are descriptive statistics, separate from held-apart predictive code lengths.
methods.held_apart_codelength: For each code and order 0–8, model ASCII letters and literal spaces plus that code’s pad alphabet. Fit counts on the training work only. Order zero uses one-half count per symbol. Each extra order interpolates context counts and the shorter order probability with prior mass 2. Reset at original work-block boundaries. Predict every symbol, using the available shorter context at block starts. Aggregate negative base-2 log probability over evaluation blocks, with probabilities fixed from training.
methods.inverse_aware: A decoder given the transform rules first decodes the original work with the same order model. All deterministic output symbols are recoverable from that source. For the random control the decoder must also recover the ordered B/D pad sequence. The source determines its exact histogram, and under the uniform-permutation model that sequence adds log2 binomial(N, number of B pads) bits once per work split. The random realization and PRNG seed are not given to that decoder. The recipe and shared training tables are conditioned on in all comparisons.
methods.selection: First 64 complete blocks after trimming the six independent source works. The boundaries are the existing project normalizer’s roughly 400-character blocks, not historical folio or line breaks. No manuscript text enters this calculation.

prior.paper: Claire Bowern and Daniel Gaskell, Enciphered after all? Word-level text metrics are compatible with some types of encipherment.

scripts.transforms.py:
"""Boundary-preserving transforms for normalized lowercase ASCII work blocks.

Spaces remain word separators. Newlines can join a work's blocks for a single
matched shuffle while remaining available for model resets. The source and
marker alphabets below exclude those block separators.
"""

from itertools import repeat
from math import comb, log2
from random import Random
import re
from string import ascii_lowercase


SOURCE_ALPHABET = ascii_lowercase + " "
MARKER_ALPHABETS = {
    "identity": "",
    "substitution": "",
    "addB": "B",
    "matched_deterministic": "BD",
    "matched_random": "BD",
    "suffix_B": "B",
}
KINDS = tuple(MARKER_ALPHABETS)
DEFAULT_SEED = 408

_BOUNDARIES = frozenset(" \n")
_SOURCE_SYMBOLS = frozenset(SOURCE_ALPHABET) | _BOUNDARIES
_PARITY_PAD = {letter: "DB"[i % 2] for i, letter in enumerate(ascii_lowercase)}
_WORD = re.compile(r"[a-z]+")
_RANDOM_PADDING = re.compile(r"(?:[a-z][BD]|[ \n])*")
_STRIP_PADDING = str.maketrans("", "", "BD")

_substitution = list(ascii_lowercase)
Random(408).shuffle(_substitution)
_FORWARD = str.maketrans(ascii_lowercase, "".join(_substitution))
_BACKWARD = str.maketrans("".join(_substitution), ascii_lowercase)


def _check_source(text: str, kind: str) -> None:
    if kind not in MARKER_ALPHABETS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown transform {kind!r}")
    if not _SOURCE_SYMBOLS.issuperset(text):
        raise ValueError("source must contain only lowercase ASCII letters, spaces, and newlines")


def encode(text: str, kind: str, seed: int = DEFAULT_SEED) -> str:
    """Transform a block or newline-joined work without changing its separators.

    Matched deterministic markers follow zero-based letter-index parity, with
    even indices producing D and odd indices producing B. Matched random uses a
    uniform shuffle of that exact marker multiset across the input's letters.
    The call's seed affects only the shuffle. Substitution uses a fixed key.
    """
    _check_source(text, kind)
    if kind == "identity":
        return text
    if kind == "substitution":
        return text.translate(_FORWARD)
    if kind == "suffix_B":
        return _WORD.sub(lambda word: word.group() + "B", text)

    if kind == "addB":
        markers = repeat("B")
    else:
        pads = [_PARITY_PAD[letter] for letter in text if letter not in _BOUNDARIES]
        if kind == "matched_random":
            Random(seed).shuffle(pads)
        markers = iter(pads)
    return "".join(c if c in _BOUNDARIES else c + next(markers) for c in text)


def decode(text: str, kind: str) -> str:
    """Recover the original source. Reject misplaced or mismatched markers."""
    if kind in ("identity", "substitution"):
        _check_source(text, kind)
        return text.translate(_BACKWARD) if kind == "substitution" else text

    source = text.translate(_STRIP_PADDING)
    _check_source(source, kind)
    if kind == "matched_random":
        expected_b = sum(_PARITY_PAD.get(c) == "B" for c in source)
        valid = _RANDOM_PADDING.fullmatch(text) is not None and text.count("B") == expected_b
    else:
        valid = encode(source, kind) == text
    if not valid:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid {kind} markers")
    return source


def side_bits(source: str, kind: str) -> float:
    """Conditional marker-code length for a source block or joined work.

    The source determines the number of marker locations n and B markers k.
    In matched random, all C(n,k) arrangements are equiprobable, so the ideal
    code length is log2(C(n,k)). Deterministic markers need zero side bits.
    """
    _check_source(source, kind)
    if kind != "matched_random":
        return 0.0
    n = sum(c not in _BOUNDARIES for c in source)
    k = sum(_PARITY_PAD.get(c) == "B" for c in source)
    return log2(comb(n, k))

limits: The synthetic shapes are designed to expose page dependence. They establish that a no-drawing rule can pass at the stated thresholds, without estimating whether any particular manuscript labels refer to drawings.

Shuffling label lines inside one folio keeps their multiset fixed and leaves label-in-page recurrence unchanged. On the pure folio-clustered feature fixture it also leaves all feature comparisons unchanged. The diagnostic checks this explicitly, so moving the existing shuffle within folio is insufficient on its own.

The stock public self-citation control is explicit and reproducible here. The archived one-table/no-drift narrative from P-G-007 lacks the exact matching stream; other deposited variants use drift or several tables. This does not substitute those variants for a later manuscript-matched one-table control.
public_interpretation: There are 50 picture records on 18 folios. The two AGREED records belong to f72v1 and both have agreement 0.833. The pinned selector retains the first on a tie, V-026. That seat has 32 objects, no explicit loci and legacy clock fields without join-compatible typed angles. The current join returns zero.

The hypothetical alternative seat V-043 contains 30 valid label loci. This is a diagnostic substitution in memory, not a change to which seat the scorer selects. ZL, IT and RF each have 30 label lines and no paragraph lines on f72v1. All 435 feature pairs from that annotation are alike under the current predicate, giving no comparison pairs. The default requirements are 20 linked objects and at least five pairs in each feature group.

The two draft annotated folios f99v and f102v2 currently offer an upper bound of 23 and 20 eligible label loci, respectively, in each pinned transliteration. Both have paragraph text. A different contributor must annotate independently. These counts do not predict coverage in an unobserved split.

detail.statement: P-G-020 has no eligible picture-label sample on the current public registry and practice split. The only AGREED folio is selected through a seat with zero effective links, and even the other agreed seat has no paragraph text on that folio. A stock one-table reuse generator sees no drawing or object features. On a synthetic layout it nevertheless gives eight of eight positive label-in-page results on declared image labels and on sham labels. It gives seven of eight positive feature-label results when feature groups are clustered by page. Exact-length, same-folio paired label-minus-sham comparisons pass zero of eight. These controls expose page-level dependence under the current global label shuffle.

synthetic_setup.ablations: Shuffle all generated word slots globally to preserve the overall word stock and the original number of slots per line while breaking page-local recurrence. For the feature test contrast a feature palette unique by folio with the same colours represented in every folio. The generated text and label links are identical in the two feature arms.
synthetic_setup.global_null: Use the existing picture_label statistics and global shuffle_picture_labels. The toy check uses the default 20-object threshold and a positive value with one-sided p <= 0.01 from 399 permutations. Neither the method nor the threshold is proposed as a validated manuscript fact.
synthetic_setup.layout: Twelve fabricated folios. Each has six cycles of a running-text line, two one-word label slots, and a running-text line. Alternating parity assigns the two adjacent slots to a declared image label and a sham. There are 72 linked lines for either arm. The same synthetic outputs are reused across feature-group conditions.
synthetic_setup.paired_comparison: Match actual-designated and sham one-word labels by exact EVA-basic glyph length of at least three within each synthetic folio. Use order by label slot for ties. Subtract the sham own-page-minus-other-page match indicator from the declared label indicator. Use a one-sided label-exchange null by swapping the pair signs 399 times. Use 20 matched pairs and p<=0.01 as the minimum and threshold.
synthetic_setup.rule: The stock vs.generators.g_self_citation writer draws from one public practice training vocabulary and recent words on its current page. It is applied unchanged to the same synthetic line-slot shapes for all conditions. The unit field does not change its selection rule. It receives no picture inventory, label links, object-feature group, or declared-versus-sham role.

synthetic_setup.ablations: Shuffle all generated word slots globally to preserve the overall word stock and the original number of slots per line while breaking page-local recurrence. For the feature test contrast a feature palette unique by folio with the same colours represented in every folio. The generated text and label links are identical in the two feature arms.
synthetic_setup.global_null: Use the existing picture_label statistics and global shuffle_picture_labels. The toy check uses the default 20-object threshold and a positive value with one-sided p <= 0.01 from 399 permutations. Neither the method nor the threshold is proposed as a validated manuscript fact.
synthetic_setup.layout: Twelve fabricated folios. Each has six cycles of a running-text line, two one-word label slots, and a running-text line. Alternating parity assigns the two adjacent slots to a declared image label and a sham. There are 72 linked lines for either arm. The same synthetic outputs are reused across feature-group conditions.
synthetic_setup.paired_comparison: Match actual-designated and sham one-word labels by exact EVA-basic glyph length of at least three within each synthetic folio. Use order by label slot for ties. Subtract the sham own-page-minus-other-page match indicator from the declared label indicator. Use a one-sided label-exchange null by swapping the pair signs 399 times. Use 20 matched pairs and p<=0.01 as the minimum and threshold.
synthetic_setup.rule: The stock vs.generators.g_self_citation writer draws from one public practice training vocabulary and recent words on its current page. It is applied unchanged to the same synthetic line-slot shapes for all conditions. The unit field does not change its selection rule. It receives no picture inventory, label links, object-feature group, or declared-versus-sham role.

detail.check: Rerun with the loci stated (unit Lz on the twelve pages, word breaks removed, best cyclic offset per pair, both shuffles). Separately, on the Beinecke scans of f73r and f73v (canvases 1006206 and 1006207), read the labels at loci f73r.7, f73r.20, f73r.26 and f73v.6, f73v.19, f73v.25 without the transliteration in view, and say whether each pair is the same word; if the shift of one place is real it should also show whether the two pages were labelled from starting figures one place apart.
findings: All eight registered numbers reproduce within one agreement. Exact best offset, my run then registered: ZL3b 27 / 27 against nulls 24.8 / 24.9 (p 0.047 and 0.035 against 0.034 and 0.050); IT2a 19 / 19 against 17.8 / 17.8 (p 0.194 and 0.157 against 0.17 and 0.18); RF1b 21 / 20 against 20.6 / 20.5 (p 0.446 and 0.403 against 1.0 and 1.0); GC2a 18 / 18 against 18.4 / 18.4 (p 1.0 / 1.0). One glyph allowed: ZL3b 82 / 82 against 75.7 / 76.2 (p 0.019 and 0.020 against 0.028 and 0.027); IT2a 83 / 82 against 76.3 / 75.2 (p 0.019 and 0.014 against 0.025 and 0.012); RF1b 68 / 69 against 66.2 / 65.7 (p 0.303 and 0.324 against 0.15 and 0.15); GC2a 78 / 75 against 75.5 / 72.9 (p 0.226 and 0.210 against 0.27 and 0.23). My null means land within 0.6 of the registered ones every time; the observed totals differ by at most 3 (GC2a one-glyph), and RF1b's p values move because my observed total is one lower and my null mean is half a point lower.

The ZL excess is one leaf, exactly as registered. f73r against f73v at offset 1: 3 exact agreements in ZL3b and 3 in IT2a, 1 in RF1b and 1 in GC2a. The three agreeing labels are f73r.7 = f73v.6 (okeody), f73r.20 = f73v.19 (okeos; GC2a ohcos), f73r.26 = f73v.25 (oky). No other offset of that pair reaches 2 in any of the four editions, and in RF1b and GC2a the pair's best is a single agreement, so the whole nominal significance of ZL and IT rests on three labels that two other editions do not read the same way.

New: ZL's own clock marks say the shared labels are not at the same figure. ZL3b writes a clock position into every figure label (the <!hh:mm> comment), and the twelve pages' labels fall into three rings: 4 labels above the wheel, 16 in the outer ring, 10 in the inner. Pairing f73r and f73v label by label, the clock marks agree best at shift -1 in the outer ring (15 of 15 comparable pairs within 30 minutes, median -30 minutes), at shift -2 in the inner ring (6 of 8 within 30 minutes), and at shift 0 for the four labels above the wheel (4 of 4, median 0). The shift that carries the shared words, +1, is the worst shift on the page: 1 of 29 pairs within 30 minutes, median +120 minutes. In the outer ring one figure position is 45 minutes, so the shared labels there are 2 positions apart (observed median +90 minutes); in the inner ring one position is 72 minutes and they are about 3 apart (observed median +210 minutes).

So the two pages were labelled from starting figures one place apart - that part of the check is confirmed, and cleanly so in the outer ring - but the rotation runs the other way from the word shift. Under the rotation, the label that sits at the same place on both wheels is f73r.k against f73v.(k+1); the shared words are at f73r.(k+1) against f73v.k, two positions further round. The shared words are therefore a repetition of three words at different figures on recto and verso of one leaf, not one label read twice.

The scan, at the resolution the public server gives (crops listed in results.scan.crops). f73r.7 and f73v.6: same word, yes - six glyphs in the same order, round o, two-legged gallows, small curve, round o, looped glyph with a descender, y. f73r.26 and f73v.25: same three-glyph outline, o, gallows, looped glyph with a descender; the gallows head looks slightly different in the two, and at about a hundred pixels per label I cannot say whether that is a different gallows (as RF1b's oty would need) or pen angle. f73r.20 and f73v.19: not confirmed - the f73v label is faint and turned about 60 degrees, and what I can see there (a run of round glyphs with a tall glyph at one end) does not obviously match the f73r label (o, gallows, short stroke, small curve, o, short final stroke).
detail.interpretation: The registered result stands: there is no list of labels repeating in order from sign to sign, and the only exact excess in any edition is three labels on one leaf, which two of the four editions do not read identically. My clock-mark check sharpens what that excess is not. The registered step read the one-place shift as 'a rotation of the whole wheel, not a counting slip', and the clock marks do show a real one-place rotation between the two pages - the outer rings line up 15 of 15 at that shift. But the rotation goes the opposite way to the word shift, so the shared words are not the same figure's label surviving on both sides of the leaf: they are the same words written two positions apart on the outer ring, three apart on the inner. That is a slightly stranger fact than a copying slip, and a weaker candidate for a decoding lever than it looked: three repeated words on one leaf, at figures that do not correspond. It also means the clock marks are worth using as an independent place marker - they let a label claim be tested against position, not only against spelling, and on these two pages they contradict the obvious reading of the spelling match. On the scan the first pair is plainly the same word and the third pair is the same outline with an unresolvable gallows, so the editions' disagreement about oky against oty is still not settled by the public image.
limits: Eight tests, no correction, exactly as registered; my p values are not smaller than the registered ones because the observed totals are the same, and a p of 1.0 only says the observed total sits at the floor of the null.

RF1b's exact total is 21 where the registered run reports 20, and GC2a's one-glyph total is 78 where it reports 75. I did not chase the difference; it is one to three agreements out of 1,403 comparisons, and it does not change any verdict, but it means my code is not bit-identical to the registered one.

The one-glyph relation is my own reading of 'allowing one glyph of difference': one substitution in equal-length strings, or one insertion where the lengths differ by one. A different tolerance (one substitution or one deletion in either direction, say) would move these totals.

The clock-mark finding uses ZL3b's own annotations, which are quantised to 15 and 30 minutes and are the transcriber's estimate of where each label sits, not a measurement from the scan. My alignment test accepts a pair as agreeing within 30 minutes, which is two thirds of an outer-ring position; the outer ring's 15-of-15 is decisive against the other shifts (0 of 15 at the shared-word shift), but the inner ring aligns only 6 of 8 and the four labels above the wheel are not spaced evenly around the wheel, so I draw no position conclusion from them.

The scan reading is not fully blind: I had the registered step's statement in view, which quotes ZL's readings of the three words, before I cut the crops. Where I could not resolve a glyph I say so rather than choosing between the editions.
The public server's maximum image is what I used; the disputed gallows in f73v.25 and the variant glyph in f73v.6 need a higher-resolution image than this, as the registered step also concluded.

I did not count figures around the two wheels on the scan. The position arithmetic comes from the transcription's line order and clock marks, so it is a claim about the transcription's internal consistency, not an independent visual measurement of the two wheels.
detail.methods: Three scripts, all read-only over the public practice partition. pl4021.py parses each of the four pinned transliterations with vs.ivtff, keeps only lines whose unit is L and subtype z (the figure labels), joins the words of each line into one glyph string with ?*{} brackets stripped, and groups each page's labels into rings by maximal runs of consecutive line numbers - the groups the transcription itself marks. For each of the 66 page pairs it computes, vectorised in numpy, the number of agreements at every cyclic offset of the longer page against the shorter and takes the maximum, then sums over pairs; the same code counts agreements at the same position with no offset. Two nulls, 1,000 shuffles each from random.Random(408): labels shuffled over the whole page, and labels shuffled only inside their own ring. p is (count of nulls at or above the observed total + 1) / 1001. pl4021_oneglyph.py is the same run with the equality test replaced by a relation that also accepts two labels that differ by one glyph (one substitution in equal-length strings, or one insertion in strings whose lengths differ by one), precomputed as a boolean matrix over the distinct label strings; the observed value and both nulls are recomputed under it. pl4021_clock.py reads the clock position out of the <!hh:mm> comment that ZL3b attaches to each figure label, pairs the f73r and f73v label lists at every shift from -4 to +4, and reports the signed clock difference per pair, overall and ring by ring; a shift where the two pages' clock marks agree is a shift where their label numbering refers to the same figure. The scan part is my own reading of crops of the two Yale canvases at the maximum size the IIIF server serves; the crop boxes are recorded in results.scan.

reproducibility.instructions: From the repository root, with the four pinned transliterations fetched (vs.fetch), extract the three scripts below to /tmp and run them with PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/pl4021.py (about 4 minutes), PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/pl4021_oneglyph.py (about 4 minutes) and PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/pl4021_clock.py (a few seconds). The first two print, per transliteration, the same-position count, the best exact offset with both null means and p values, and the best one-glyph offset with both null means and p values; the third prints the clock-difference table that the position finding rests on. All three only read the public practice partition and the transcription comments; none writes to the repository. The scan part is reproducible from the crop boxes in results.scan: fetch the two canvases at full size and cut those boxes.

scripts.pl4021.py:
"""P-L4-021: rerun of P-L4-007 on the figure labels only (unit Lz), four transliterations.

Declared before running (from the step): the figure-label loci of the twelve zodiac pages, glyph
strings with word breaks removed; for each of the 66 page pairs the largest number of agreements
over every cyclic offset of the longer page against the shorter, summed; 1000 shuffles; two nulls,
labels shuffled over the whole page and labels shuffled only inside their own ring (the groups the
transcription marks). Also reported: agreements at the same position with no offset, and which page
pair carries the excess.
"""
import sys, random, collections
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from vs import corpus, ivtff, path

TURNS = 1000
SEED = 408


def labels(translit):
    """page -> list of (line, ring index, glyph string with word breaks removed)."""
    pages = ivtff.parse(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS[translit]))
    out = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for pg in pages:
        for ln in pg.lines:
            if ln.unit == "L" and ln.subtype == "z" and ln.words:
                w = "".join(x.strip("?*{}") for x in ln.words)
                if w:
                    out[pg.id].append((ln.n, w))
    for p in out:
        out[p].sort()
    return out


def rings(rows):
    """Maximal runs of consecutive line numbers: the label groups the transcription marks.
    Returns a list of lists of positions within `rows`."""
    groups, cur = [], [0]
    for i in range(1, len(rows)):
        if rows[i][0] == rows[i - 1][0] + 1:
            cur.append(i)
        else:
            groups.append(cur)
            cur = [i]
    groups.append(cur)
    return groups


def pair_index(La, Lb):
    """M[o, i] = (i + o) % La: index into the longer page for offset o, position i of the shorter."""
    return (np.arange(Lb)[None, :] + np.arange(La)[:, None]) % La


def measure(pages, shuffles=None):
    """pages: dict page -> list of (line, string). Returns summed best-offset agreements, summed
    same-position agreements, summed comparisons, and the per-pair best offsets."""
    ids = sorted(pages)
    codes = {s: i for i, s in enumerate({s for rows in pages.values() for _n, s in rows})}
    arr = {p: np.array([codes[s] for _n, s in rows], dtype=np.int32) for p, rows in pages.items()}
    best = same = cmp_ = 0
    detail = []
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ids)):
            a, b = arr[ids[i]], arr[ids[j]]
            if len(a) < len(b):
                a, b = b, a
            M = pair_index(len(a), len(b))
            agree = (a[M] == b[None, :]).sum(axis=1)
            o = int(agree.argmax())
            best += int(agree[o])
            n = min(len(a), len(b))
            same += int((a[:n] == b[:n]).sum())
            cmp_ += n
            detail.append((ids[i], ids[j], o, int(agree[o]), int((a[:n] == b[:n]).sum())))
    return best, same, cmp_, detail


def shuffled(pages, rng, within_ring):
    out = {}
    for p, rows in pages.items():
        items = list(rows)
        if within_ring:
            for g in rings(rows):
                pick = [rows[i] for i in g]
                rng.shuffle(pick)
                for k, i in enumerate(g):
                    items[i] = pick[k]
        else:
            rng.shuffle(items)
        out[p] = items
    return out


for tl in ("zl", "it", "rf", "gc"):
    pages = labels(tl)
    sizes = sorted((len(v) for v in pages.values()), reverse=True)
    obs_best, obs_same, cmp_, detail = measure(pages)
    one = sum(1 for p, q, o, e, s in detail if e >= 1)
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    nulls = {True: [], False: []}
    for _ in range(TURNS):
        for within in (True, False):
            pages2 = shuffled(pages, rng, within)
            nulls[within].append(measure(pages2)[0])
    n_page = [x for x in nulls[False]]
    n_ring = [x for x in nulls[True]]
    p_page = (sum(1 for x in n_page if x >= obs_best) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    p_ring = (sum(1 for x in n_ring if x >= obs_best) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    print(f"{tl}: pages={len(pages)} labels={sum(sizes)} sizes={sizes}")
    print(f"   same position, no offset: {obs_same} in {cmp_} comparisons ({100 * obs_same / cmp_:.2f}%)")
    print(f"   best cyclic offset: {obs_best}; null whole-page mean {sum(n_page) / TURNS:.1f} (p={p_page:.3f}); "
          f"null within-ring mean {sum(n_ring) / TURNS:.1f} (p={p_ring:.3f})", flush=True)
    top = sorted(detail, key=lambda d: -d[3])[:4]
    print("   pairs carrying the most agreements:", ", ".join(f"{a}+{b} offset {o}: {e}" for a, b, o, e, _s in top), flush=True)
scripts.pl4021_clock.py:
"""P-L4-021: are the three shared f73r/f73v labels the same figure's label, seen twice?

ZL3b writes a clock position into every figure label (the <!hh:mm> comment in the transcription
file), which is the scribe's own place marker on the wheel. If the one-place shift between f73r
and f73v were a rotation of the labelled wheel, the shared labels would sit at the same clock
position on the two pages. This script pairs the two pages' label lists at every small shift,
separately for each of the three label rings (the four labels above the wheel, the 16-label outer
ring, the 10-label inner ring), and prints the clock difference per pair. A shift where the rings
line up is where the two wheels' label numbering refers to the same figure.
"""
import re
import sys, os

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
from vs import corpus, ivtff, path


def clockmap(pid, translit="zl"):
    """line number -> clock position in minutes, read from the <!hh:mm> comment."""
    text = open(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS[translit]), encoding="utf-8").read()
    out = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(rf"<{pid}\.(\d+),[^>]*>\s*(.*)$", line)
        if not m:
            continue
        c = re.search(r"<!\s*(\d\d):(\d\d)>", m.group(2))
        if c:
            out[int(m.group(1))] = int(c.group(1)) * 60 + int(c.group(2))
    return out


def labels(pid, cm, translit="zl"):
    """figure labels on one page, in line order: (line, clock minutes, glyph string)."""
    for pg in ivtff.parse(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS[translit])):
        if pg.id != pid:
            continue
        return sorted(
            (ln.n, cm[ln.n], "".join(w.strip("?*{}") for w in ln.words))
            for ln in pg.lines
            if ln.unit == "L" and ln.subtype == "z" and ln.words and ln.n in cm
        )


def rings(rows):
    """Maximal runs of consecutive line numbers: the label groups the transcription marks."""
    groups, cur = [], [0]
    for i in range(1, len(rows)):
        if rows[i][0] == rows[i - 1][0] + 1:
            cur.append(i)
        else:
            groups.append(cur)
            cur = [i]
    groups.append(cur)
    return groups


def circ(a, b):
    """Signed clock difference a - b in minutes, folded into (-360, 360]."""
    d = (a - b) % 720
    return d - 720 if d > 360 else d


r = labels("f73r", clockmap("f73r"))
v = labels("f73v", clockmap("f73v"))
gr = {i: g for g, grp in enumerate(rings(r)) for i in grp}
gv = {i: g for g, grp in enumerate(rings(v)) for i in grp}
print(f"labels with clock marks: f73r {len(r)}, f73v {len(v)}")
print(f"rings (labels above the wheel, outer ring, inner ring): "
      f"f73r {[len(g) for g in rings(r)]}, f73v {[len(g) for g in rings(v)]}")

# the shift that carries the shared words, and the clock difference it implies
for s in range(-4, 5):
    pairs = [(r[i + s], v[i]) for i in range(len(v)) if 0 <= i + s < len(r)]
    same = sum(1 for a, b in pairs if a[2] == b[2])
    ds = sorted(circ(a[1], b[1]) for a, b in pairs)
    med = ds[len(ds) // 2]
    print(f"shift {s:+d}: {same} shared words; clock difference median {med:+d} min, "
          f"{sum(1 for d in ds if abs(d) <= 30)}/{len(ds)} pairs within 30 min")

print("\nper ring, at the shift where that ring's clock marks line up:")
for ring, s in ((0, 0), (1, -1), (2, -2)):
    ds = sorted(circ(r[i + s][1], v[i][1]) for i in range(len(v))
                if 0 <= i + s < len(r) and gv[i] == ring and gr[i + s] == ring)
    print(f"ring {ring}, shift {s:+d}: {ds}")

print("\nper ring, at the shift that carries the shared words (s=+1):")
for ring in (0, 1, 2):
    ds = sorted(circ(r[i + 1][1], v[i][1]) for i in range(len(v))
                if 0 <= i + 1 < len(r) and gv[i] == ring and gr[i + 1] == ring)
    step = 720 / len(ds) if ds else 0
    print(f"ring {ring}, shift +1: {ds} (one figure position there is {step:.0f} min)")
scripts.pl4021_oneglyph.py:
"""P-L4-021: rerun of P-L4-007 on the figure labels only (unit Lz), four transliterations.

Declared before running (from the step): the figure-label loci of the twelve zodiac pages, glyph
strings with word breaks removed; for each of the 66 page pairs the largest number of agreements
over every cyclic offset of the longer page against the shorter, summed; 1000 shuffles; two nulls,
labels shuffled over the whole page and labels shuffled only inside their own ring (the groups the
transcription marks). Also reported: agreements at the same position with no offset, and which page
pair carries the excess.
"""
import sys, random, collections
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from vs import corpus, ivtff, path

TURNS = 1000
SEED = 408


def labels(translit):
    """page -> list of (line, ring index, glyph string with word breaks removed)."""
    pages = ivtff.parse(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS[translit]))
    out = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for pg in pages:
        for ln in pg.lines:
            if ln.unit == "L" and ln.subtype == "z" and ln.words:
                w = "".join(x.strip("?*{}") for x in ln.words)
                if w:
                    out[pg.id].append((ln.n, w))
    for p in out:
        out[p].sort()
    return out


def rings(rows):
    """Maximal runs of consecutive line numbers: the label groups the transcription marks.
    Returns a list of lists of positions within `rows`."""
    groups, cur = [], [0]
    for i in range(1, len(rows)):
        if rows[i][0] == rows[i - 1][0] + 1:
            cur.append(i)
        else:
            groups.append(cur)
            cur = [i]
    groups.append(cur)
    return groups


def pair_index(La, Lb):
    """M[o, i] = (i + o) % La: index into the longer page for offset o, position i of the shorter."""
    return (np.arange(Lb)[None, :] + np.arange(La)[:, None]) % La


def one_glyph(a, b):
    if a == b or abs(len(a) - len(b)) > 1:
        return False
    if len(a) == len(b):
        return sum(x != y for x, y in zip(a, b)) == 1
    lo, hi = (a, b) if len(a) < len(b) else (b, a)
    i = 0
    while i < len(lo) and lo[i] == hi[i]:
        i += 1
    return lo[i:] == hi[i + 1:]


def measure(pages, near=None):
    """pages: dict page -> list of (line, string). Returns summed best-offset agreements, summed
    same-position agreements, summed comparisons, and the per-pair best offsets."""
    ids = sorted(pages)
    strs = sorted({s for rows in pages.values() for _n, s in rows})
    codes = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(strs)}
    if near is not None:
        near[:, :] = False
        for i, a in enumerate(strs):
            for j, b in enumerate(strs[i:], start=i):
                v = a == b or one_glyph(a, b)
                near[i, j] = near[j, i] = v
    arr = {p: np.array([codes[s] for _n, s in rows], dtype=np.int32) for p, rows in pages.items()}
    best = same = cmp_ = 0
    detail = []
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ids)):
            a, b = arr[ids[i]], arr[ids[j]]
            if len(a) < len(b):
                a, b = b, a
            M = pair_index(len(a), len(b))
            agree = (near[a[M], b[None, :]] if near is not None else (a[M] == b[None, :])).sum(axis=1)
            o = int(agree.argmax())
            best += int(agree[o])
            n = min(len(a), len(b))
            same += int((near[a[:n], b[:n]] if near is not None else (a[:n] == b[:n])).sum())
            cmp_ += n
            detail.append((ids[i], ids[j], o, int(agree[o]), int((a[:n] == b[:n]).sum())))
    return best, same, cmp_, detail


def shuffled(pages, rng, within_ring):
    out = {}
    for p, rows in pages.items():
        items = list(rows)
        if within_ring:
            for g in rings(rows):
                pick = [rows[i] for i in g]
                rng.shuffle(pick)
                for k, i in enumerate(g):
                    items[i] = pick[k]
        else:
            rng.shuffle(items)
        out[p] = items
    return out


for tl in ("zl", "it", "rf", "gc"):
    pages = labels(tl)
    sizes = sorted((len(v) for v in pages.values()), reverse=True)
    near = np.zeros((len({s for rows in pages.values() for _n, s in rows}),) * 2, dtype=bool)
    obs_best, obs_same, cmp_, detail = measure(pages)
    obs_best_g, obs_same_g, _, detail_g = measure(pages, near=near)
    one = sum(1 for p, q, o, e, s in detail if e >= 1)
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    nulls = {True: [], False: []}
    nulls_g = {True: [], False: []}
    for _ in range(TURNS):
        for within in (True, False):
            pages2 = shuffled(pages, rng, within)
            nulls[within].append(measure(pages2)[0])
            nulls_g[within].append(measure(pages2, near=near)[0])
    n_page = [x for x in nulls[False]]
    n_ring = [x for x in nulls[True]]
    p_page = (sum(1 for x in n_page if x >= obs_best) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    p_ring = (sum(1 for x in n_ring if x >= obs_best) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    print(f"{tl}: pages={len(pages)} labels={sum(sizes)} sizes={sizes}")
    print(f"   same position, no offset: {obs_same} in {cmp_} comparisons ({100 * obs_same / cmp_:.2f}%)")
    print(f"   best cyclic offset: {obs_best}; null whole-page mean {sum(n_page) / TURNS:.1f} (p={p_page:.3f}); "
          f"null within-ring mean {sum(n_ring) / TURNS:.1f} (p={p_ring:.3f})", flush=True)
    gp = (sum(1 for x in nulls_g[False] if x >= obs_best_g) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    gr = (sum(1 for x in nulls_g[True] if x >= obs_best_g) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    print(f"   best cyclic offset, one glyph allowed: {obs_best_g}; null whole-page mean {sum(nulls_g[False]) / TURNS:.1f} (p={gp:.3f}); "
          f"null within-ring mean {sum(nulls_g[True]) / TURNS:.1f} (p={gr:.3f}); same position {obs_same_g}", flush=True)
    topg = sorted(detail_g, key=lambda d: -d[3])[:4]
    print("   one-glyph pairs carrying the most agreements:", ", ".join(f"{a}+{b} offset {o}: {e}" for a, b, o, e, _s in topg), flush=True)
    top = sorted(detail, key=lambda d: -d[3])[:4]
    print("   pairs carrying the most agreements:", ", ".join(f"{a}+{b} offset {o}: {e}" for a, b, o, e, _s in top), flush=True)

experiment.json.summary: An independent rerun of P-L4-007 on 299 figure labels reproduces all eight registered numbers to within one agreement (ZL3b exact 27 against a null of 24.8, p = 0.047 and 0.035; one glyph allowed 82 against 75.7, p = 0.019 and 0.020), and ZL's own clock marks put the three shared f73r/f73v labels two to three figure positions apart, so the one-place shift is not one label copied across the leaf but three words repeated at figures that do not correspond.

step.json.check: Rerun with the loci stated (unit Lz on the twelve pages, word breaks removed, best cyclic offset per pair, both shuffles). Separately, on the Beinecke scans of f73r and f73v (canvases 1006206 and 1006207), read the labels at loci f73r.7, f73r.20, f73r.26 and f73v.6, f73v.19, f73v.25 without the transliteration in view, and say whether each pair is the same word; if the shift of one place is real it should also show whether the two pages were labelled from starting figures one place apart.
findings: All eight registered numbers reproduce within one agreement. Exact best offset, my run then registered: ZL3b 27 / 27 against nulls 24.8 / 24.9 (p 0.047 and 0.035 against 0.034 and 0.050); IT2a 19 / 19 against 17.8 / 17.8 (p 0.194 and 0.157 against 0.17 and 0.18); RF1b 21 / 20 against 20.6 / 20.5 (p 0.446 and 0.403 against 1.0 and 1.0); GC2a 18 / 18 against 18.4 / 18.4 (p 1.0 / 1.0). One glyph allowed: ZL3b 82 / 82 against 75.7 / 76.2 (p 0.019 and 0.020 against 0.028 and 0.027); IT2a 83 / 82 against 76.3 / 75.2 (p 0.019 and 0.014 against 0.025 and 0.012); RF1b 68 / 69 against 66.2 / 65.7 (p 0.303 and 0.324 against 0.15 and 0.15); GC2a 78 / 75 against 75.5 / 72.9 (p 0.226 and 0.210 against 0.27 and 0.23). My null means land within 0.6 of the registered ones every time; the observed totals differ by at most 3 (GC2a one-glyph), and RF1b's p values move because my observed total is one lower and my null mean is half a point lower.

The ZL excess is one leaf, exactly as registered. f73r against f73v at offset 1: 3 exact agreements in ZL3b and 3 in IT2a, 1 in RF1b and 1 in GC2a. The three agreeing labels are f73r.7 = f73v.6 (okeody), f73r.20 = f73v.19 (okeos; GC2a ohcos), f73r.26 = f73v.25 (oky). No other offset of that pair reaches 2 in any of the four editions, and in RF1b and GC2a the pair's best is a single agreement, so the whole nominal significance of ZL and IT rests on three labels that two other editions do not read the same way.

New: ZL's own clock marks say the shared labels are not at the same figure. ZL3b writes a clock position into every figure label (the <!hh:mm> comment), and the twelve pages' labels fall into three rings: 4 labels above the wheel, 16 in the outer ring, 10 in the inner. Pairing f73r and f73v label by label, the clock marks agree best at shift -1 in the outer ring (15 of 15 comparable pairs within 30 minutes, median -30 minutes), at shift -2 in the inner ring (6 of 8 within 30 minutes), and at shift 0 for the four labels above the wheel (4 of 4, median 0). The shift that carries the shared words, +1, is the worst shift on the page: 1 of 29 pairs within 30 minutes, median +120 minutes. In the outer ring one figure position is 45 minutes, so the shared labels there are 2 positions apart (observed median +90 minutes); in the inner ring one position is 72 minutes and they are about 3 apart (observed median +210 minutes).

So the two pages were labelled from starting figures one place apart - that part of the check is confirmed, and cleanly so in the outer ring - but the rotation runs the other way from the word shift. Under the rotation, the label that sits at the same place on both wheels is f73r.k against f73v.(k+1); the shared words are at f73r.(k+1) against f73v.k, two positions further round. The shared words are therefore a repetition of three words at different figures on recto and verso of one leaf, not one label read twice.

The scan, at the resolution the public server gives (crops listed in results.scan.crops). f73r.7 and f73v.6: same word, yes - six glyphs in the same order, round o, two-legged gallows, small curve, round o, looped glyph with a descender, y. f73r.26 and f73v.25: same three-glyph outline, o, gallows, looped glyph with a descender; the gallows head looks slightly different in the two, and at about a hundred pixels per label I cannot say whether that is a different gallows (as RF1b's oty would need) or pen angle. f73r.20 and f73v.19: not confirmed - the f73v label is faint and turned about 60 degrees, and what I can see there (a run of round glyphs with a tall glyph at one end) does not obviously match the f73r label (o, gallows, short stroke, small curve, o, short final stroke).
step.json.interpretation: The registered result stands: there is no list of labels repeating in order from sign to sign, and the only exact excess in any edition is three labels on one leaf, which two of the four editions do not read identically. My clock-mark check sharpens what that excess is not. The registered step read the one-place shift as 'a rotation of the whole wheel, not a counting slip', and the clock marks do show a real one-place rotation between the two pages - the outer rings line up 15 of 15 at that shift. But the rotation goes the opposite way to the word shift, so the shared words are not the same figure's label surviving on both sides of the leaf: they are the same words written two positions apart on the outer ring, three apart on the inner. That is a slightly stranger fact than a copying slip, and a weaker candidate for a decoding lever than it looked: three repeated words on one leaf, at figures that do not correspond. It also means the clock marks are worth using as an independent place marker - they let a label claim be tested against position, not only against spelling, and on these two pages they contradict the obvious reading of the spelling match. On the scan the first pair is plainly the same word and the third pair is the same outline with an unresolvable gallows, so the editions' disagreement about oky against oty is still not settled by the public image.
limits: Eight tests, no correction, exactly as registered; my p values are not smaller than the registered ones because the observed totals are the same, and a p of 1.0 only says the observed total sits at the floor of the null.

RF1b's exact total is 21 where the registered run reports 20, and GC2a's one-glyph total is 78 where it reports 75. I did not chase the difference; it is one to three agreements out of 1,403 comparisons, and it does not change any verdict, but it means my code is not bit-identical to the registered one.

The one-glyph relation is my own reading of 'allowing one glyph of difference': one substitution in equal-length strings, or one insertion where the lengths differ by one. A different tolerance (one substitution or one deletion in either direction, say) would move these totals.

The clock-mark finding uses ZL3b's own annotations, which are quantised to 15 and 30 minutes and are the transcriber's estimate of where each label sits, not a measurement from the scan. My alignment test accepts a pair as agreeing within 30 minutes, which is two thirds of an outer-ring position; the outer ring's 15-of-15 is decisive against the other shifts (0 of 15 at the shared-word shift), but the inner ring aligns only 6 of 8 and the four labels above the wheel are not spaced evenly around the wheel, so I draw no position conclusion from them.

The scan reading is not fully blind: I had the registered step's statement in view, which quotes ZL's readings of the three words, before I cut the crops. Where I could not resolve a glyph I say so rather than choosing between the editions.
The public server's maximum image is what I used; the disputed gallows in f73v.25 and the variant glyph in f73v.6 need a higher-resolution image than this, as the registered step also concluded.

I did not count figures around the two wheels on the scan. The position arithmetic comes from the transcription's line order and clock marks, so it is a claim about the transcription's internal consistency, not an independent visual measurement of the two wheels.
step.json.methods: Three scripts, all read-only over the public practice partition. pl4021.py parses each of the four pinned transliterations with vs.ivtff, keeps only lines whose unit is L and subtype z (the figure labels), joins the words of each line into one glyph string with ?*{} brackets stripped, and groups each page's labels into rings by maximal runs of consecutive line numbers - the groups the transcription itself marks. For each of the 66 page pairs it computes, vectorised in numpy, the number of agreements at every cyclic offset of the longer page against the shorter and takes the maximum, then sums over pairs; the same code counts agreements at the same position with no offset. Two nulls, 1,000 shuffles each from random.Random(408): labels shuffled over the whole page, and labels shuffled only inside their own ring. p is (count of nulls at or above the observed total + 1) / 1001. pl4021_oneglyph.py is the same run with the equality test replaced by a relation that also accepts two labels that differ by one glyph (one substitution in equal-length strings, or one insertion in strings whose lengths differ by one), precomputed as a boolean matrix over the distinct label strings; the observed value and both nulls are recomputed under it. pl4021_clock.py reads the clock position out of the <!hh:mm> comment that ZL3b attaches to each figure label, pairs the f73r and f73v label lists at every shift from -4 to +4, and reports the signed clock difference per pair, overall and ring by ring; a shift where the two pages' clock marks agree is a shift where their label numbering refers to the same figure. The scan part is my own reading of crops of the two Yale canvases at the maximum size the IIIF server serves; the crop boxes are recorded in results.scan.

reproducibility.instructions: From the repository root, with the four pinned transliterations fetched (vs.fetch), extract the three scripts below to /tmp and run them with PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/pl4021.py (about 4 minutes), PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/pl4021_oneglyph.py (about 4 minutes) and PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/pl4021_clock.py (a few seconds). The first two print, per transliteration, the same-position count, the best exact offset with both null means and p values, and the best one-glyph offset with both null means and p values; the third prints the clock-difference table that the position finding rests on. All three only read the public practice partition and the transcription comments; none writes to the repository. The scan part is reproducible from the crop boxes in results.scan: fetch the two canvases at full size and cut those boxes.

scripts.pl4021.py:
"""P-L4-021: rerun of P-L4-007 on the figure labels only (unit Lz), four transliterations.

Declared before running (from the step): the figure-label loci of the twelve zodiac pages, glyph
strings with word breaks removed; for each of the 66 page pairs the largest number of agreements
over every cyclic offset of the longer page against the shorter, summed; 1000 shuffles; two nulls,
labels shuffled over the whole page and labels shuffled only inside their own ring (the groups the
transcription marks). Also reported: agreements at the same position with no offset, and which page
pair carries the excess.
"""
import sys, random, collections
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from vs import corpus, ivtff, path

TURNS = 1000
SEED = 408


def labels(translit):
    """page -> list of (line, ring index, glyph string with word breaks removed)."""
    pages = ivtff.parse(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS[translit]))
    out = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for pg in pages:
        for ln in pg.lines:
            if ln.unit == "L" and ln.subtype == "z" and ln.words:
                w = "".join(x.strip("?*{}") for x in ln.words)
                if w:
                    out[pg.id].append((ln.n, w))
    for p in out:
        out[p].sort()
    return out


def rings(rows):
    """Maximal runs of consecutive line numbers: the label groups the transcription marks.
    Returns a list of lists of positions within `rows`."""
    groups, cur = [], [0]
    for i in range(1, len(rows)):
        if rows[i][0] == rows[i - 1][0] + 1:
            cur.append(i)
        else:
            groups.append(cur)
            cur = [i]
    groups.append(cur)
    return groups


def pair_index(La, Lb):
    """M[o, i] = (i + o) % La: index into the longer page for offset o, position i of the shorter."""
    return (np.arange(Lb)[None, :] + np.arange(La)[:, None]) % La


def measure(pages, shuffles=None):
    """pages: dict page -> list of (line, string). Returns summed best-offset agreements, summed
    same-position agreements, summed comparisons, and the per-pair best offsets."""
    ids = sorted(pages)
    codes = {s: i for i, s in enumerate({s for rows in pages.values() for _n, s in rows})}
    arr = {p: np.array([codes[s] for _n, s in rows], dtype=np.int32) for p, rows in pages.items()}
    best = same = cmp_ = 0
    detail = []
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ids)):
            a, b = arr[ids[i]], arr[ids[j]]
            if len(a) < len(b):
                a, b = b, a
            M = pair_index(len(a), len(b))
            agree = (a[M] == b[None, :]).sum(axis=1)
            o = int(agree.argmax())
            best += int(agree[o])
            n = min(len(a), len(b))
            same += int((a[:n] == b[:n]).sum())
            cmp_ += n
            detail.append((ids[i], ids[j], o, int(agree[o]), int((a[:n] == b[:n]).sum())))
    return best, same, cmp_, detail


def shuffled(pages, rng, within_ring):
    out = {}
    for p, rows in pages.items():
        items = list(rows)
        if within_ring:
            for g in rings(rows):
                pick = [rows[i] for i in g]
                rng.shuffle(pick)
                for k, i in enumerate(g):
                    items[i] = pick[k]
        else:
            rng.shuffle(items)
        out[p] = items
    return out


for tl in ("zl", "it", "rf", "gc"):
    pages = labels(tl)
    sizes = sorted((len(v) for v in pages.values()), reverse=True)
    obs_best, obs_same, cmp_, detail = measure(pages)
    one = sum(1 for p, q, o, e, s in detail if e >= 1)
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    nulls = {True: [], False: []}
    for _ in range(TURNS):
        for within in (True, False):
            pages2 = shuffled(pages, rng, within)
            nulls[within].append(measure(pages2)[0])
    n_page = [x for x in nulls[False]]
    n_ring = [x for x in nulls[True]]
    p_page = (sum(1 for x in n_page if x >= obs_best) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    p_ring = (sum(1 for x in n_ring if x >= obs_best) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    print(f"{tl}: pages={len(pages)} labels={sum(sizes)} sizes={sizes}")
    print(f"   same position, no offset: {obs_same} in {cmp_} comparisons ({100 * obs_same / cmp_:.2f}%)")
    print(f"   best cyclic offset: {obs_best}; null whole-page mean {sum(n_page) / TURNS:.1f} (p={p_page:.3f}); "
          f"null within-ring mean {sum(n_ring) / TURNS:.1f} (p={p_ring:.3f})", flush=True)
    top = sorted(detail, key=lambda d: -d[3])[:4]
    print("   pairs carrying the most agreements:", ", ".join(f"{a}+{b} offset {o}: {e}" for a, b, o, e, _s in top), flush=True)
scripts.pl4021_clock.py:
"""P-L4-021: are the three shared f73r/f73v labels the same figure's label, seen twice?

ZL3b writes a clock position into every figure label (the <!hh:mm> comment in the transcription
file), which is the scribe's own place marker on the wheel. If the one-place shift between f73r
and f73v were a rotation of the labelled wheel, the shared labels would sit at the same clock
position on the two pages. This script pairs the two pages' label lists at every small shift,
separately for each of the three label rings (the four labels above the wheel, the 16-label outer
ring, the 10-label inner ring), and prints the clock difference per pair. A shift where the rings
line up is where the two wheels' label numbering refers to the same figure.
"""
import re
import sys, os

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
from vs import corpus, ivtff, path


def clockmap(pid, translit="zl"):
    """line number -> clock position in minutes, read from the <!hh:mm> comment."""
    text = open(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS[translit]), encoding="utf-8").read()
    out = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(rf"<{pid}\.(\d+),[^>]*>\s*(.*)$", line)
        if not m:
            continue
        c = re.search(r"<!\s*(\d\d):(\d\d)>", m.group(2))
        if c:
            out[int(m.group(1))] = int(c.group(1)) * 60 + int(c.group(2))
    return out


def labels(pid, cm, translit="zl"):
    """figure labels on one page, in line order: (line, clock minutes, glyph string)."""
    for pg in ivtff.parse(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS[translit])):
        if pg.id != pid:
            continue
        return sorted(
            (ln.n, cm[ln.n], "".join(w.strip("?*{}") for w in ln.words))
            for ln in pg.lines
            if ln.unit == "L" and ln.subtype == "z" and ln.words and ln.n in cm
        )


def rings(rows):
    """Maximal runs of consecutive line numbers: the label groups the transcription marks."""
    groups, cur = [], [0]
    for i in range(1, len(rows)):
        if rows[i][0] == rows[i - 1][0] + 1:
            cur.append(i)
        else:
            groups.append(cur)
            cur = [i]
    groups.append(cur)
    return groups


def circ(a, b):
    """Signed clock difference a - b in minutes, folded into (-360, 360]."""
    d = (a - b) % 720
    return d - 720 if d > 360 else d


r = labels("f73r", clockmap("f73r"))
v = labels("f73v", clockmap("f73v"))
gr = {i: g for g, grp in enumerate(rings(r)) for i in grp}
gv = {i: g for g, grp in enumerate(rings(v)) for i in grp}
print(f"labels with clock marks: f73r {len(r)}, f73v {len(v)}")
print(f"rings (labels above the wheel, outer ring, inner ring): "
      f"f73r {[len(g) for g in rings(r)]}, f73v {[len(g) for g in rings(v)]}")

# the shift that carries the shared words, and the clock difference it implies
for s in range(-4, 5):
    pairs = [(r[i + s], v[i]) for i in range(len(v)) if 0 <= i + s < len(r)]
    same = sum(1 for a, b in pairs if a[2] == b[2])
    ds = sorted(circ(a[1], b[1]) for a, b in pairs)
    med = ds[len(ds) // 2]
    print(f"shift {s:+d}: {same} shared words; clock difference median {med:+d} min, "
          f"{sum(1 for d in ds if abs(d) <= 30)}/{len(ds)} pairs within 30 min")

print("\nper ring, at the shift where that ring's clock marks line up:")
for ring, s in ((0, 0), (1, -1), (2, -2)):
    ds = sorted(circ(r[i + s][1], v[i][1]) for i in range(len(v))
                if 0 <= i + s < len(r) and gv[i] == ring and gr[i + s] == ring)
    print(f"ring {ring}, shift {s:+d}: {ds}")

print("\nper ring, at the shift that carries the shared words (s=+1):")
for ring in (0, 1, 2):
    ds = sorted(circ(r[i + 1][1], v[i][1]) for i in range(len(v))
                if 0 <= i + 1 < len(r) and gv[i] == ring and gr[i + 1] == ring)
    step = 720 / len(ds) if ds else 0
    print(f"ring {ring}, shift +1: {ds} (one figure position there is {step:.0f} min)")
scripts.pl4021_oneglyph.py:
"""P-L4-021: rerun of P-L4-007 on the figure labels only (unit Lz), four transliterations.

Declared before running (from the step): the figure-label loci of the twelve zodiac pages, glyph
strings with word breaks removed; for each of the 66 page pairs the largest number of agreements
over every cyclic offset of the longer page against the shorter, summed; 1000 shuffles; two nulls,
labels shuffled over the whole page and labels shuffled only inside their own ring (the groups the
transcription marks). Also reported: agreements at the same position with no offset, and which page
pair carries the excess.
"""
import sys, random, collections
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from vs import corpus, ivtff, path

TURNS = 1000
SEED = 408


def labels(translit):
    """page -> list of (line, ring index, glyph string with word breaks removed)."""
    pages = ivtff.parse(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS[translit]))
    out = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for pg in pages:
        for ln in pg.lines:
            if ln.unit == "L" and ln.subtype == "z" and ln.words:
                w = "".join(x.strip("?*{}") for x in ln.words)
                if w:
                    out[pg.id].append((ln.n, w))
    for p in out:
        out[p].sort()
    return out


def rings(rows):
    """Maximal runs of consecutive line numbers: the label groups the transcription marks.
    Returns a list of lists of positions within `rows`."""
    groups, cur = [], [0]
    for i in range(1, len(rows)):
        if rows[i][0] == rows[i - 1][0] + 1:
            cur.append(i)
        else:
            groups.append(cur)
            cur = [i]
    groups.append(cur)
    return groups


def pair_index(La, Lb):
    """M[o, i] = (i + o) % La: index into the longer page for offset o, position i of the shorter."""
    return (np.arange(Lb)[None, :] + np.arange(La)[:, None]) % La


def one_glyph(a, b):
    if a == b or abs(len(a) - len(b)) > 1:
        return False
    if len(a) == len(b):
        return sum(x != y for x, y in zip(a, b)) == 1
    lo, hi = (a, b) if len(a) < len(b) else (b, a)
    i = 0
    while i < len(lo) and lo[i] == hi[i]:
        i += 1
    return lo[i:] == hi[i + 1:]


def measure(pages, near=None):
    """pages: dict page -> list of (line, string). Returns summed best-offset agreements, summed
    same-position agreements, summed comparisons, and the per-pair best offsets."""
    ids = sorted(pages)
    strs = sorted({s for rows in pages.values() for _n, s in rows})
    codes = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(strs)}
    if near is not None:
        near[:, :] = False
        for i, a in enumerate(strs):
            for j, b in enumerate(strs[i:], start=i):
                v = a == b or one_glyph(a, b)
                near[i, j] = near[j, i] = v
    arr = {p: np.array([codes[s] for _n, s in rows], dtype=np.int32) for p, rows in pages.items()}
    best = same = cmp_ = 0
    detail = []
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ids)):
            a, b = arr[ids[i]], arr[ids[j]]
            if len(a) < len(b):
                a, b = b, a
            M = pair_index(len(a), len(b))
            agree = (near[a[M], b[None, :]] if near is not None else (a[M] == b[None, :])).sum(axis=1)
            o = int(agree.argmax())
            best += int(agree[o])
            n = min(len(a), len(b))
            same += int((near[a[:n], b[:n]] if near is not None else (a[:n] == b[:n])).sum())
            cmp_ += n
            detail.append((ids[i], ids[j], o, int(agree[o]), int((a[:n] == b[:n]).sum())))
    return best, same, cmp_, detail


def shuffled(pages, rng, within_ring):
    out = {}
    for p, rows in pages.items():
        items = list(rows)
        if within_ring:
            for g in rings(rows):
                pick = [rows[i] for i in g]
                rng.shuffle(pick)
                for k, i in enumerate(g):
                    items[i] = pick[k]
        else:
            rng.shuffle(items)
        out[p] = items
    return out


for tl in ("zl", "it", "rf", "gc"):
    pages = labels(tl)
    sizes = sorted((len(v) for v in pages.values()), reverse=True)
    near = np.zeros((len({s for rows in pages.values() for _n, s in rows}),) * 2, dtype=bool)
    obs_best, obs_same, cmp_, detail = measure(pages)
    obs_best_g, obs_same_g, _, detail_g = measure(pages, near=near)
    one = sum(1 for p, q, o, e, s in detail if e >= 1)
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    nulls = {True: [], False: []}
    nulls_g = {True: [], False: []}
    for _ in range(TURNS):
        for within in (True, False):
            pages2 = shuffled(pages, rng, within)
            nulls[within].append(measure(pages2)[0])
            nulls_g[within].append(measure(pages2, near=near)[0])
    n_page = [x for x in nulls[False]]
    n_ring = [x for x in nulls[True]]
    p_page = (sum(1 for x in n_page if x >= obs_best) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    p_ring = (sum(1 for x in n_ring if x >= obs_best) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    print(f"{tl}: pages={len(pages)} labels={sum(sizes)} sizes={sizes}")
    print(f"   same position, no offset: {obs_same} in {cmp_} comparisons ({100 * obs_same / cmp_:.2f}%)")
    print(f"   best cyclic offset: {obs_best}; null whole-page mean {sum(n_page) / TURNS:.1f} (p={p_page:.3f}); "
          f"null within-ring mean {sum(n_ring) / TURNS:.1f} (p={p_ring:.3f})", flush=True)
    gp = (sum(1 for x in nulls_g[False] if x >= obs_best_g) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    gr = (sum(1 for x in nulls_g[True] if x >= obs_best_g) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
    print(f"   best cyclic offset, one glyph allowed: {obs_best_g}; null whole-page mean {sum(nulls_g[False]) / TURNS:.1f} (p={gp:.3f}); "
          f"null within-ring mean {sum(nulls_g[True]) / TURNS:.1f} (p={gr:.3f}); same position {obs_same_g}", flush=True)
    topg = sorted(detail_g, key=lambda d: -d[3])[:4]
    print("   one-glyph pairs carrying the most agreements:", ", ".join(f"{a}+{b} offset {o}: {e}" for a, b, o, e, _s in topg), flush=True)
    top = sorted(detail, key=lambda d: -d[3])[:4]
    print("   pairs carrying the most agreements:", ", ".join(f"{a}+{b} offset {o}: {e}" for a, b, o, e, _s in top), flush=True)
