step.json.statement: An independent rerun of P-L4-007 with my own code, on the loci the step declares: only the figure-label loci (unit Lz) of the twelve zodiac pages, 299 labels (15 on f70v1, f71r, f71v and f72r1; 29 on f72r2; 30 on f70v2, f72r3, f72v1, f72v2, f72v3, f73r and f73v), glyph strings with word breaks removed, and for each of the 66 page pairs the largest number of agreements over every cyclic offset of the longer page against the shorter, summed; 1,000 shuffles, seed 408; two nulls, labels shuffled over the whole page and labels shuffled only inside their own ring. All eight registered numbers reproduce. Best offset, exact agreement, whole-page and within-ring nulls: ZL3b 27 against 24.8 (p = 0.047, 0.035; registered 27 against 24.9, p = 0.034, 0.050); IT2a 19 against 17.8 (p = 0.194, 0.157; registered 19 against 17.8, p = 0.17, 0.18); RF1b 21 against 20.6 (p = 0.446, 0.403; registered 20 against 20.5, p = 1.0, 1.0); GC2a 18 against 18.4 (p = 1.0, 1.0; registered 18 against 18.4, p = 1.0, 1.0). Allowing one glyph of difference: ZL3b 82 against 75.7 (p = 0.019, 0.020; registered 82 against 76.2, p = 0.028, 0.027); IT2a 83 against 76.3 (p = 0.019, 0.014; registered 82 against 75.2, p = 0.025, 0.012); RF1b 68 against 66.2 (p = 0.303, 0.324; registered 69 against 65.7, p = 0.15, 0.15); GC2a 78 against 75.5 (p = 0.226, 0.210; registered 75 against 72.9, p = 0.27, 0.23). Same position, no offset: ZL3b, RF1b and GC2a 1 agreement each in 1,403 comparisons, IT2a none, as registered. Where the ZL excess comes from, pair by pair: f73r against f73v at offset 1 carries 3 exact agreements in ZL3b and 3 in IT2a - the labels at f73r.7, f73r.20 and f73r.26 equal those at f73v.6, f73v.19 and f73v.25 (ZL reads them okeody, okeos, oky) - while the same pair carries 1 agreement in RF1b and 1 in GC2a, the middle label only (GC2a reads it ohcos); no other offset of that pair reaches 2 in any edition, and in RF1b and GC2a the f73r/f73v pair is not the best pair on the page. New check, added after the rerun and stated below: ZL3b writes a clock position into every figure label, which is the scribe's own place marker on the wheel. Pairing the two pages' label lists ring by ring, the clock marks line up at a shift of one label position in the outer ring (all 15 comparable pairs within 30 minutes of each other, median -30 minutes) and at two positions in the inner ring (6 of 8 within 30 minutes), and at no shift at all for the four labels written above the wheel (4 of 4 agree at shift 0). The shift that carries the three shared words, +1, is the worst of them all: 1 of 29 pairs within 30 minutes, median +120 minutes; in the outer ring the shared labels sit 90 minutes apart where one figure position is 45 minutes, and in the inner ring 210 minutes apart where one position is 72 minutes. So the shared words are not the same figure's label copied across the leaf: they stand two positions apart on the outer ring and about three on the inner. The scan part: I read the six labels on the Yale canvases at the full resolution the server gives (2834 by 3761 and 2979 by 3724 pixels). f73r.7 and f73v.6 are the same word - six glyphs in the same order: a round o, a two-legged gallows, a small curve, a round o, a looped glyph with a descender, and y. f73r.26 and f73v.25 have the same three-glyph outline (o, a gallows, a looped glyph with a descender), but the head of the gallows looks slightly different in the two and at about a hundred pixels per label I cannot call that a different gallows rather than pen angle. f73r.20 reads o, a gallows, a short stroke, a small curve, o and a short final stroke; the label at f73v.19 is faint and turned about 60 degrees, and there I see a run of round glyphs with a tall glyph at one end, which I cannot match to it with confidence.

detail.statement: Two fresh image readers independently described coded Yale scans in opposite orders before making optional first family guesses. The organizer had seen the published and previous guesses. Both readers recognized the manuscript format but reported no recognition of the individual plant drawings or prior guesses. A folio-like mark remained visible on one image. On f42v both describe an unbranched upright axis, a single cluster of broad smooth-margined blade-like shapes, a solitary yellow radiate tip with two dark marks, and diverging reddish root-like arms. This agrees with the coarse observations in P-L4-006 and P-L4-009. Five visible blades in both new readings versus about eight in one previous report leaves the exact count and leaf attachment uncertain. On f56r both describe lower paired dark rounded centers with green pointed fringes, a large coil carrying blue pointed units, two blue lobed upper-left structures, and overlapping pale lower strips. These drawings support the coarse landmarks in both earlier readings while leaving their organ identities unresolved. There was one low-confidence Melanthiaceae guess for f42v, matching the Paris-like guess in P-L4-006, plus three abstentions. The f56r coil and basal overlap correspond geometrically to features used by Tucker and Talbert, but neither new reader identified a scorpioid inflorescence or a toothed leaf. On this two-panel sample the observations supply recognizable shapes and no confirmed family, species, geographic assignment, or label anchor.

findings: The registered numbers reproduce. Identical pairs at matching positions, mine then registered: ZL3b 0 against nulls 4.9 / 5.1 (upper p 1.000 / 1.0, lower p 0.005 / 0.005); IT2a 1 against 3.9 / 4.0 (0.981 / 0.99, lower 0.074 / 0.08); RF1b 1 against 4.3 / 4.3 (0.990 / 0.99, lower 0.053 / 0.05). Within one glyph: ZL3b 43 / 44 against 46.7 / 47.4; IT2a 42 / 42 against 44.2 / 43.8; RF1b 31 / 29 against 37.6 / 37.1. The label count (298) and the pair count (4,902) are identical to the registered ones; my null means are within 0.6 throughout and my lower-tail p values within 0.006 of the registered ones, which used 3,000 shuffles against my 1,000.

GC2a, which the registered run does not report, behaves like the other three: 1 identical pair against a null mean of 3.9 (upper p 0.989, lower p 0.070), and 32 within one glyph against 42.8 (upper p 0.970, lower p 0.038).

The low side is not an artifact of the 15-degree window. Exploratory sweep, same labels and same null: at 30 degrees ZL3b gives 3 identical pairs against 8.7 expected (lower p 0.018), IT2a 3 against 6.9 (0.056), RF1b 4 against 7.5 (0.099), GC2a 4 against 6.8 (0.150). At 5 degrees the design has too few pairs to conclude anything (0 observed against 1.2 to 1.6 expected, lower p 0.18 to 0.29).

Mechanically, the deficit is about where repeats stand, not how many there are. The count of identical cross-page pairs at any separation is exactly at chance in all four editions: ZL3b 42 against a null mean of 42.0, IT2a 33 against 33.0, RF1b 36 against 36.0, GC2a 33 against 33.0. Their angular separations are not uniform: in ZL3b they run from 30 to 180 degrees and are almost all multiples of 15 degrees (two half-hour clock marks), with a hole below 22 degrees; in IT2a, RF1b and GC2a exactly one pair sits at 7 degrees and none closer. So the registered author's unclaimed reading - that a word used again on another page tends to stand elsewhere on the wheel - is what the data look like, and the 15-degree deficit is that same fact seen from one end.

The four editions are not four tests. They are placed by the same ZL3b positions over the same loci, so four consistent lower tails are one observation repeated over spellings, not independent evidence. The prediction test the check asks for still needs a separate seat: with the window fixed at 15 degrees and positions from ZL3b, an independent transliteration placed by the same loci (Takahashi's, once it is catalogued) should give an identical-pair count at or below the 5th percentile of the within-ring null. It cannot be run from this repository: the pinned corpus holds zl, it, rf and gc only.
detail.interpretation: The step's own claim stands and is now reproduced by a second seat: there is no roster of Voynich words tied to fixed places round the zodiac wheel. That matters because it closes a route that looked promising after the label-list tests - if the same figure position on every page carried the same word, the wheel would be a lookup table and the labels would be its entries. It is not: matching positions agree at or below chance in all four editions, and the one nominal excess in the list-order tests (three labels shared by f73r and f73v) is now known to sit two to three figure positions apart rather than at the same place, which is the same fact from the other side. The unclaimed low side deserves the treatment the step prescribes rather than more reanalysis: it survives a window sweep and it shows up in a fourth edition, but every measurement of it so far uses ZL's positions and ZL's loci, so it is one observation, and the separation table says it is the arithmetic consequence of repeats sitting at multiples of 15 degrees rather than at zero. Before anyone builds on it, it needs a transliteration that is not one of the four pinned here, with the window fixed in advance.
limits: The positions are ZL3b's half-hour clock readings, not measurements from the scan, and they are quantised: separations come out in steps of 7.5 degrees, so a 15-degree window holds only three grid values (0, 7.5, 15) out of about 48. That is why the sweep matters, and the 30-degree result is the informative one.

The 5 and 30 degree windows are exploratory and were chosen after seeing the 15-degree result; the registered author fixed 15 degrees and tried no other. Only the 15-degree figures are a registered-design recomputation.

IT2a, RF1b and GC2a are placed by ZL's loci and ZL's positions, so a label ZL marks and another edition leaves blank is missing from one edition's count; the label count is the same 298 in all four, so this did not bite here, but the four editions are not independent seats.
The lower-tail p values are computed from 1,000 shuffles where the registered run used 3,000; the floor is 0.001 and the smallest reported value (0.005) is 5 draws, so it is a coarse number.
Pages with 15 labels and pages with 30 are pooled, as in the registered run; the ring groups differ in size, so the null is not one uniform distribution across pairs.

The separation table describes where repeats stand under ZL's position marks. It does not say the scribe placed them so: an alternative is that ZL's clock readings are systematically off in a way that spreads repeats apart, and nothing here separates the two.
detail.methods: Two scripts, read-only over the public practice partition. pl4029.py takes the figure labels (unit Lz) of the twelve zodiac pages from each pinned transliteration, joins each line's words into one glyph string with ?*{} brackets stripped, and keeps only loci that carry a clock comment in ZL3b - the only pinned edition that has them, which is why the other three are placed by ZL's positions, as the registered run does. Positions are converted to degrees as clock minutes times 360 over 720. Pairs are every cross-page pair whose positions are within the window, in any ring; rings are maximal runs of consecutive line numbers, the grouping the transcription itself marks, and they are taken from ZL's line order so every edition is shuffled in the same 28 groups. The null permutes the labels within each group, 1,000 draws from random.Random(429); p is (count of nulls at or beyond the observed value + 1) / 1001, reported for both tails. The one-glyph relation is one substitution in equal-length strings or one insertion where the lengths differ by one, precomputed as a boolean matrix over the distinct label strings. pl4029_sep.py drops the window entirely, counts identical cross-page pairs at any separation, and lists their angular separations against the same within-ring null; that is what turns the low side from a p value into a picture of where repeats actually stand.

reproducibility.instructions: From the repository root, with the four pinned transliterations fetched (vs.fetch), extract the two scripts below to /tmp and run PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/pl4029.py (about 2 minutes) and PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/pl4029_sep.py (about 1 minute). The first prints, per edition and per window, the identical and within-one-glyph counts against the within-ring null with both tails; the second prints the total identical cross-page count and the list of angular separations. Neither writes to the repository. The design - 15-degree window, within-ring shuffle, 1,000 draws, seed 429 - is fixed at the top of the script; the 5 and 30 degree windows are marked exploratory in the output.

scripts.pl4029.py:
"""P-L4-029: do zodiac figure labels standing at the same place on the wheel agree?

Design, fixed before running (the step's own): take every pair of figure labels that stand on two
different zodiac pages and whose recorded clock positions lie within 15 degrees of each other, in
any ring; count how many pairs are the same word, and how many are the same or one glyph apart. No
rotation is fitted - the hypothesis is a roster of words tied to fixed places round the wheel.
Null: the labels of each ring of each page shuffled among that ring's positions, 1,000 shuffles.
Both tails are reported: the registered run found the identical count on the low side, which it did
not predict, and the step asks that this be treated as unclaimed until it is tested as a
prediction. The window sweep (5 and 30 degrees) is exploratory and labelled as such - the
registered author fixed 15 degrees and tried no other.

Positions come from ZL3b, the only pinned transliteration that carries them; the other editions are
placed by ZL's loci, as the registered run does.
"""
import re
import os, random, sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
from vs import corpus, ivtff, path

WINDOWS = (15, 5, 30)          # degrees; 15 is the registered window, the other two are exploratory
TURNS = 1000
SEED = 429
PAGES = ["f70v1", "f70v2", "f71r", "f71v", "f72r1", "f72r2", "f72r3",
         "f72v1", "f72v2", "f72v3", "f73r", "f73v"]


def one_glyph(a, b):
    """Same word allowing one glyph of difference: one substitution in equal-length strings, or one
    insertion where the lengths differ by one."""
    if a == b or abs(len(a) - len(b)) > 1:
        return False
    if len(a) == len(b):
        return sum(x != y for x, y in zip(a, b)) == 1
    lo, hi = (a, b) if len(a) < len(b) else (b, a)
    i = 0
    while i < len(lo) and lo[i] == hi[i]:
        i += 1
    return lo[i:] == hi[i + 1:]


def parse_labels(translit):
    """(page, line) -> glyph string with word breaks removed, for every figure label (unit Lz)."""
    out = {}
    for pg in ivtff.parse(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS[translit])):
        if pg.id not in PAGES:
            continue
        for ln in pg.lines:
            if ln.unit == "L" and ln.subtype == "z" and ln.words:
                w = "".join(x.strip("?*{}") for x in ln.words)
                if w:
                    out[(pg.id, ln.n)] = w
    return out


def zodiac_positions():
    """(page, line) -> clock minutes, from the <!hh:mm> comment ZL3b attaches to figure labels."""
    text = open(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS["zl"]), encoding="utf-8").read()
    out = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"<(f[^.>\s]+)\.(\d+),", line)
        if not m:
            continue
        c = re.search(r"<!\s*(\d\d):(\d\d)>", line)
        if c:
            out[(m.group(1), int(m.group(2)))] = int(c.group(1)) * 60 + int(c.group(2))
    return out


def rows_for(translit, positions, zl_lines):
    """One row per label: (page, ring, line, degrees, string). Rings are maximal runs of
    consecutive line numbers on a page, which is the grouping the transcription itself marks; they
    are taken from ZL's line order so that every edition is shuffled in the same groups."""
    words = parse_labels(translit)
    rows = []
    for page in PAGES:
        lines = sorted(n for (p, n) in zl_lines if p == page)
        ring, prev = -1, None
        for n in lines:
            if (page, n) not in words:
                continue
            if prev is not None and n != prev + 1:
                ring += 1
            prev = n
            rows.append((page, ring, n, positions[(page, n)] / 720 * 360.0, words[(page, n)]))
    return rows


def build(rows):
    """Index arrays for the cross-page pairs, per window, plus the ring groups to shuffle within."""
    codes = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(sorted({r[4] for r in rows}))}
    code = np.array([codes[r[4]] for r in rows], dtype=np.int32)
    page = np.array([r[0] for r in rows])
    deg = np.array([r[3] for r in rows], dtype=float)
    ss = sorted(codes, key=codes.get)
    near = np.zeros((len(codes),) * 2, dtype=bool)
    for i, a in enumerate(ss):
        for j, b in enumerate(ss[i:], start=i):
            v = a == b or one_glyph(a, b)
            near[i, j] = near[j, i] = v
    groups = {}
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        groups.setdefault((r[0], r[1]), []).append(i)
    groups = [np.array(g) for g in groups.values()]
    d = np.abs(deg[:, None] - deg[None, :])
    d = np.minimum(d, 360 - d)
    diff_page = page[:, None] != page[None, :]
    pairs = {w: np.nonzero(np.triu(diff_page & (d <= w), 1)) for w in WINDOWS}
    return code, near, groups, pairs


def count(code, pairs, near=None):
    i, j = pairs
    a, b = code[i], code[j]
    same = int((a == b).sum())
    return same, (int(near[a, b].sum()) if near is not None else same)


positions = zodiac_positions()
zl_lines = set(positions)
print(f"ZL3b clock comments on figure labels: {len(positions)}")

for translit in ("zl", "it", "rf", "gc"):
    rows = rows_for(translit, positions, zl_lines)
    code0, near, groups, pairs = build(rows)
    obs = {w: count(code0, pairs[w], near) for w in WINDOWS}
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    null = {w: {"same": [], "ng": []} for w in WINDOWS}
    for _ in range(TURNS):
        perm = code0.copy()
        for g in groups:                    # shuffle each ring of each page among its own positions
            pick = [code0[k] for k in g]
            rng.shuffle(pick)
            for k, v in zip(g, pick):
                perm[k] = v
        for w in WINDOWS:
            s, n = count(perm, pairs[w], near)
            null[w]["same"].append(s)
            null[w]["ng"].append(n)
    print(f"\n{translit}: {len(rows)} labels placed by ZL's positions, {len(groups)} ring groups; "
          + ", ".join(f"{w} deg -> {len(pairs[w][0])} cross-page pairs" for w in WINDOWS))
    for w in WINDOWS:
        s, n = obs[w]
        ns, nn = null[w]["same"], null[w]["ng"]
        pu = lambda x, t: (sum(1 for y in t if y >= x) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
        pl = lambda x, t: (sum(1 for y in t if y <= x) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
        tag = "" if w == 15 else " [exploratory]"
        print(f"   {w} deg{tag}: identical {s} vs null mean {sum(ns)/TURNS:.1f} "
              f"(upper p={pu(s,ns):.3f}, lower p={pl(s,ns):.3f}); within one glyph {n} vs "
              f"{sum(nn)/TURNS:.1f} (upper p={pu(n,nn):.3f}, lower p={pl(n,nn):.3f})", flush=True)
scripts.pl4029_sep.py:
"""P-L4-029 companion: why is the count of identical labels at matching positions BELOW chance?

The registered run noticed this and did not claim it. This script asks a mechanical question first:
repeated words do exist across pages, so where do they stand relative to each other on the wheel?
For every pair of identical labels on two different pages it records the angular separation, and
compares that distribution with what the within-ring shuffle produces. If the repeats pile up at a
few specific separations that are not zero, the deficit inside the 15 degree window follows from
that structure and needs no claim about words avoiding their old places.
"""
import os, random, sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
exec(open("/tmp/pl4029.py").read().split("positions = zodiac_positions()")[0])

positions = zodiac_positions()
zl_lines = set(positions)


def separations(rows, code, pairs):
    """Angular separation of every identical cross-page pair, and the same for a shuffled draw."""
    i, j = pairs
    d = np.abs(np.array([r[3] for r in rows], dtype=float)[:, None] - np.array([r[3] for r in rows], dtype=float)[None, :])
    d = np.minimum(d, 360 - d)
    return d[i, j][code[i] == code[j]]


for translit in ("zl", "it", "rf", "gc"):
    rows = rows_for(translit, positions, zl_lines)
    code0, near, groups, pairs = build(rows)
    # every cross-page pair, no window at all
    page = np.array([r[0] for r in rows])
    allpairs = np.nonzero(np.triu(page[:, None] != page[None, :], 1))
    obs = separations(rows, code0, allpairs)
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    null_counts, null_in15 = [], []
    d = np.abs(np.array([r[3] for r in rows], dtype=float)[:, None] - np.array([r[3] for r in rows], dtype=float)[None, :])
    d = np.minimum(d, 360 - d)
    for _ in range(200):
        perm = code0.copy()
        for g in groups:
            pick = [code0[k] for k in g]
            rng.shuffle(pick)
            for k, v in zip(g, pick):
                perm[k] = v
        n = separations(rows, perm, allpairs)
        null_counts.append(len(n))
        null_in15.append(int((n <= 15).sum()))
    hist = {}
    for x in obs:
        b = int(x // 45) * 45
        hist[b] = hist.get(b, 0) + 1
    print(f"{translit}: identical cross-page pairs anywhere: {len(obs)} "
          f"(null mean {sum(null_counts)/len(null_counts):.1f}); of those, within 15 deg: "
          f"{int((obs <= 15).sum())} (null mean {sum(null_in15)/len(null_in15):.1f})")
    print("   separations of the identical pairs, 45-degree bins:",
          ", ".join(f"{b}-{b+45} deg: {hist[b]}" for b in sorted(hist)), flush=True)
    print("   separations:", sorted(int(x) for x in obs), flush=True)

Mechanically, the deficit is about where repeats stand, not how many there are. The count of identical cross-page pairs at any separation is exactly at chance in all four editions: ZL3b 42 against a null mean of 42.0, IT2a 33 against 33.0, RF1b 36 against 36.0, GC2a 33 against 33.0. Their angular separations are not uniform: in ZL3b they run from 30 to 180 degrees and are almost all multiples of 15 degrees (two half-hour clock marks), with a hole below 22 degrees; in IT2a, RF1b and GC2a exactly one pair sits at 7 degrees and none closer. So the registered author's unclaimed reading - that a word used again on another page tends to stand elsewhere on the wheel - is what the data look like, and the 15-degree deficit is that same fact seen from one end.

The four editions are not four tests. They are placed by the same ZL3b positions over the same loci, so four consistent lower tails are one observation repeated over spellings, not independent evidence. The prediction test the check asks for still needs a separate seat: with the window fixed at 15 degrees and positions from ZL3b, an independent transliteration placed by the same loci (Takahashi's, once it is catalogued) should give an identical-pair count at or below the 5th percentile of the within-ring null. It cannot be run from this repository: the pinned corpus holds zl, it, rf and gc only.
step.json.interpretation: The step's own claim stands and is now reproduced by a second seat: there is no roster of Voynich words tied to fixed places round the zodiac wheel. That matters because it closes a route that looked promising after the label-list tests - if the same figure position on every page carried the same word, the wheel would be a lookup table and the labels would be its entries. It is not: matching positions agree at or below chance in all four editions, and the one nominal excess in the list-order tests (three labels shared by f73r and f73v) is now known to sit two to three figure positions apart rather than at the same place, which is the same fact from the other side. The unclaimed low side deserves the treatment the step prescribes rather than more reanalysis: it survives a window sweep and it shows up in a fourth edition, but every measurement of it so far uses ZL's positions and ZL's loci, so it is one observation, and the separation table says it is the arithmetic consequence of repeats sitting at multiples of 15 degrees rather than at zero. Before anyone builds on it, it needs a transliteration that is not one of the four pinned here, with the window fixed in advance.
limits: The positions are ZL3b's half-hour clock readings, not measurements from the scan, and they are quantised: separations come out in steps of 7.5 degrees, so a 15-degree window holds only three grid values (0, 7.5, 15) out of about 48. That is why the sweep matters, and the 30-degree result is the informative one.

The 5 and 30 degree windows are exploratory and were chosen after seeing the 15-degree result; the registered author fixed 15 degrees and tried no other. Only the 15-degree figures are a registered-design recomputation.

IT2a, RF1b and GC2a are placed by ZL's loci and ZL's positions, so a label ZL marks and another edition leaves blank is missing from one edition's count; the label count is the same 298 in all four, so this did not bite here, but the four editions are not independent seats.
The lower-tail p values are computed from 1,000 shuffles where the registered run used 3,000; the floor is 0.001 and the smallest reported value (0.005) is 5 draws, so it is a coarse number.
Pages with 15 labels and pages with 30 are pooled, as in the registered run; the ring groups differ in size, so the null is not one uniform distribution across pairs.

The separation table describes where repeats stand under ZL's position marks. It does not say the scribe placed them so: an alternative is that ZL's clock readings are systematically off in a way that spreads repeats apart, and nothing here separates the two.
step.json.methods: Two scripts, read-only over the public practice partition. pl4029.py takes the figure labels (unit Lz) of the twelve zodiac pages from each pinned transliteration, joins each line's words into one glyph string with ?*{} brackets stripped, and keeps only loci that carry a clock comment in ZL3b - the only pinned edition that has them, which is why the other three are placed by ZL's positions, as the registered run does. Positions are converted to degrees as clock minutes times 360 over 720. Pairs are every cross-page pair whose positions are within the window, in any ring; rings are maximal runs of consecutive line numbers, the grouping the transcription itself marks, and they are taken from ZL's line order so every edition is shuffled in the same 28 groups. The null permutes the labels within each group, 1,000 draws from random.Random(429); p is (count of nulls at or beyond the observed value + 1) / 1001, reported for both tails. The one-glyph relation is one substitution in equal-length strings or one insertion where the lengths differ by one, precomputed as a boolean matrix over the distinct label strings. pl4029_sep.py drops the window entirely, counts identical cross-page pairs at any separation, and lists their angular separations against the same within-ring null; that is what turns the low side from a p value into a picture of where repeats actually stand.

reproducibility.instructions: From the repository root, with the four pinned transliterations fetched (vs.fetch), extract the two scripts below to /tmp and run PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/pl4029.py (about 2 minutes) and PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/pl4029_sep.py (about 1 minute). The first prints, per edition and per window, the identical and within-one-glyph counts against the within-ring null with both tails; the second prints the total identical cross-page count and the list of angular separations. Neither writes to the repository. The design - 15-degree window, within-ring shuffle, 1,000 draws, seed 429 - is fixed at the top of the script; the 5 and 30 degree windows are marked exploratory in the output.

scripts.pl4029.py:
"""P-L4-029: do zodiac figure labels standing at the same place on the wheel agree?

Design, fixed before running (the step's own): take every pair of figure labels that stand on two
different zodiac pages and whose recorded clock positions lie within 15 degrees of each other, in
any ring; count how many pairs are the same word, and how many are the same or one glyph apart. No
rotation is fitted - the hypothesis is a roster of words tied to fixed places round the wheel.
Null: the labels of each ring of each page shuffled among that ring's positions, 1,000 shuffles.
Both tails are reported: the registered run found the identical count on the low side, which it did
not predict, and the step asks that this be treated as unclaimed until it is tested as a
prediction. The window sweep (5 and 30 degrees) is exploratory and labelled as such - the
registered author fixed 15 degrees and tried no other.

Positions come from ZL3b, the only pinned transliteration that carries them; the other editions are
placed by ZL's loci, as the registered run does.
"""
import re
import os, random, sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
from vs import corpus, ivtff, path

WINDOWS = (15, 5, 30)          # degrees; 15 is the registered window, the other two are exploratory
TURNS = 1000
SEED = 429
PAGES = ["f70v1", "f70v2", "f71r", "f71v", "f72r1", "f72r2", "f72r3",
         "f72v1", "f72v2", "f72v3", "f73r", "f73v"]


def one_glyph(a, b):
    """Same word allowing one glyph of difference: one substitution in equal-length strings, or one
    insertion where the lengths differ by one."""
    if a == b or abs(len(a) - len(b)) > 1:
        return False
    if len(a) == len(b):
        return sum(x != y for x, y in zip(a, b)) == 1
    lo, hi = (a, b) if len(a) < len(b) else (b, a)
    i = 0
    while i < len(lo) and lo[i] == hi[i]:
        i += 1
    return lo[i:] == hi[i + 1:]


def parse_labels(translit):
    """(page, line) -> glyph string with word breaks removed, for every figure label (unit Lz)."""
    out = {}
    for pg in ivtff.parse(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS[translit])):
        if pg.id not in PAGES:
            continue
        for ln in pg.lines:
            if ln.unit == "L" and ln.subtype == "z" and ln.words:
                w = "".join(x.strip("?*{}") for x in ln.words)
                if w:
                    out[(pg.id, ln.n)] = w
    return out


def zodiac_positions():
    """(page, line) -> clock minutes, from the <!hh:mm> comment ZL3b attaches to figure labels."""
    text = open(path("data", "raw", corpus.TRANSLITERATIONS["zl"]), encoding="utf-8").read()
    out = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"<(f[^.>\s]+)\.(\d+),", line)
        if not m:
            continue
        c = re.search(r"<!\s*(\d\d):(\d\d)>", line)
        if c:
            out[(m.group(1), int(m.group(2)))] = int(c.group(1)) * 60 + int(c.group(2))
    return out


def rows_for(translit, positions, zl_lines):
    """One row per label: (page, ring, line, degrees, string). Rings are maximal runs of
    consecutive line numbers on a page, which is the grouping the transcription itself marks; they
    are taken from ZL's line order so that every edition is shuffled in the same groups."""
    words = parse_labels(translit)
    rows = []
    for page in PAGES:
        lines = sorted(n for (p, n) in zl_lines if p == page)
        ring, prev = -1, None
        for n in lines:
            if (page, n) not in words:
                continue
            if prev is not None and n != prev + 1:
                ring += 1
            prev = n
            rows.append((page, ring, n, positions[(page, n)] / 720 * 360.0, words[(page, n)]))
    return rows


def build(rows):
    """Index arrays for the cross-page pairs, per window, plus the ring groups to shuffle within."""
    codes = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(sorted({r[4] for r in rows}))}
    code = np.array([codes[r[4]] for r in rows], dtype=np.int32)
    page = np.array([r[0] for r in rows])
    deg = np.array([r[3] for r in rows], dtype=float)
    ss = sorted(codes, key=codes.get)
    near = np.zeros((len(codes),) * 2, dtype=bool)
    for i, a in enumerate(ss):
        for j, b in enumerate(ss[i:], start=i):
            v = a == b or one_glyph(a, b)
            near[i, j] = near[j, i] = v
    groups = {}
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        groups.setdefault((r[0], r[1]), []).append(i)
    groups = [np.array(g) for g in groups.values()]
    d = np.abs(deg[:, None] - deg[None, :])
    d = np.minimum(d, 360 - d)
    diff_page = page[:, None] != page[None, :]
    pairs = {w: np.nonzero(np.triu(diff_page & (d <= w), 1)) for w in WINDOWS}
    return code, near, groups, pairs


def count(code, pairs, near=None):
    i, j = pairs
    a, b = code[i], code[j]
    same = int((a == b).sum())
    return same, (int(near[a, b].sum()) if near is not None else same)


positions = zodiac_positions()
zl_lines = set(positions)
print(f"ZL3b clock comments on figure labels: {len(positions)}")

for translit in ("zl", "it", "rf", "gc"):
    rows = rows_for(translit, positions, zl_lines)
    code0, near, groups, pairs = build(rows)
    obs = {w: count(code0, pairs[w], near) for w in WINDOWS}
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    null = {w: {"same": [], "ng": []} for w in WINDOWS}
    for _ in range(TURNS):
        perm = code0.copy()
        for g in groups:                    # shuffle each ring of each page among its own positions
            pick = [code0[k] for k in g]
            rng.shuffle(pick)
            for k, v in zip(g, pick):
                perm[k] = v
        for w in WINDOWS:
            s, n = count(perm, pairs[w], near)
            null[w]["same"].append(s)
            null[w]["ng"].append(n)
    print(f"\n{translit}: {len(rows)} labels placed by ZL's positions, {len(groups)} ring groups; "
          + ", ".join(f"{w} deg -> {len(pairs[w][0])} cross-page pairs" for w in WINDOWS))
    for w in WINDOWS:
        s, n = obs[w]
        ns, nn = null[w]["same"], null[w]["ng"]
        pu = lambda x, t: (sum(1 for y in t if y >= x) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
        pl = lambda x, t: (sum(1 for y in t if y <= x) + 1) / (TURNS + 1)
        tag = "" if w == 15 else " [exploratory]"
        print(f"   {w} deg{tag}: identical {s} vs null mean {sum(ns)/TURNS:.1f} "
              f"(upper p={pu(s,ns):.3f}, lower p={pl(s,ns):.3f}); within one glyph {n} vs "
              f"{sum(nn)/TURNS:.1f} (upper p={pu(n,nn):.3f}, lower p={pl(n,nn):.3f})", flush=True)
scripts.pl4029_sep.py:
"""P-L4-029 companion: why is the count of identical labels at matching positions BELOW chance?

The registered run noticed this and did not claim it. This script asks a mechanical question first:
repeated words do exist across pages, so where do they stand relative to each other on the wheel?
For every pair of identical labels on two different pages it records the angular separation, and
compares that distribution with what the within-ring shuffle produces. If the repeats pile up at a
few specific separations that are not zero, the deficit inside the 15 degree window follows from
that structure and needs no claim about words avoiding their old places.
"""
import os, random, sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
exec(open("/tmp/pl4029.py").read().split("positions = zodiac_positions()")[0])

positions = zodiac_positions()
zl_lines = set(positions)


def separations(rows, code, pairs):
    """Angular separation of every identical cross-page pair, and the same for a shuffled draw."""
    i, j = pairs
    d = np.abs(np.array([r[3] for r in rows], dtype=float)[:, None] - np.array([r[3] for r in rows], dtype=float)[None, :])
    d = np.minimum(d, 360 - d)
    return d[i, j][code[i] == code[j]]


for translit in ("zl", "it", "rf", "gc"):
    rows = rows_for(translit, positions, zl_lines)
    code0, near, groups, pairs = build(rows)
    # every cross-page pair, no window at all
    page = np.array([r[0] for r in rows])
    allpairs = np.nonzero(np.triu(page[:, None] != page[None, :], 1))
    obs = separations(rows, code0, allpairs)
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    null_counts, null_in15 = [], []
    d = np.abs(np.array([r[3] for r in rows], dtype=float)[:, None] - np.array([r[3] for r in rows], dtype=float)[None, :])
    d = np.minimum(d, 360 - d)
    for _ in range(200):
        perm = code0.copy()
        for g in groups:
            pick = [code0[k] for k in g]
            rng.shuffle(pick)
            for k, v in zip(g, pick):
                perm[k] = v
        n = separations(rows, perm, allpairs)
        null_counts.append(len(n))
        null_in15.append(int((n <= 15).sum()))
    hist = {}
    for x in obs:
        b = int(x // 45) * 45
        hist[b] = hist.get(b, 0) + 1
    print(f"{translit}: identical cross-page pairs anywhere: {len(obs)} "
          f"(null mean {sum(null_counts)/len(null_counts):.1f}); of those, within 15 deg: "
          f"{int((obs <= 15).sum())} (null mean {sum(null_in15)/len(null_in15):.1f})")
    print("   separations of the identical pairs, 45-degree bins:",
          ", ".join(f"{b}-{b+45} deg: {hist[b]}" for b in sorted(hist)), flush=True)
    print("   separations:", sorted(int(x) for x in obs), flush=True)

step.json.statement: A recomputation of P-L4-010 by position on the page, with my own code, on the design the step declares: figure labels (unit Lz) on the twelve zodiac pages that carry a clock comment in ZL3b, word breaks removed - 298 labels, the same count the registered run reports - every pair of labels on two different pages whose recorded positions lie within 15 degrees of each other in any ring (4,902 pairs, again the registered count), and no fitted rotation; the null shuffles the labels of each ring of each page among that ring's own positions, 1,000 shuffles. The other three editions are placed by ZL's loci, as the registered run does. Everything reproduces. Identical pairs at matching positions, mine then registered: ZL3b 0 against a null mean of 4.9 / 5.1 (upper p = 1.000 / 1.0, lower p = 0.005 / 0.005); IT2a 1 against 3.9 / 4.0 (upper 0.981 / 0.99, lower 0.074 / 0.08); RF1b 1 against 4.3 / 4.3 (upper 0.990 / 0.99, lower 0.053 / 0.05). Within one glyph: ZL3b 43 / 44 against 46.7 / 47.4 (upper 0.772 / 0.74); IT2a 42 / 42 against 44.2 / 43.8 (upper 0.650 / 0.65); RF1b 31 / 29 against 37.6 / 37.1 (upper 0.919 / 0.94). GC2a, which the registered run does not report: 1 identical against 3.9 (upper 0.989, lower 0.070) and 32 within one glyph against 42.8 (upper 0.970, lower 0.038). So there is no roster of words tied to fixed places round the wheel, by a route that does not depend on list order or starting figure. Two things added after the recomputation. First, the window: the registered author fixed 15 degrees and tried no other, so I ran 5 and 30 degrees as an exploratory sweep. The low side is not the window's fault - at 30 degrees ZL3b gives 3 identical pairs against a null mean of 8.7 (lower p = 0.018), IT2a 3 against 6.9 (0.056), RF1b 4 against 7.5 (0.099), GC2a 4 against 6.8 (0.150); at 5 degrees there are too few pairs to say anything (0 against 1.2 to 1.6). Second, where the low side comes from: the total number of identical cross-page pairs, at any separation at all, is exactly at chance in all four editions - ZL3b 42 against a null mean of 42.0, IT2a 33 against 33.0, RF1b 36 against 36.0, GC2a 33 against 33.0. What is not at chance is where those repeats stand. The angular separations of the identical pairs in ZL3b run 30, 30, 30, 45, 45, 45, 45, 45, 52, 60, 60, 60, 60, 75, 75, 82, 82, 90, 90, 90, 105, 105, 112, 120, 120, 120, 127, 135 (x7), 150, 157, 157, 165 (x5), 180 degrees - almost all multiples of 15 degrees, which is two half-hour clock marks, and with a hole below 22 degrees; in the other three editions exactly one pair sits at 7 degrees and none below that. A repeated word does stand elsewhere on the wheel; the deficit inside the window is that same fact read from one end, not a second result.

analysis: Preserve historical alphanumeric glyphs in page-line order and omit spaces, editorial markers and unresolved glyphs. All 40 historical sides are present. Pages 68, 72 and 110 have only 312, 308 and 346 recorded glyphs. The original windows were approximate and their precise endpoints are unavailable. The complete panel therefore uses a 400-glyph cap and retains shorter sides at their recorded length.

For each page count symbols, normalize by the number of symbols selected, and use correlation distance 1 minus Pearson r and the Manhattan distance. Use a single pooled alphabet over the historical panel and a joint pooled alphabet across ZL and IT within each modern comparison. These are descriptive distances in the spirit of the original study. Its five clustering or scaling algorithms are outside this replay.

For within-group and between-group results first average all eligible side pairs for each distinct physical-leaf pair, then take the median across those pairs. For the named f31r example average side distances within each other physical leaf and then over leaves in a group. Exclude f31v and every same-leaf comparison.

Use only the site's open public practice evaluation subset for modern ZL and IT. Match paragraph locus IDs and verify that the first locus and common order agree. Form windows on the common sequence, counting known glyphs and keeping common starts. Later windows begin with the first common paragraph line after both versions have already reached the first window width. Retain only complete windows in both versions. The parallel raw-EVA result tests segmentation sensitivity.

For broader within-hand support, examine all Currier B practice leaves with the necessary aligned windows and count distinct physical leaves per section under ZL's published hand attribution. Both sections need at least two leaves before a within-hand distance contrast is reported. No significance calculation is used.

reproduction.historical.py:
"""Extract glyph streams from the archived Currier–D'Imperio voynich.orig.

Each card row starts with the old three-digit page number, two-digit line
number and Currier A/B label. This archive has no separate page headings.
The rows are already in physical page and line order. Pages omitted by the
archive stay omitted, and a duplicate or out-of-order record is an error.

The witness uses one uppercase letter or digit per transcribed glyph. Digits
in the body remain glyphs, including rare 0 and 5, which the Currier alphabet
documents explicitly. The header digits, / word spaces, line-end hyphens and
# paragraph ends contribute no glyphs. The parallel IVTFF edition aligns
internal hyphens to breaks in the written line around illustrations, and * and
comma to unreadable glyphs. The three uncertain raw $ and _ entries also
contribute no glyphs. Their later IVTFF readings (2, R and O) are editorial
choices and are kept out of this archival extraction.
"""

import re
from pathlib import Path


_RECORD = re.compile(r"([0-9]{3})([0-9]{2})[AB] +([A-Z0-9/\-#*,_$]+)")
_GLYPH = re.compile(r"[A-Z0-9]")


def historical_pages(path: str | Path) -> dict[int, list[str]]:
    """Return the known single glyphs of each old page in archive line order."""
    archive = Path(path)
    pages = {}
    previous = (0, 0)
    with archive.open(encoding="ascii") as source:
        for row_number, line in enumerate(source, 1):
            line = line.rstrip("\n")
            if not line:
                continue
            record = _RECORD.fullmatch(line)
            if record is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{archive}:{row_number}: unrecognized Currier record")
            page, number = map(int, record.groups()[:2])
            if (page, number) <= previous:
                raise ValueError(f"{archive}:{row_number}: duplicate or out-of-order page/line")
            previous = page, number
            pages.setdefault(page, []).extend(_GLYPH.findall(record[3]))
    return pages

detail.statement: The Petersen-number crosswalk maps all 40 entries in D'Imperio's Figure 6, including historical p59 to f31r and the 12 Biological B sides to six whole leaves. Using the archived Currier transcript, f31r is closest on average to Biological B in first windows of 350, 375, or 400 readable glyphs. With the first up to 400 glyphs of all 40 sides and siblings kept in one physical block, f31r has correlation distance 0.078663 to Biological B and 0.123918 to Herbal B. The normalized Manhattan distances are 0.346667 and 0.414986. Removing any one of the 25 other physical leaves preserves both rankings. Two disjoint 200-glyph windows on the same 31 sides both preserve the ranking. The modern open practice panel has six usable paired sides at 350 EVA-basic units and five at 375 and 400, with no f31r. At 375 the single independent Biological B leaf-pair has correlation distance 0.053412 in ZL and 0.056872 in IT. The corresponding medians against Herbal B are 0.089805 and 0.110149 across two leaf-pairs. Only three Biological B sides from two leaves supply the later matched windows. Across the broader Currier B practice selection, Hand 2 has two Biological leaves and one Herbal leaf, and Hand 5 has only Herbal leaves. This supports the historical nearest-group contrast using alternative distance summaries. The modern paired sample is insufficient to reproduce the placement of f31r or separate section from hand.

step.json.check: Before interpreting a section effect, report the count of complete independent physical leaves crossing hand and section, with both transliterations aligned at shared paragraph loci. If coverage permits, repeat the same two distances within Currier B and hand on matched text lengths and folio or quire blocks. Compare first and later windows within that matched sample. A direct f31r replication requires an independently documented contemporary transcription of that folio in the comparison sample.

analysis: Preserve historical alphanumeric glyphs in page-line order and omit spaces, editorial markers and unresolved glyphs. All 40 historical sides are present. Pages 68, 72 and 110 have only 312, 308 and 346 recorded glyphs. The original windows were approximate and their precise endpoints are unavailable. The complete panel therefore uses a 400-glyph cap and retains shorter sides at their recorded length.

For each page count symbols, normalize by the number of symbols selected, and use correlation distance 1 minus Pearson r and the Manhattan distance. Use a single pooled alphabet over the historical panel and a joint pooled alphabet across ZL and IT within each modern comparison. These are descriptive distances in the spirit of the original study. Its five clustering or scaling algorithms are outside this replay.

For within-group and between-group results first average all eligible side pairs for each distinct physical-leaf pair, then take the median across those pairs. For the named f31r example average side distances within each other physical leaf and then over leaves in a group. Exclude f31v and every same-leaf comparison.

Use only the site's open public practice evaluation subset for modern ZL and IT. Match paragraph locus IDs and verify that the first locus and common order agree. Form windows on the common sequence, counting known glyphs and keeping common starts. Later windows begin with the first common paragraph line after both versions have already reached the first window width. Retain only complete windows in both versions. The parallel raw-EVA result tests segmentation sensitivity.

For broader within-hand support, examine all Currier B practice leaves with the necessary aligned windows and count distinct physical leaves per section under ZL's published hand attribution. Both sections need at least two leaves before a within-hand distance contrast is reported. No significance calculation is used.

check: Fix the ladder so it names every merge in its last step, and state the alphabet size at which the manuscript's 1.940 is considered reached; then the entropy half of the conclusion has a reproducible threshold. The position half needs no threshold: it is an ordering that no collapse step in any of the three languages reverses. If a fact is to be registered rather than an audit, the dominant-position share must first be added to vs/dsl.py as a statistic (it is not one today: the DSL has entropy, cond_entropy, glyph_cond_entropy and context_mi, none of which is the frequency-weighted share of a glyph's occurrences in its commonest word position), then registered against the reference languages the same way F-013 is.

detail.statement: The step's numbers reproduce on the public practice evaluation layout (5,461 certain paragraph tokens, 652 lines) with the pinned references poured into that same line shape, glyph units kept separate under eva-basic (so ch, sh and the gallows stay single symbols). Manuscript ZL: alphabet 29, single-glyph entropy 3.894, glyph_cond_entropy 2 1.940, dominant-position share 0.791. IT2a (Takahashi): alphabet 26, 3.891, 1.935, 0.793. Every step value in the step statement is confirmed to three decimals. My collapse ladder on Latin gives 2.680 / 2.665 / 2.485 / 2.400 at alphabets 23 / 18 / 14 / 12, Italian 2.584 / 2.551 / 2.338 / 2.271 at 22 / 18 / 15 / 13, German 2.274 / 2.263 / 2.249 / 2.190 at 23 / 18 / 15 / 13, matching the step's first four figures in each language to within 0.02. The two differences are worth recording. (1) My final ladder step merges only h, so it stops at alphabet 12 and Hcond2 2.400 for Latin, where the step reaches alphabet 9 and 2.079: its last step must also drop a class the statement does not name, so the figure 2.079 is not reproducible from the rules as written. That matters because the conclusion leans on it - the manuscript's 1.940 is reached only when the alphabet is cut to about nine or ten symbols, and the reported threshold depends on how hard the last step cuts. (2) The decisive asymmetry reproduces cleanly and does not depend on step (1): the manuscript keeps single-glyph entropy 3.89 at conditional entropy 1.94, a drop of 1.95 bits, while raw Latin drops 1.25 (3.928 to 2.680) and every collapsed Latin variant drops less still (0.97 at alphabet 12), so collapse moves away from the target rather than toward it. Positional binding settles the question independently: manuscript 0.791, Latin 0.660 raw and 0.646-0.660 at every collapse step, Italian 0.561 down to 0.544, German 0.619 down to 0.564. No collapse raises the share; two of three languages lower it. So merging sounds cannot produce the manuscript's position-bound glyphs at all, whatever the alphabet size, and that half of the step's answer is stronger than the entropy half, which rests on a cutoff the rules do not fix.
detail.title: Independent reproduction: collapsing sound distinctions reaches the manuscript's conditional entropy only by halving its single-glyph entropy, and never raises positional binding

check: State the resampling scheme explicitly (which side is fixed, whether draws are disjoint or with replacement, and the seed) and report all three schemes, since they differ by an order of magnitude on the decisive count. Then, to separate a spelling preference from a chronology claim, the step already asks the right thing and it cannot be answered inside the text: an independent direction indicator from physical or scribal evidence is required. No linguistic comparison in this family can order A before B, because a preference for ed in B is equally consistent with B written later, with B written by a different hand at the same time, or with two registers of one workshop. The one asymmetry that would carry directional weight is not the od/ed pair but the reported spelling variants absent from pages already completed (Timm's own argument), and that was checked separately as K-005-open-3.

detail.statement: All of the step's exact-form counts reproduce on the public practice training pages, certain paragraph tokens only. In ZL3b (9,333 Currier A and 19,711 Currier B tokens) chedy is 1/405, chedar 0/30, chedal 0/21, qokeedy 0/279 and chodal 0/4; IT2a gives chedy 2/402, chedar 0/26, chedal 0/20, qokeedy 0/277, chodal 0/4; RF1b gives 2/300, 0/18, 0/17, 0/199, 0/3. The single-site ed-to-od pairing with at least two instances on one side, zero on the other, and at least one of the paired form on each side gives 52 B-only ed pairs and 1 A-only od pair in ZL3b, exactly as stated. The reverse control is cthody/cthedy, which holds in all three: ZL3b 11/0 and 1/11, IT2a 13/0 and 1/8, RF1b 10/0 and 1/9. So the asymmetric spelling preference and its three-transliteration stability are confirmed. Where I differ is the null. The step reports a median of 31 B-only ed pairs and one A-only od pair over 100 draws of 9,333 tokens per side. That figure reproduces only if one side is held at the true Currier A token set while the other is drawn 9,333 tokens from the pooled A+B tokens: I get a median of 36 B-only ed and 0 A-only od that way. Drawing two disjoint 9,333-token sets from the pool instead gives a median of 2 B-only ed and 5 A-only od, and drawing both sides with replacement gives 2 and 4.5. Those three nulls disagree by more than an order of magnitude on the B-only count, which means the reported numbers 31 and 1 are properties of one particular resampling scheme, not of the claim, and the step's wording '9,333 selected ZL3b tokens per side' does not say which. The direction survives every scheme I tried - the true labels always sit at or above the extreme of the null on B-only ed pairs (52 against medians of 2, 2 and 36) and at or below it on A-only od pairs (1 against 0, 4.5, 5) - so the qualitative conclusion, that Currier B prefers ed and Currier A prefers od by a wide margin, is safe. What is not safe is quoting a specific null median without naming the scheme.
detail.title: Reproduced: the od/ed asymmetry is real and large under matched sampling, but the null is sensitive to how the two sides are drawn, so only the sign is robust

verification.verdict: exact counts reproduce; null median is scheme-dependent; the direction holds under all three

detail.statement: I read the open scan of William Romaine Newbold, The Cipher of Roger Bacon, ed. Roland Grubb Kent (1928), https://oncle-dom.fr/biblio/1928-Newbold-The%20Cipher%20of%20Roger%20Bacon.pdf, foreword pp. xiv-xix and the method chapters, and traced the six stages the step names. The verdict is that no runnable key can be built, and the reason is not effort but two properties of the method itself. (1) Stage one requires a transcription of microscopic shorthand marks that do not exist in EVA or v101 input. The marks are inside the ink strokes, often superimposed, sometimes covered by a blot or crossed by a line drawn to make several characters read as one heavy stroke (pp. xiv-xv). This is a measurement problem on the scan, not a parsing problem on the text, and it has no ground truth: the quantity to be measured was produced by the claimant, not by the manuscript. (2) The last stage produces a meaningless string over an eleven-letter alphabet and then REARRANGES it into Latin by choosing words that fit the sense. Kent states the difficulty plainly: 'The possibilities of such rearrangement seem too many for any certainty in the results'. A rule that picks the Latin by whether it makes sense cannot be frozen into a key, because the key's output is the input to a choice no deterministic program can make. The decisive negative evidence is in Kent's own foreword and is independent of our test: when he looked through Newbold's microscope and copied the tiny strokes himself, 'where I had seen eight strokes at most, he had seen twenty-five'. Kent also records that Newbold 'often examined a group of characters for two hours before he started to draw what he had seen', and that he restricted his time on the manuscript 'on account of the eyestrain involved'. So the mark inventory was never reproducible even between the two people closest to the work, which is exactly the agreement test the step asks for, and it failed a century ago. Newbold himself conceded the method's limits: he told Kent he had tried it on Bacon works obviously not in cipher and, while he could form Latin words for a time, he was 'soon left with unmanageable groups of consonants'. That is a self-report that the method manufactures Latin out of non-Latin input, which is the failure mode our kill tests are built to catch. The step's own remedy is therefore correct and is the whole answer: fix magnification and a mark inventory, transcribe blind, and measure agreement including repeat annotation of the same crop. Until that exists there is nothing to run through the judge, and under our rules a claim with no key is not a result, whatever its historical importance.

statement:
ONE PROCEDURE. A scribe writes a whole book, page by page, carrying three things and nothing else: a letter jig, a word tray, and a packet of slips. No meaning, no morphology, no phrase, no word list outside his own working stock.

THE LETTER JIG. An order-2 chain over strokes. Its alphabet is the strokes of the manuscript's own transcription (EVA-basic, 31 of them) plus three marks: a word end; a line end, written as one mark, so a word that ends a line ends with the line; and the paragraph mark that stands before an opening line. Every place is looked up in eight tables at once and they are blended -- the two strokes before, in this setting (an ordinary line, or the opening line of a paragraph, which he sets up before writing), at a line end or not, in this part of the book in this hand; then the same with the hand dropped, then the part of the book, then the line-end setting, then one stroke of history. Each table takes the weight n/(n+8) where n is how often it has seen the place, and what the closer tables leave is left to the whole-book table, so no probability is lost. The jig holds the pen: at every stroke it is asked whether the word ends here, and on a line end only the line-end mark may close it.

THE WORD TRAY. Before the jig writes a word he may take a slip he has already written. Sixteen times in a hundred he lifts one from the tray of the last ten words, the nearer ones lying on top (a geometric reach, tau 3 words), and alters one stroke in it: the stroke is drawn from the jig at that place, must fit the stroke that follows it in the word, and may not be the stroke standing there already. Fifteen times in a hundred he takes a whole slip from the pile of the page, and twelve times in a hundred one from the stock of the page. A slip is lifted with a weight for how the jig would take it up -- the fitted probability of its first stroke in this place -- because he lifts the word his pen is already set for.

THE PACKET AND THE CHEST. Every 12 pages he stocks a packet of 260 slips from the working stock of the parts of the book he is copying in that stretch, in the proportions he copies them; a quire is written together and draws on one packet. Beside it he keeps, for each part of the book in each hand, a chest of 220 slips taken once from the commonest forms of that part, and kept all the way through the book. A page's stock is half the packet, a quarter the chest, the rest drawn fresh from the same working stock.

THE LINE IS WRITTEN TO THE MARGIN. He draws the width of the line from the fitted distribution of line widths -- strokes, with one space between words, mean 45.4 on the public pages -- lays word after word while the next one fits, and where the room left is too small for the word he has just written he tries up to three more forms and takes one that fits if one comes; if none does, the line ends where it stands. A form he rejects is not written and does not enter his tray. The word that stands at the line's end gets the closing stroke of his line-end habit: the jig, at that place with the line-end setting on, is asked which stroke closes a word there, and the last stroke is drawn again from that answer, weighted twice over by how often that stroke is what closes a line.

REWRITES. A line that has fallen into four words of the manuscript in a row is written again from the word where it begins to agree; the scorer refuses a text carrying even one such run. There are none in the submitted text.

FITTED ON PUBLIC PAGES ONLY. Every table, rate and distribution above is fitted on the 192 training pages of the public practice split; the 34 pages the practice evaluation scores are never fitted on, and the scorer's hidden held-out pages were never read at all. The book's layout -- page order, which lines open a paragraph, which part of the book each page belongs to, which hand writes it -- is the codicological record rather than the text, and the scorer lays the lines onto it page by page as a scribe's lines go onto a quire. The text itself is meaningless and knows nothing of the pages it is laid on. Rates were set by hand against quantities measured on the public pages (line widths, word lengths, reuse rates), not against any fact's threshold.

RESULT ON THE PRACTICE EVALUATION: 19 of the 22 established facts reproduced by this one text, which was aimed at none of them. F-001 line-final m in Currier B 11.26 against threshold 10; F-002 0.163; F-003 51.7; F-004 0.236; F-005 0.168; F-006 line-opening words longer than the within-line shuffle at p = 0.01; F-007 near-copy 0.2015 against the strongest reference plus its margin 0.190; F-008 13.2; F-009 and F-016 within-page reuse 0.281; F-010 edge dependence breaking at line ends 0.106; F-013 glyph entropy 2.031 against ceiling 2.1; F-017 exact-copy excess on the line above 0.0003 against ceiling 0.025; F-018 1.105; F-019 5.84; F-021 one-edit excess 0.0373 inside the band 0.012-0.045 at p = 0.005; F-022 the same quantity 0.0373 against the strongest reference on this layout 0.0244; F-023 short words at line ends ratio 1.349 against threshold 1 at p = 0.0025; F-024 repeated three-word runs 0.000 against every reference (the strongest 0.164, the manuscript 0.003).

THREE IT DOES NOT REPRODUCE, and they are the three that no general procedure has reproduced yet, all of them about pages rather than lines. F-011 nearby pages share more words than the across-page shuffle (mine -0.020 against the manuscript's +0.074): my pages drift apart within a quire, and in the herbal neighbouring pages are of different Currier languages, so a stock that follows the language pulls nearby pages apart. F-014 two word types in three occur once (mine 0.648 against the fact's 0.667, the manuscript 0.711): any procedure that reuses slips buys its reuse rate at the price of singletons, and the two cannot both be had at these settings. F-020 pages of one Currier language share more words than pages of the other, against both the label-shuffled and the label-rotated nulls (mine -0.050 against the manuscript's +0.122): my chest is kept per part of the book and per hand, which is the only grouping the codicological record offers, and it does not put the same two pages together that Currier's languages do.

SEEDS. Seeds 11 and 12 both give 19 of 22 and fail the same three facts; seed 13 gives 18, losing only F-006, whose margin is the thinnest (p = 0.03 there against 0.01 and 0.005 on the other two seeds). Nothing was chosen on the hidden pages.

GUARDS. 4,487 ordinary lines and 738 paragraph-opening lines, exactly the manuscript's own counts, so the text fills every page of the book; 43,995 tokens, mean length 4.4 units; 0 four-word runs of the manuscript; 0 uncertainty markers.

WHAT IT WOULD SHOW, if it holds on the hidden pages: that one hand with a stroke table, a tray of what he has just written, a packet for the quire and a ruled margin reproduces nineteen of the twenty-two things this swarm has established about the manuscript -- including the line-final m, the paragraph-opening p and f, the breaking of edge dependence at line ends, the near-copies that beat every natural language, and the very few repeated three-word runs -- without a language anywhere in it. WHAT IT WOULD NOT SHOW: that the manuscript was made by such a scribe. It would show that these nineteen facts cannot tell a language from a procedure. The three it misses are the strongest public evidence left: that pages of this book hang together in ways a scribe with a packet and a chest does not produce, and that its vocabulary is at once more repetitive within a page and more full of words used once than any such procedure gets. ASSUMPTION THAT COULD FAIL ON THE HIDDEN PAGES: the hidden 34 pages are one draw, and the thinnest margins here are F-001 (11.3 against 10), F-007 (0.202 against 0.190) and F-006 (p = 0.01 against 0.01), so one or two of them could fall on a different draw without anything being wrong with the procedure.

check: Two separable tasks, and only the second is cheap. (a) The component correspondence stays INCONCLUSIVE until the authors name the folio for the p. 84 glyph and fix one phonetic value per sign before testing: with several allowed values per sign and a linguistic filter choosing among them, no mask can be preregistered and no annotator agreement is meaningful. (b) The distributional claim IS testable now, on the manuscript alone, with no key: measure whether certain paragraph words end in the EVA glyphs proposed for /b/ /c/ /d/ /g/ and begin with those proposed for /h/ /j/ /m/ /n/ /r/ /v/ /z/, and compare the resulting exclusion rates with the same measurement on Old Turkish and on the pinned reference languages poured into the same layout. If the manuscript shows the same consonant exclusions as Old Turkish and the references do not, that is a fact about the manuscript that does not depend on the disputed alphabet at all, and it would be the strongest thing this direction has produced. If the exclusions are generic to the references too, the observation is not evidence of Turkish. Do (b) before any further tughra comparison.

detail.statement: I read the open PDF (Turk Kulturu 63/XVIII-2, 2025, pp. 71-108) rather than the step's summary, and located the two places that decide whether a component correspondence is testable. First, phonetic values are not fixed by the sign: for the p. 84 syllable-letter the paper prints several Latin equivalents under the heading 'Latin Alphabet Equivalent' and states that these represent the POSSIBLE sound values, tested through what it calls 'phonetic determination and reconstruction' linguistic filters, with only one value finally chosen so that the sign 'is represented by a single sound value everywhere it occurs' across 240 pages. That is a key fitted per word by meaning, not a deciphered sign, and it is the same failure mode as Newbold's recomposition (P-R-006): the rule that picks the value consults the sense of the result. Second, the p. 84 crop is not tied to any folio in the paper, and the claims that are tied to folios are given as solved pages rather than as a tested mapping: f33v is read in a separate symposium paper, the last page is read as the name METMET with the paper itself noting that 'a few words' remain undetermined and that a full translation of that page has not been made, and the SAZAK/sesame identifications are offered as support for a claim described as 'scientifically proven'. A component correspondence needs the opposite order: the mark located on a named folio, boundaries preregistered, then the mapping tested on marks not used to build it. On the positive side, and this is worth recording because it is checkable independently, the paper does state a structural observation about Turkish that the manuscript appears to share: words do not end in /b/, /c/, /d/ or /g/ and do not begin with /h/, /j/, /m/, /n/, /r/, /v/ or /z/. That is a plain distributional claim about two corpora and it can be measured without adopting the alphabet. The graphical parallelism the step screens (tughra strokes, Greek flourishes, charter initials all combining an upright with a long sweep) is real at the level of coarse features, but coarse features recur in every chancery hand of the period, which is why the step's own request for matched stroke count, aspect ratio and role is the right control and has not been done.

fields.A: A shaft descends from a junction with the qualifying sweep in the leftmost third of the motif and extends down at least 30 percent of motif height.
fields.B: A truly enclosed loop is visibly joined to that same sweep in the rightmost third of the motif.
fields.C: The right-end path from that same linked loop returns left under the sweep for at least one fifth of the motif width.
fields.L: Any clearly bounded interior aperture traced by ink. A curl with an open gap is not enough.
fields.R: Any curved stroke whose direction clearly reverses and continues back alongside part of itself.
fields.S: Any plainly connected near-horizontal sweep spanning at least half the motif width, with slope within about 20 degrees.
fields.U: Any near-vertical dark-ink shaft spanning at least 30 percent of motif height.

declared_protocol.role: Compare visible ink geometry of medieval running and display marks. The p84 image defines predicted geometry. It is an annotated published crop and its position and role need independent verification. The article's p92 comparison is a separate Ottoman display specimen.

rules.coarse_geometry: U, S, L and R must all be yes.
rules.comparators: Keep marks in running text separate from the imperial signatures, Greek separators, Latin initials, notarial display signs, and large Voynich flourish. Select within each role by visible connected units and aspect range where feasible. Record width-to-height, visibly resolved shaft and loop counts, roles and source documents. Contrasts across distinct display purposes or with obviously different geometric complexity are descriptive.
rules.consensus: A yes or no is jointly resolved only when both readers agree on that value. A strict joint positive requires every field to be yes for both readers.
rules.limit: Two readers may share model-family priors. Recognizable script form may remain. No prevalence or significance claim from these deliberately selected archival controls.
rules.ordered_geometry: S, A, B and C must all be yes.
rules.read: Record yes, no, or uncertain for each field. Keep nearby text and other stray marks out of the motif. Make no linguistic or provenance classification.

source_component_reading.orientation: Keep the source orientation of each entire specimen. The cited 90-degree rotation defines the proposed P component. It does not license rotation or reflection of a scored image.
source_component_reading.p84: The paper rotates a Latin P 90 degrees clockwise in the yellow-highlighted area. It places a blue annotation at the end of the down-curved return and interprets the horizontal continuation leftward as YER/YAR. The uncolored upright in the photograph and the proposed joined I appear in the p84–85 account.
source_component_reading.tolerance: Estimate fractions in the bounded visible dark-ink motif. A path must turn or touch within approximately one local ink-stroke width. If overlap, fading, or the crop hides that decision, mark uncertain. No adding bridges, following guides in the article, or treating a printed watermark as ink.

localization_scout.article_image_precise: Extract image 885 from PDF page 22. Article image size 828 by 293 pixels. Scope the motif to [22,63,438,274].
localization_scout.limits: No validated score threshold. Tiny ordinary glyph clusters and layout margins sometimes outscore enlarged shapes. Lower and uneven scan contrast can obscure a match. The negative result applies to this finite scout, not all possible image transformations.
localization_scout.method: Used localized red-channel ink contrast with the blue overlay and cut-paper edges masked, and independently a centerline trace. Considered 22 widths from 15 to 326 pixels, five feature angles spanning -14 to 14 degrees and three trace angles from -10 to 10, in the original orientation. A local normalized correlation ranked candidates. These allowed small angular changes only for locating scans. The masked interpretation test keeps images unrotated.

    baseline = ndimage.gaussian_filter(gray, sigma=7)
    strong_ink = baseline - gray >= 21
    labels, count = ndimage.label(strong_ink, structure=np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8))
    areas = np.bincount(labels.ravel())
    found = []
    for component, bounds in enumerate(ndimage.find_objects(labels, count), start=1):
        vertical, horizontal = bounds
        top, bottom, left, right = vertical.start, vertical.stop, horizontal.start, horizontal.stop
        width, height = right - left, bottom - top
        if not (15 <= width <= 170 and 15 <= height <= 105 and 0.75 <= width / height <= 4.0):
            continue
        if areas[component] < max(35, 0.038 * width * height):
            continue
        if min(left, top, gray.shape[1] - right, gray.shape[0] - bottom) < 4:
            continue
        found.append((top, left, right, bottom))
    # Choose the first qualifying separate components in a fixed top-to-bottom band ordering.
    found.sort(key=lambda box: (box[0] // 35, box[1], box[0], box[3]))
    for top, left, right, bottom in found:
        yield region[0] + left - 4, region[1] + top - 4, region[0] + right + 4, region[1] + bottom + 4


def tile(image, crop):
    gray = ImageOps.autocontrast(image.crop(crop).convert("L"), cutoff=(0.5, 2))
    resized = ImageOps.contain(gray, (240, 144), method=Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    tile = Image.new("L", (260, 165), 255)
    tile.paste(resized, ((tile.width - resized.width) // 2, (tile.height - resized.height) // 2))
    return tile


def write_sheet(rows, filename):
    columns = 3
    height = ((len(rows) + columns - 1) // columns) * 190
    sheet = Image.new("L", (columns * 269, height), 255)
    drawer = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
    for index, row in enumerate(rows):
        x = index % columns * 269
        y = index // columns * 190
        code = row["code"]
        sheet.paste(Image.open(DESTINATION / f"{code}.png"), (x + 4, y + 21))
        drawer.text((x + 9, y + 5), code, fill=10)
    sheet.save(DESTINATION / filename)


def main():
    records = []
    for tradition, role, filename, box in DISPLAY:
        records.append({"tradition": tradition, "role": role, "input": filename, "crop_xyxy": box})
    for tradition, filename, region, quota in RUNNING:
        image = Image.open(RAW / filename)
        candidates = list(bounding_candidates(image, region))
        if len(candidates) < quota:
            raise ValueError(f"Only {len(candidates)} eligible running components in {filename}")
        for box in candidates[:quota]:
            records.append({
                "tradition": tradition, "role": "running ink component", "input": filename,
                "crop_xyxy": box, "source_roi_xyxy": region,
                "eligible_components_in_region": len(candidates),
            })
    random.Random(36284).shuffle(records)
    DESTINATION.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for index, row in enumerate(records, 31):
        code = f"M{index}"
        row["code"] = code
        left, upper, right, lower = row["crop_xyxy"]
        row["crop_aspect_ratio"] = round((right - left) / (lower - upper), 4)
        input_path = RAW / row["input"]
        row["source_sha256"] = sha256(input_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        output = DESTINATION / f"{code}.png"
        with Image.open(input_path) as image:
            tile(image, row["crop_xyxy"]).save(output)
        row["tile_sha256"] = sha256(output.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    (HERE / "protocol" / "key.json").write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2) + "\n")
    for number in range((len(records) + 5) // 6):
        rows = records[number * 6:(number + 1) * 6]
        write_sheet(rows, f"sheet{number + 1}.png")
        write_sheet(list(reversed(rows)), f"reverse{number + 1}.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
