detail.limitations: The ciphertext vocabulary is fitted directly to public Voynich training pages and assignment to plaintext is random; neither the key nor the model is claimed as historical or deciphering. The plaintext dictionary is selected on the preceding portion of the same book, so held-out sections are not independent books. Escape output permits all ASCII letters, including glyphs not recognized as ordinary EVA, and its fixed ROT13 is merely reversible, not a security claim. The presented compressed key bits are not the complete description length or a comparison with the Voynich-only baseline. The existing codebook family does not implement the escape and the trusted scorer does not run this local script. Evaluation uses the public practice split and two readings of the same manuscript, not the secret held-out pages. No claimed language/cipher cell was ruled out.
detail.method: Build an observed ciphertext vocabulary from certain ASCII-lowercase paragraph tokens on public ZL practice-training pages, excluding words beginning with z to reserve that prefix for escapes. For each of Dante, Libro de Buen Amor, the Paston Letters and Jan Hus Postilla, choose the 500, 2,000 or 5,000 most frequent plaintext types in the first 50,000 normalized tokens. Independently shuffle the sorted ciphertext vocabulary with seeds 17, 37 and 73 and assign the first K entries to those plaintext types. Encode the next 25,000 tokens: dictionary words use their assigned ciphertext word; other words use z plus fixed ROT13 on their literal spelling. The z prefix is an escape introducer, not a mandatory terminal glyph. The completed map and escape rule recover every planted test exactly, as asserted. The plaintext frequency training window and test window do not overlap, and the ZL codeword sample is separate from public practice-evaluation ZL and IT pages. Evaluate only dictionary membership of the observed words in the assigned ciphertext side of the key; this is a syntactic coverage measurement, not a prediction that the random paired plaintext is correct. The escape channel can produce non-EVA letters, so its appearance is counted separately from dictionary output.

detail.statement: Randomly assigned dictionaries made from 6,253 certain ZL practice-training word types allow repeated non-e glyphs and multi-gallows entries, but coverage and key cost trade off. Across four historical works and three assignment seeds, a 5,000-entry key covers on average 67.0% of tokens and 48–49% of types in the public ZL and IT practice-evaluation samples; its compressed dictionary alone costs 224,376–245,864 bits, or 8.98–9.83 bits per 25,000-token planted test. A reversible escape handles unknown plaintext words, but its output is not constrained to the Voynich glyph inventory. No matching key or real plaintext is inferred from these coverage figures.

detail.check: Develop a probabilistic or otherwise uncertainty-aware decoder for alternative stem/column partitions and context-sensitive homophone collisions. Freeze fitting and search budgets, plaintext-frequency constraints and nulls on independent calibration texts; test on new disjoint books, new keys and longer ciphertext. detail.limitations: The penalty encourages but does not exactly enforce the reference distribution. Inferred longest-prefix groups are a deterministic heuristic, not a posterior over column assignments, and multiple nested eligible prefixes are common. The upper bound uses ground truth on test tokens and is not an attainable unsupervised estimate. Different books share language, edition conventions and in two cases a Bible translation; each book’s same test passage is reused across keys, so the 15 cases per cell are not 15 independent books. The iid and Markov generators are limited diagnostics, and 19 permutations have low resolution. A known period is an oracle in the cyclic null, while an unknown period can reduce power. The vocabulary, sample lengths and λ/penalty choices constrain only this search; low accuracy does not rule out richer searches or the broader cipher family. No Voynich or secret held-out manuscript text is used.
detail.method: Use the pinned Hermes P.III table and five Latin books under the P-J-023 control pipeline. For each target book the external Latin unigram and add-one bigram reference excludes that whole book. Take its first 12,000 plaintext letters for cipher training and next 4,000 for held-out evaluation. For 10, 24, or 131 sampled rows, use three seeds and either independent random selection or a fixed cycle. Generate a real-text, reference-unigram iid, and reference-bigram Markov plaintext per setting, with the same seeded row-selection process. The decoder sees ciphertext word strings and the candidate alphabet, not plaintext, true row IDs, or row table. Four compared methods are frequency-ranked two-character suffix mapping; unconstrained two-sweep suffix bigram search from P-J-023; suffix search with a soft 3×N KL penalty toward the external reference letter distribution; and a word-specific search initialized from that suffix model. For the latter, infer each word’s longest prefix of at least two characters shared by at least four distinct training word forms; otherwise use a singleton group. Penalize by 12 objective units each pair of distinct word forms in the same inferred group assigned the same plaintext letter, plus the same 3×N KL penalty. All searches perform exactly two deterministic coordinate-ascent sweeps with one start. Unknown held-out words use the constrained suffix mapping, then the commonest reference letter. Parameters and budget were fixed for this pilot, not independently preregistered.
detail.null_and_uncertainty: For each held-out decoded stream, compare its bigram loss with 19 global shuffles and 19 shuffles within index modulo the planted column count; add-one lower-tail p=.05 is the minimum attainable. The latter control is given the actual period for cyclic cases, although that information is not given to the decoder, and is merely an artificial stratification for random selection. The evaluator alone reports the training token-weighted majority true-column share for inferred groups, the fraction of training tokens with multiple nested eligible prefixes, and an optimistic held-out type-map accuracy ceiling obtained by assigning each observed spelling its most common true letter. These diagnostics use the planted key after fitting and are not a posterior distribution over columns.

check: Calibrate a model on genuinely separate historical works, not just disjoint windows within each work, and fix its search and external five-width gate before manuscript scoring. Check local predictive loss, calibrated interval coverage, unseen word behavior and transition probabilities. If the gate passes, identify a separate manuscript sample large enough for all five fixed widths and pre-register its split and comparison; otherwise report failure and stop. Include structured non-language and quire or sheet grouping only when independently supported by sufficient data.

detail.check: Calibrate a model on genuinely separate historical works, not just disjoint windows within each work, and fix its search and external five-width gate before manuscript scoring. Check local predictive loss, calibrated interval coverage, unseen word behavior and transition probabilities. If the gate passes, identify a separate manuscript sample large enough for all five fixed widths and pre-register its split and comparison; otherwise report failure and stop. Include structured non-language and quire or sheet grouping only when independently supported by sufficient data.
detail.gate: Freeze selected parameters and the external test gate before any manuscript comparison. For each historical test window and each width 2,810, 4,215, 5,620, 7,025 and 8,430, require the observed exponent to exceed the medians of 32 exact-frequency shuffles and 32 empirical-bigram nulls fitted to that test, and lie between the 4th and 61st sorted values of 64 independent model samples. Also require test local loss no worse than both the fixed-cache and no-cache baselines. Every work and width must pass. Report observed exponents, order-statistic interval, sample min/median/max, null medians and complete block counts. This is an exploratory fixed pilot gate, not the original paper’s broader 16-work protocol or a guaranteed-coverage interval.
detail.limitations: The parameter objective was designed for this pilot and uses four simulated draws per candidate/book; it is not preregistered and does not establish model generality. The same four books supply disjoint windows across train, development and test, so the test is not a new set of works and the historical editions may have normalized orthography. The 64-sample order-statistic interval is a finite predictive range, not a proven confidence or coverage guarantee; the widest width has only three complete blocks. Test-fitted shuffle and empirical-bigram distributions are controls, not deployable predictors. Failure of these six fixed candidates does not prove all topic models fail. The code reads no manuscript tokens or secret split, and no Voynich generator scoreboard or physical-bifolio test was run after the external gate failed.
detail.method: Use the same four pinned historical works and nonoverlapping 30,000-token train, development and test windows as P-G-026. Train the normalized bigram/unigram/character-backoff and 4,096-token cache from that pilot. Divide each training window into ten equal contiguous topic inventories. Each has a smoothed word distribution (3,000 observed topic tokens plus 1,000 units of the global backoff). A latent state initially uniform over topics stays or is uniformly redrawn with probability 1/period each token. Emissions mix the bigram and topic distributions, then mix with the finite cache; filtering uses the exact ten-state forward probabilities, so the claimed local loss and generator implement the same normalized model. Predefine six (topic weight, cache weight, mean period) candidates: (0,.3,8000), (.3,.3,2000), (.6,.3,2000), (.3,.3,8000), (.6,.3,8000), (.8,.1,8000). Select on development windows only by minimizing the average over books of [model bits/token minus fixed-cache bits/token + 10 times the average absolute difference between the observed five-width Taylor exponents and the median of four generated development samples]. This explicitly trades local prediction against long-range fit; the coefficient and candidate set are fixed pilot choices, not an established optimal model. The selected tuple is (.6,.3,8000).

check: Before registering any hidden-page claim, identify the authors’ original implementation or justify another explicitly defined statistic that does not merely telescope to uniqueness position and frequency. Prove its relationship to those variables, validate hand-computed prefix trees including prefix-of-another-word boundaries, then calibrate the proposed statistic and fixed historical comparisons on independent samples and structured generators. Specify sampling, segmentation, weighting, uncertainty and minimum support before a hidden-page run. Do not treat this regularized convention as the authors’ documented method.

detail.check: Before registering any hidden-page claim, identify the authors’ original implementation or justify another explicitly defined statistic that does not merely telescope to uniqueness position and frequency. Prove its relationship to those variables, validate hand-computed prefix trees including prefix-of-another-word boundaries, then calibrate the proposed statistic and fixed historical comparisons on independent samples and structured generators. Specify sampling, segmentation, weighting, uncertainty and minimum support before a hidden-page run. Do not treat this regularized convention as the authors’ documented method.
detail.limitations: The two witnesses transcribe the same manuscript; the three windows per historical source are not independent books. The generators are fit to the public training pages and written to their shape; these are structured controls, not independent fits to hidden pages. Five seeds per generator and no inferential test provide an exploratory sign comparison, not power or causal identification. The hidden pages were not used. The source implementation was not found in the searches performed; absence of a search result does not establish unavailability.
detail.method: Use exactly 30,000 certain lowercase ASCII word tokens; raw character positions and types; type-weighted regressions separately by word length 4–8. Let C(p) be the token count of prefix p, C(empty)=N, and c the full word count. The uniqueness point u is the first prefix belonging to one type; if the complete word prefixes another type, u=length+1 and the last segment is an end marker. For every segment i up through u, compute -log2((C(prefix_i)-c+1)/(C(prefix_{i-1})-c+1)); the end marker has competing count zero. Average the u values. These ratios are an explicit add-one regularization, not a normalized conditional probability. The last numerator is 1, so all intermediate factors cancel and the exact mean is log2(N-c+1)/u. Compare the earlier finite-only convention in the task’s parent record; neither convention is confirmed as the paper’s implementation.

detail.statement: Under one explicitly specified add-one regularization of the competing-prefix ratios, including the uniqueness-point segment makes the mean telescope exactly to log2(N - word_count + 1) divided by the uniqueness-point index. It is therefore algebraically coupled to frequency and uniqueness position, rather than an independent information measure. In 30,000-token public training samples from both ZL and IT, four historical books (three windows each), and five seeds each of three public-trained generators per transcription, all 220 length-specific fits (lengths 4–8) have positive type-frequency versus relative-uniqueness slopes and negative slopes for this regularized mean information. These exploratory signs alone do not distinguish the manuscript from these particular structured generators.

In 30,000-token public training samples from both ZL and IT, four historical books (three windows each), and five seeds each of three public-trained generators per transcription, all 220 length-specific fits (lengths 4–8) have positive type-frequency versus relative-uniqueness slopes and negative slopes for this regularized mean information. These exploratory signs alone do not distinguish the manuscript from these particular structured generators.

experiment.json.summary: A finite add-one uniqueness-point convention makes mean information algebraically dependent on uniqueness position; three structured generators match the reported slope directions.

step.json.check: Before registering any hidden-page claim, identify the authors’ original implementation or justify another explicitly defined statistic that does not merely telescope to uniqueness position and frequency. Prove its relationship to those variables, validate hand-computed prefix trees including prefix-of-another-word boundaries, then calibrate the proposed statistic and fixed historical comparisons on independent samples and structured generators. Specify sampling, segmentation, weighting, uncertainty and minimum support before a hidden-page run. Do not treat this regularized convention as the authors’ documented method.
step.json.limitations: The two witnesses transcribe the same manuscript; the three windows per historical source are not independent books. The generators are fit to the public training pages and written to their shape; these are structured controls, not independent fits to hidden pages. Five seeds per generator and no inferential test provide an exploratory sign comparison, not power or causal identification. The hidden pages were not used. The source implementation was not found in the searches performed; absence of a search result does not establish unavailability.
step.json.method: Use exactly 30,000 certain lowercase ASCII word tokens; raw character positions and types; type-weighted regressions separately by word length 4–8. Let C(p) be the token count of prefix p, C(empty)=N, and c the full word count. The uniqueness point u is the first prefix belonging to one type; if the complete word prefixes another type, u=length+1 and the last segment is an end marker. For every segment i up through u, compute -log2((C(prefix_i)-c+1)/(C(prefix_{i-1})-c+1)); the end marker has competing count zero. Average the u values. These ratios are an explicit add-one regularization, not a normalized conditional probability. The last numerator is 1, so all intermediate factors cancel and the exact mean is log2(N-c+1)/u. Compare the earlier finite-only convention in the task’s parent record; neither convention is confirmed as the paper’s implementation.

import csv,random,json,math,hashlib
from urllib.request import urlopen
from collections import defaultdict
paths=['https://zenodo.org/api/records/23407412/files/predictions_rep%d.csv/content' % i for i in range(1,4)]
expected=['380ac745f59a984244b219ed218ba433','6ea27bf54de02598847ad1b53b87b09e','e80709783db8d0bfa70d84e826854eb7']
byrep=[]; out=[]
for j,(p,h) in enumerate(zip(paths,expected),1):
 raw=urlopen(p,timeout=30).read();assert hashlib.md5(raw).hexdigest()==h
 g=defaultdict(list)
 for r in csv.DictReader(raw.decode().splitlines()):
  assert int(r['replication'])==j
  g[r['folio']].append(float(r['baseline_loss'])-float(r['model_loss']))
 d={f:(len(v),sum(v)) for f,v in g.items()};byrep.append(d)
 n=sum(x[0] for x in d.values()); gain=sum(x[1] for x in d.values())/n
 rng=random.Random(42024+j); ids=sorted(d);boots=[]
 for _ in range(10000):
  selected=rng.choices(ids,k=len(ids)); boots.append(sum(d[i][1] for i in selected)/sum(d[i][0] for i in selected))
 boots.sort();loo=[(sum(x[1] for f,x in d.items() if f!=i)/sum(x[0] for f,x in d.items() if f!=i)) for i in ids]
 out.append({'rep':j,'tokens':n,'folios':len(ids),'gain':gain,'bootstrap_95':[boots[249],boots[9749]],'folios_positive':sum(s>0 for n,s in d.values()),'folios_negative':sum(s<0 for n,s in d.values()),'leave_one_folio_gain_range':[min(loo),max(loo)],'sha256':hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()})
inter=[]
for i in range(3):
 for j in range(i+1,3):
  a,b=byrep[i],byrep[j]; shared=sorted(a.keys()&b.keys());inter.append({'replications':[i+1,j+1],'shared_test_folios':len(shared),'overlap_fraction_of_smaller':len(shared)/min(len(a),len(b))})
print(json.dumps({'result':out,'test_folio_overlap':inter},indent=2))

detail.limitations: This deliberately simple escaped spelling is a diagnostic construction, not a historically sourced cipher or a claim that the selected marker was used in the manuscript. A valid escape is not automatically a sensible plaintext, and no key is inferred. Dictionary assignments are random and use public Voynich training types, so membership is not recovery; reference windows and generated texts are not independent of their own fitted training vocabulary. ZL and IT transcribe the same pages. The 16-character cap refuses some test words; none is silently accepted. Fixed-width and compressed JSON costs are descriptive components, omit full program, plaintext distribution and preimage charges, and do not constitute the judge’s full model score. No secret held-out manuscript pages were accessed.
detail.method: Use public training ZL paragraph words for the candidate codebook after excluding all y-initial words (5,797 types), and reserve y as escape prefix. For each lowercase ASCII byte emit four base-four digits a/e/i/o, preceded once by y; decode validates each byte, length 1–16, and exact syntax. Encode whole words, preserving spaces; reject rather than silently alter any longer OOV word. Fit plaintext frequency ranks on the first 50,000 tokens of each hash-verified historical reference; assign 1,000 or 5,000 random codewords with seeds 17/37/73; encode and exactly decode the next 25,000 tokens. Evaluate dictionary membership and strict escape syntax on the public ZL/IT practice-evaluation witnesses. Count dictionary JSON compressed by the project’s judge, compressed codec-function source separately, 3 bits per five-symbol escape glyph as a fixed-width cost, and literal UTF-8 plaintext size as an accounting reference. These component sizes are not a full MDL score and must not be summed without specifying the whole coding scheme.

detail.statement: A prefix-reserved, exactly reversible escape using only EVA a/e/i/o/y glyphs handles unknown lowercase ASCII words of length at most 16; longer words are explicitly refused. Across four historical books and three random codebook assignments, with 5,000 assigned entries, 2,166–6,452 of 25,000 planted test words use the escape and 0–4 are refused. The escaped tokens average 28.55–30.98 EVA glyphs, and a simple fixed-width charge for their five-symbol stream is 201,294–557,400 bits; the compressed dictionary alone costs 224,168–245,536 bits. None of the 5,461 ZL or 5,394 IT public practice-evaluation tokens is a valid escaped word under this frozen syntax. The channel therefore provides no literal escape coverage of those samples, despite exact planted round-trips; dictionary membership is not decipherment.

Develop a stronger control for latent line-level mixtures, prespecify the eight edge pairs, aggregate score, minimum support, seed and permutation budget, then test held-out ZL and IT without interpreting a null rejection as proof of direct transitions.
detail.limitations: This is a local prototype, not a reviewed or registered scorer. The 20 null books and 20 alternatives each give very imprecise error and power estimates, and the Markov and latent-line examples are deliberately strong. A latent line state violates the permutation exchangeability assumption and can mimic a direct adjacent-word signal; the experiment cannot determine which explanation applies to the manuscript. The independent cell shuffle preserves each cell inventory but not the word inventory of each individual line. Different witness transcriptions share the manuscript, and public practice evaluation is already inspected. No hidden pages were used. The actual p-value resolution is 0.025 for 39 and 0.01 for 99 permutations.
detail.method: Select certain nonempty paragraph words and preserve original positions and gaps. Groups are (page, paragraph-first-line flag, exact original line length, zero-based position); independently permute full word identities inside each cell. Count eight ordered last/first EVA-basic glyph pairs (y or n) × (q, o, ch, d) over truly adjacent selected words. For each pair, its expected count is the sum over eligible boundaries of the product of the relevant left and right cell marginal probabilities. The frozen aggregate score is sum((observed - expected)^2 / (expected + 1)) over the eight pairs. Use this same analytic expectation for every shuffle and add-one permutation p-values; 39 permutations for each synthetic example and 99 for each public example. Refuse fewer than 30 cells with at least two distinct words. This minimum does not guarantee statistic movement; a reviewed scorer must also refuse invariant statistics.

detail.statement: A proposed layout-conditioned null shuffles intact certain words jointly within (page, paragraph-first-line flag, exact line token count, exact word position) cells; adjacent boundaries then share the same shuffled word. On 20 synthetic books with independent conditional word choices it rejects 1/20 at 0.05; on 20 planted first-order dependent books it rejects 20/20. However, it also rejects 20/20 books with a shared latent line state, showing that the null can flag line-level heterogeneity without a direct transition mechanism. A sparse layout with no movable cells is refused. Exploratory practice-training and practice-evaluation results show positive aggregate discrepancies in ZL and IT; neither the null nor those results are registered held-out facts.

statement: A four-table mechanical sampler learns the frequencies of all certain paragraph word types in four relative line-position bins on ZL public training pages. It samples a public-training line length, draws each table cell independently with fixed seed 390291, and writes the artificial word zzzzzzzzzz in every fourth slot as a guard against copying any four-word manuscript phrase. The table does not name or classify the sh/ch contrast; its general position tables retain every training-word positional tendency. It assumes word spaces and advance knowledge of line length. The artificial filler and copied vocabulary are features of the construction, not a reading. Fit uses no held-out pages.

detail.statement: An independent arithmetic check of the twelve stated rotations used the submitted fleet-fable object positions and the first clock marker on each submitted label line in pinned ZL3b-n.txt. Freeze tokenization, alphabet, prefix depth, sample size, books, type weighting, support and uncertainty; compare independent books and multiple structured generators. detail.definition: For token count N, type count c(w), and token prefix count C2(w), define score S2(w)=log2((N-c(w)+1)/(C2(w)-c(w)+1)), on words of at least two characters. C2 counts all tokens whose spelling starts with the same two characters, regardless of their lengths. This is minus the log of the add-one competitor fraction, not a normalized conditional probability. Fixing N and c does not fix C2, so S2 cannot be a function of frequency and uniqueness position alone. If prefix segment surprisals use the same add-one competitor counts, their first two terms telescope exactly to this S2; unlike averaging through the uniqueness point, the terminal competitor count generally varies. The end-of-word marker is not counted as a character; a word which prefixes another remains a competitor at depth two.

same_frequency_counterexample.note: To hold uniqueness position fixed too, compare cat (prefix ca shared by car) with dog in corpus cat, car, dog, dot, dot: both are count 1, have uniqueness point 3, but ca has two tokens and do has three, so scores are log2(5/2) and log2(5/3).

method.control: For each seed 827, 828, 829, iterate original types in sorted order, randomly shuffle each type’s character multiset once using random.Random(seed), and replace all occurrences of the type consistently. Recount resulting types and prefixes; collisions merge types, so frequency spectrum need not remain exactly invariant. This destroys positional structure but preserves each token’s character multiset, length, ordering and total tokens. The three controls are not independent books or historically plausible production mechanisms.
method.limitations: Exploratory, thresholds not preregistered, no uncertainty interval and only three randomizations per book. Shared prefix counts create dependencies; samples within a single book are not replicates. The raw statistic remains sensitive to c and N, alphabet/normalization and +1 smoothing. No authors’ implementation was located or reproduced. The control is a permutation of a language source, not an independent structured generator. No manuscript claim or held-out comparison is made.
method.processing: vs.refcorpus.blocks_of strips Gutenberg wrappers and normalizes each reference language, including Latin j/v mapping; blocks were rejoined in source order. Segments are normalized characters, not EVA-basic units. Prefix counts include all token lengths. For each length 4–8, regress S2 on log2(type count/N) with equal weight per distinct type, reporting mean and slope; all groups have at least 100 types.
method.sample: First 30,000 normalized tokens of each pinned work: la_augustine (late antique), it_villani (c. 1350), fr_rose (13th c.) and en_chaucer (c. 1390). These are distinct from the four books in the parent pilot but the editions and genre differ; no manuscript data measured.

detail.statement: A fixed two-character competing-prefix score depends on prefix-neighbour counts as well as word frequency, avoiding the uniqueness-position telescope. In four 30,000-token historical book samples, each of 20 length-stratified means is below every one of its three type-letter-shuffle controls; source slopes against log frequency are negative in 19 of 20 groups. This is an exploratory comparison with one simple control, not a language test or a replication of the authors’ implementation.

check: Before a hidden-page test, establish a historically motivated channel, pre-register its syntax on independent training data, and compare against disjoint planted samples and other plausible non-language processes. Use a normalized plaintext model, fully specified prefix codes for transmitted ciphertext, codec and dictionary, and preimages; give every refused word a paid lossless fallback. Calibrate unknown-key recovery and false positives on independent keys, samples and books; compare dictionary-only, escape-only and combined variants at matched complete cost. No such recovery, full charge, or hidden-page claim is supplied here.

detail.accounting: Dictionary-only refuses every out-of-vocabulary word; escape-only and combined refuse plaintext words longer than 16. Cipher character counts exclude the nine refusals and cannot be taken as complete compression scores. Compressed canonical dictionary JSON costs 50,032 bits under judge.compressed_bits, but does not include codec, model, encoding overhead or a lossless fallback, so it is not a full key or MDL cost. methods.aligned: For source and marker events separately, condition on the last n source symbols and their markers, and for a marker include its just-emitted source character. Add-0.5 unigram and context interpolation prior mass 2. Marker location follows from the prior decoded source character; distinct B/D alphabet and known transform make alignment free under these assumptions.
methods.forward: P-J-011 interpolated Markov character model at n output symbols, not n source symbols; additive unigram .5 and interpolated shorter contexts with prior mass 2.
methods.limitations: The source and aligned estimators differ in smoothing, fitted parameterization and event-state conditioning; direct rate differences combine those effects. Counts are predictive code lengths, not measured compression files; model descriptions, transform rules, block boundaries and source alphabet are treated as shared. Single validation partition, one random draw per block; not manuscript evidence.
methods.random: Per-block shuffled exact deterministic-marker histogram, seeded independently by block and split. The inverse benchmark bills log2 binomial(n,k) per block, conditioned on recovered source and known rule. Marker sequence is not given to decoder.
methods.selection: 48 consecutive training-work blocks fit, next 16 validate source Markov order, refit 64; first 64 blocks of separate evaluation work. The validation split was fixed before these results; same works as P-J-011, so these are not new work-pair replications.
methods.source: P-J-011 cleaned extraction scripts and source metadata; symbols a-z plus space; block ends and rules known to encoder and decoder.

detail.statement: On the three cleaned independent work pairs from P-J-011, choose source order 0–8 on the first 48 training-work blocks against the next 16, then refit on the 64 and evaluate once on the first 64 blocks of the other work. Order 3 is selected in all three. Constant letter-padding forward per-source bits are 3.355, 3.150, 3.249 (Latin, Italian, German); an alignment-aware model using the last three source symbols and their emitted markers yields 3.065, 2.985, 2.962. The source inverse benchmark is 3.224, 3.034, 3.184. The aligned and forward models have different smoothing and state, so these differences are not a controlled causal estimate of context length alone. For a matched random permutation of B/D markers the inverse benchmark bills per-block log2 binomial choices, yielding 3.997, 3.819, 3.965 bits per original symbol. All transformed blocks invert exactly. For constant suffix, a known-rule decoder tracks whether the preceding source symbol is a letter: it maps a source-space prediction to B followed by a forced space and emits the final B at the known block boundary. It uses exactly the original source model bits; conventional forward suffix results are included.

detail.limitations: The public practice split is not the season holdout. Both transcription witnesses describe the same folios and agree on most checked classes; they are not independent page samples. The evaluation rows are selected for matching line lengths and can still be misaligned, and the two witness row sets differ. Training only uses ZL, so IT is external to training transcription but not an independent model fit. One class scheme, one fit, conditional bootstrap, and preliminary permutation checks do not prove a language mechanism. No original code or class definitions have been obtained.
detail.model: Define 17 first-character classes acdefgiklmnopqrsy plus OTHER. These classes are a simple independent alternative, not the paper’s classes. Position bins are target index 1, indices 2–3, 4–6, and 7+ (zero based). Train two categorical distributions on all eligible ZL training pairs: baseline target class conditional on position bin, and alternative target class conditional on position and immediate predecessor class. Each gets independent add-one smoothing over 18 possible classes. Score on public evaluation rows as log P_alt - log P_base in nats, using the single fixed fit; each row receives equal weight.
detail.selection: Use project IVTFF reader and the public practice split only, with ZL training and the same ZL or IT evaluation folios (no season-heldout seed). Paragraph unit P; use a target and its immediate physical-line predecessor only when both are certain nonempty lowercase ASCII alphabetic words, do not bridge rejected tokens. Exclude the first token of each line. Match evaluation lines by folio and line id, require equal raw token counts, and calculate each witness separately; matching count alone does not guarantee same word segmentation. There are 3,140 common valid ordinal positions, of which both previous and target first-glyph classes agree at 2,989. The ZL and IT analyses have slightly different valid positions.
detail.statement: A simple, explicitly specified 18-class first-glyph predictor trained on 175 ZL public-training folios gains 0.0234 nats per target token over a position-only model on 3,140 ZL tokens and 0.0223 on 3,162 IT tokens from equal-length matched public evaluation lines. Paired whole-folio bootstrap intervals for each fixed model exclude zero, and each measured gain exceeds 100 within-folio, position-bin predecessor shuffles. This is an exploratory alternative classification, not a reproduction of the paper’s unpublished 18 classes or its model.
detail.title: A specified first-glyph predecessor model gains on both public witnesses
detail.uncertainty: For each witness, resample whole evaluation folios with replacement 2,000 times, seed 29111, preserving all rows and token weighting; percentile entries 49 and 1949 are reported. Intervals condition on one fitted model and are not independent-model training intervals. For each of 100 seeds 0–99, shuffle predecessor classes among rows within each folio and position bin and rescore the same targets with the fixed model. This retains predecessor marginal counts per folio/bin but destroys local pairing; it is not a complete line-structure or causal control.

import json
from vs import redteam
for author in ['mtx-light','giffordino']:
 x=json.load(open('experiments/G-every-fact/'+author+'/attack.json'))

detail.statement: Rerunning the current vs.redteam.fact_attack with cut book and each submission’s first_lines when present reproduces the six practice measurements in P-G-025. R-028: F-005 0.169454, F-013 2.032998, F-014 0.687280; R-042: 0.180215, 2.092275, 0.609345. The corresponding manuscript values are 0.230432, 1.940360, 0.710540. R-028 passes all three fact thresholds, R-042 misses F-014. This checks the two fixed outputs only; it does not test seed-to-seed variation or the slope in the proposed sweep. detail.design: Each seeded book has six pages, 36 lines per page and 12 two-bit words per line. A line independently receives a binary latent state. In latent settings, each word’s first and last bit is independently the latent state with probability p, otherwise its complement; conditional on the state there is no direct predecessor-to-successor influence. The independent condition draws both bits independently with probability 0.5. In the positive Markov setting, last bits retain p=0.8 latent dependence, while each target word from index 5 onward copies the previous word’s last bit as its first bit with probability 0.85, otherwise flips it.
detail.limits: The probe is noisy and conditioning on a noisy latent surrogate leaves residual mixture dependence. At p=1 all target words are identical within each page-position-proxy group, so the proxy permutation is immovable and its lack of rejection does not show valid calibrated inference; an implementation with a movement gate must refuse the test. This study has only 30 books and 99 permutations per setting, binary glyphs and one line-state process; the same seed indices are shared across settings. Positive-control rejection rates do not establish general power. No manuscript data were examined, no hidden-page test performed, and this is not a trusted scorer primitive.
detail.statement: In a synthetic pilot, stratifying fixed-cell complete-word shuffles by an independent four-word proxy for each line’s latent state fails to control latent-line confounding. Out of 30 generated books per setting, the binary proxy rejects all 30 at each state accuracy 0.7, 0.8 and 0.9; a five-level count proxy rejects 28, 30 and 22 respectively. At accuracy 1 it rejects none, but the target groups are immovable, so that case has no power. The independent-word condition rejects once in 30 with either proxy. These results concern a synthetic equality statistic, not a held-out manuscript fact.
detail.test: The four initial words are excluded from the tested boundaries and used as a proxy: either whether at least two of their last bits are one, or the exact count 0–4. Test seven boundaries between positions 4–11 with the one-sided number where previous last bit equals next first bit. Shuffle complete words jointly within page, exact target position, and proxy class; the baseline omits proxy class. Hence adjacent boundaries share the same permuted word and the probe does not overlap test positions. For each book and method use 99 shuffles, seeded 10000+book seed, and p=(1+#shuffles with statistic >= observed)/100; repeat book seeds 0–29. This statistic is a simple surrogate, not the parent proposal’s eight-pair aggregate.

detail.statement: A new exploratory check uses the first 7,000 normalized words from each of three cleaned works (Augustine, Dante and Nibelungenlied), ten shuffles, one random monoalphabetic substitution and three independent equal-probability three-sign homophonic encodings. For each plaintext sample compare no removals, the single most frequent type, and the top ceil(1% of plaintext distinct types); use the same number of removals in each transformed sample. Ties are broken by first appearance. Count forward unequal-word pairs at distances 1–3, mark an unordered pair type skewed when absolute forward minus reverse counts exceed 5, and divide by the number of observed unordered pair types. Original skew ratios with no removals versus 1% removal are Latin 0.001982 to 0.000141, Italian 0.003644 to 0.000301, German 0.005210 to 0.000746. A bijective character substitution preserves the results exactly, and a planted five-symbol directional cycle is detected; in the tested toy homophonic encodings skew ratios are zero or near zero. In the no-removal samples, distinct types per token are 0.392, 0.307, 0.207, while hapax types per token are 0.289, 0.214, 0.107. These are different readings of unique words. Pair-type and pair-occurrence denominators also differ. This is a sensitivity pilot, not an exact replication or a manuscript result.

detail.controls: For each period and seed generate an independent ten-character random plaintext motif using seed+3000, repeat it to 8,000 characters, encrypt with independently sampled random columns, and run the identical search. detail.generator: Use the pinned Hermes P.III CSV (SHA-256 fe3f24a46dbc6b655eab8dbbd75addf84ee4a7dbd387ad802af75d02edfe5b4d). Normalize the pinned it_villani and fr_rose works via vs.refcorpus.blocks_of, concatenate only letters present in the table alphabet (spaces and out-of-alphabet characters removed), and take characters 4,000–11,999. The books were not included in the earlier five-book Latin recovery pilot; the selections are Italian and French rather than Latin. For each period 10, 24 or 131 and seed 207, 411 or 917, sample that many distinct table rows. For cyclic mode use the rows in sequence; for random mode sample row indices independently and uniformly. Output the table word for the plaintext character and selected row. The evaluator knows the planted period and plaintext; the search does not.
detail.limits: The search’s no-period null destroys all sequential plaintext structure, so rejection cannot identify a cipher schedule. The shortest-significant rule and adversarial control are exploratory and require new independent confirmation. Exact-word equality ignores OCR/transcription noise and may fail on variable spellings; selected row counts are treated as true cycle length although equivalent table rows could reduce the observable period. The synthetic motif is not a natural-language null. No Bayesian partition decoder, recovery of unknown keys, period uncertainty interval, or manuscript test is provided; P-J-026 remains open.

detail.search: Take the first 4,000 ciphertext words. For lags 2–160 calculate exact word-equality rate between tokens separated by that lag. Baseline reports the lag with maximum rate, breaking ties toward smaller lags. To calibrate maximum selection, compare all lag rates to the maxima from 49 independent global shuffles of the word sequence; p=(1+#shuffle maxima >= observed)/50. The exploratory revised rule reports the smallest lag with this maximum-adjusted p <= .05. Report the selected peak rate on the following disjoint 4,000 ciphertext tokens, but do not claim this is a separate significance test. NumPy 2.5.4 default_rng is used for shuffles; seeds and complete results are included.
detail.statement: On 18 planted cyclic-column ciphertexts from two new books, maximum exact-word recurrence over lags 2–160 recovers the true period in 9/18 and otherwise selects a multiple; an exploratory shortest-significant-lag rule recovers all 18 and rejects no 18 random-column historical-text cases. But with random columns and a repeated ten-character plaintext, all nine tests reject and eight report lag 10: periodic plaintext itself can mimic the same evidence. The shortest-lag rule was chosen after inspecting the first experiment. Neither test recovers the plaintext or key.

statement: A four-table mechanical sampler learns the frequencies of all certain paragraph word types in four relative line-position bins on ZL public training pages. It samples a public-training line length, draws each table cell independently with fixed seed 390291, and writes the artificial word zzzzzzzzzz in every fourth slot as a guard against copying any four-word manuscript phrase. The table does not name or classify the sh/ch contrast; its general position tables retain every training-word positional tendency. It assumes word spaces and advance knowledge of line length. The artificial filler and copied vocabulary are features of the construction, not a reading. Fit uses no held-out pages. This is the unchanged position-table output submitted in R-047 against F-029, reused to test whether the same general procedure also reproduces F-030; the sampler was not refitted for the k/t contrast.

detail.design: Reuse the fixed P-G-026 hyperparameters (topic weight .6, cache weight .3, mean topic-switch interval 8,000; ten topics, 4,096-token cache) selected on four earlier books. Separately for each new book, fit its first 30,000 normalized tokens and score the next 30,000; no parameters are selected using these tests. Books are Villani’s Cronica, Roman de la Rose, and Chaucer’s Canterbury Tales and Other Poems. All are separate works from the hyperparameter-selection books, though these editions, languages, genres and periods do not sample all historical writing and are not independent in a population sense. Token input is standard project refcorpus normalization, ascii a–z, maximum length 30.
detail.gate: Use exactly the earlier pilot joint gate: the candidate must have no worse test log loss than both the fixed-cache and no-cache baselines, and for each width 2,810, 4,215, 5,620, 7,025 and 8,430, the observed exponent must exceed the medians of 32 fixed-frequency shuffles and 32 test-fitted empirical-bigram samples and lie between the 4th and 61st sorted values of 64 independent model simulations. Order-statistic intervals are exploratory rather than verified nominal coverage. Work-by-width outcomes and null medians are recorded below.
detail.limits: Parameters were optimized on the previous development works; per-book inventories, transitions and character backoff are necessarily fitted on the first 30,000 tokens of each new book. Predictive intervals and five-width joint gate are stringent exploratory checks, not formal population-coverage guarantees. Tests share widths, text samples and model fits and are dependent. Only three additional historical works were evaluated; no new structured non-language generator was fit, no reliable sheet grouping was assumed, and no manuscript data were used.
detail.normalization: The character backoff generates a first letter from a normalized 26-letter distribution, thereafter chooses either a letter or end from normalized 27-way distributions, forcing termination at length 30. The global backoff is a normalized .9 empirical-token/.1 bounded-character mixture. Each successor, topic and finite-cache component is a convex combination of an empirical distribution and this backoff, and the final distribution mixes them with nonnegative weights summing to one. The ten-state filter updates normalized weights using Bayes’ rule and a normalized state transition. This is an algebraic normalization argument for the implementation, not a separate exhaustive numerical proof of all strings. Every unseen test type has positive backoff probability; counts below include repeated unseen tokens.

evidence.public_feasibility_method: Use dsl.pictures(), dsl.tokens(), dsl.select({certain:true}) and dsl._picture_objects on corpus.split_pages(practice) separately for ZL and IT. Count objects and P-unit tokens only; no words or overlap outcomes are emitted. The referenced commit is the then-current public main; the source can change.
evidence.simulation_method: 720 independent worlds per cell; 12 folios, 12 pairs per folio, six two-folio sign blocks, one-sided exact tie-inclusive randomization tail <=.05; Wilson 95% intervals. Shared bias has pre-assignment hit rates .52/.12 and a block-level fair orientation. The independent seed and per-dose draws differ from the original 720-replicate sweep. One-table uses 120 equally long symbols, 50 body tokens from page-specific exponential random weights, 24 uniformly sampled distinct candidate symbols, block-level fair role assignment, and up to 12 actual insertions per folio by replacing noncandidate body tokens. Candidate roles and body share a vocabulary but candidates are sampled uniformly, not from the body table. Simulated groups are equal-length and disjoint, but the simulation does not implement actual manuscript frequency bins or observational sampling.

detail.statement: Using repository main 800a4a4, the public practice split and the current picture selector, the two AGREED annotation records are both f72v1. The selected objects link to 28 certain ZL and 30 certain IT training label lines, but there are zero certain paragraph tokens on that folio; no selected folio appears in the public evaluation split. No recurrence outcomes were inspected, and there are currently zero usable label/body folios for this design. An independently implemented synthetic check of 12 folios, 12 matched pairs and six two-folio blocks gives 30/720 false rejections with correct block signs, 74/720 if treating folios as independent, and 193/720 if treating pairs as independent in the shared-bias zero-dose layout. At dose 0.25 the correct-block count is 107/720. These broadly reproduce the prior study’s direction with new seeds, not its exact draws. In a second synthetic role-blind one-table layout, page-specific word weights generate body words while two disjoint candidate streams are sampled symmetrically; actual label-only hits are planted by replacing equal-length noncandidate filler words. Correct-block rejection is 19/720 at zero dose and 519/720 at dose .25. These synthetic assignment and independence assumptions do not follow from observational annotations.

detail.statement: Timm (2014, section 9, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.6639v3) uses the distribution of od/ed spellings to argue for an A-before-B production order. Prior P-L1-001 showed an asymmetric preference and exceptions to a strict one-way generalization. In public practice-training paragraph tokens, this descriptive sensitivity counts each certain word containing literal EVA ed or od at most once per substring; the two counts can overlap. ZL ed share B minus A is 0.2051 (95% page-bootstrap interval 0.1807–0.2304); within section H it is 0.1548 (0.1261–0.1825). IT gives 0.2069 overall and 0.1534 in H; RF gives 0.1605 and 0.0992. Each uses 2,000 within-group page resamples, seed 503. The interval describes page-sampling sensitivity only, not independent-leaf sampling or uncertainty in handwriting. The H contrast has 79 A pages all assigned hand 1 and 29 B pages assigned hands 2, 3 or 5; section restriction therefore does not separate hand from language. The only same-hand/same-section contrast here is hand 3, section S: one A page versus 19 B pages (ZL 2/377 versus 1780/8796 ed tokens), too little A-side replication for an independent hand-matched conclusion. Token-weighted and page-mean results and od counts are included. This supports a distributional contrast but cannot order production or explain its cause.

detail.block_experiment: For each of 10, 24 and 120 fixed initial table rows, advance to the next row after every 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 plaintext letters, cyclically. Use three nonoverlapping 5,000-letter windows at offsets 0, 5,000 and 10,000 of each book. The same word layout is used for every sample. detail.check: Independently fix row counts, row-selection procedure, exact tokenizer, metric definitions, uncertainty and acceptance ranges before using new plaintext and cipher keys. Compare all four statistics jointly, using public evaluation and independent texts only after choices are frozen; add relevant historical selection rules and noise. Develop a trusted declarative evaluator and calibrated unknown-key search with planted positives and matched search budgets, including the cost and recoverability of the row schedule. detail.common_method: Use the first 5,000 certain lowercase ASCII paragraph tokens of ZL public practice-training pages as the fixed layout and baseline. Never join across line ends or uncertain tokens. Calculate plug-in word entropy, raw-character entropy, H(next raw character | previous raw character) within words, and the share of adjacent unequal words at Levenshtein distance one. Take three previously unused plaintext works, Villani, Roman de la Rose and Chaucer, verify pinned hashes and normalize with vs.refcorpus.blocks_of, retaining only symbols present in the 24-letter Hermes table. These three works are distinct but their windows and per-key outputs are not independent texts.
detail.limitations: The previous cyclic pilot and this adaptation were motivated by observed public manuscript patterns; choices are not preregistered, and this is not a statistical test or a hidden-page result. The two overlapping metrics do not correct the substantial conditional-glyph gap, and conditional entropy here is in raw characters, not EVA-basic units. Three texts and correlated seeds/window samples cannot support general power or uncertainty claims. The stochastic rule is synthetic, not demonstrated historical practice. A known-key round-trip does not establish unknown-key search power. Several required declarative scorer and multi-metric registration pieces remain unimplemented.
detail.random_experiment: After seeing the block experiment, explore independent random decisions to stay on the current row with probabilities 1/8, 1/4 or 1/2, otherwise advance one row cyclically. Use the next, disjoint 5,000-letter window at offset 15,000, three fixed seeds (113, 271, 449), and initially the same 10, 24 and 120 rows. After inspecting those outputs, add 40, 48 and 64 rows at probability 1/8 on the same windows and seeds. Thus those values are adaptively selected on this public comparison and cannot serve as independent validation. Knowing the actual random schedule and table exactly recovers the plaintext; the cost and unknown-key recoverability of that schedule are not measured.
detail.source: Hermes P.III CSV at https://github.com/hermesj/R_Voynich_Stats/blob/0ef1439fa9d90aeab42951a51d0d5a0e27db1f8f/R%20code/Historical_ciphers/keys/ciphers_poly_III_in_order.csv, SHA-256 fe3f24a46dbc6b655eab8dbbd75addf84ee4a7dbd387ad802af75d02edfe5b4d. detail.statement: Using a row for multiple successive plaintext letters sharply increases the one-edit share of adjacent Polygraphia III ciphertext words. In an exploratory follow-up with a one-eighth chance of staying on the current row, the 40- and 48-row settings overlap the public-training sample’s word entropy and adjacent one-edit rate, but their within-word conditional raw-character entropy is 2.276–2.483 bits versus the sample’s 1.536. These settings and controls were chosen after earlier exploratory results and do not constitute a joint fit, a historical reconstruction or an unknown-key recovery.
detail.title: Polygraphia row reuse raises one-edit matches but leaves a large glyph-entropy gap

statement: Using a row for multiple successive plaintext letters sharply increases the one-edit share of adjacent Polygraphia III ciphertext words. In an exploratory follow-up with a one-eighth chance of staying on the current row, the 40- and 48-row settings overlap the public-training sample’s word entropy and adjacent one-edit rate, but their within-word conditional raw-character entropy is 2.276–2.483 bits versus the sample’s 1.536. These settings and controls were chosen after earlier exploratory results and do not constitute a joint fit, a historical reconstruction or an unknown-key recovery.

experiment.json.summary: Test block and randomized row reuse against joint public-training cipher statistics.

step.json.block_experiment: For each of 10, 24 and 120 fixed initial table rows, advance to the next row after every 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 plaintext letters, cyclically. Use three nonoverlapping 5,000-letter windows at offsets 0, 5,000 and 10,000 of each book. The same word layout is used for every sample. For each setting the evaluator knows all rows and the schedule and exactly inverts all 5,000 characters; this is not unknown-key recovery.

config.layout: first 5000 certain ZL practice-training paragraph words
config.source: fixed first rows of Hermes P.III table

step.json.check: Independently fix row counts, row-selection procedure, exact tokenizer, metric definitions, uncertainty and acceptance ranges before using new plaintext and cipher keys. Compare all four statistics jointly, using public evaluation and independent texts only after choices are frozen; add relevant historical selection rules and noise. Develop a trusted declarative evaluator and calibrated unknown-key search with planted positives and matched search budgets, including the cost and recoverability of the row schedule. Do not register a hidden-page claim or exclude a language/cipher cell based on these descriptive pilots.
step.json.common_method: Use the first 5,000 certain lowercase ASCII paragraph tokens of ZL public practice-training pages as the fixed layout and baseline. Never join across line ends or uncertain tokens. Calculate plug-in word entropy, raw-character entropy, H(next raw character | previous raw character) within words, and the share of adjacent unequal words at Levenshtein distance one. Take three previously unused plaintext works, Villani, Roman de la Rose and Chaucer, verify pinned hashes and normalize with vs.refcorpus.blocks_of, retaining only symbols present in the 24-letter Hermes table. These three works are distinct but their windows and per-key outputs are not independent texts.
step.json.limitations: The previous cyclic pilot and this adaptation were motivated by observed public manuscript patterns; choices are not preregistered, and this is not a statistical test or a hidden-page result. The two overlapping metrics do not correct the substantial conditional-glyph gap, and conditional entropy here is in raw characters, not EVA-basic units. Three texts and correlated seeds/window samples cannot support general power or uncertainty claims. The stochastic rule is synthetic, not demonstrated historical practice. A known-key round-trip does not establish unknown-key search power. Several required declarative scorer and multi-metric registration pieces remain unimplemented.
step.json.random_experiment: After seeing the block experiment, explore independent random decisions to stay on the current row with probabilities 1/8, 1/4 or 1/2, otherwise advance one row cyclically. Use the next, disjoint 5,000-letter window at offset 15,000, three fixed seeds (113, 271, 449), and initially the same 10, 24 and 120 rows. After inspecting those outputs, add 40, 48 and 64 rows at probability 1/8 on the same windows and seeds. Thus those values are adaptively selected on this public comparison and cannot serve as independent validation. Knowing the actual random schedule and table exactly recovers the plaintext; the cost and unknown-key recoverability of that schedule are not measured.
step.json.source: Hermes P.III CSV at https://github.com/hermesj/R_Voynich_Stats/blob/0ef1439fa9d90aeab42951a51d0d5a0e27db1f8f/R%20code/Historical_ciphers/keys/ciphers_poly_III_in_order.csv, SHA-256 fe3f24a46dbc6b655eab8dbbd75addf84ee4a7dbd387ad802af75d02edfe5b4d. method.followup: After pilot selection, alpha=0.8, top_k=30; seeds 1000 through 1019 inclusive; otherwise identical. Count per-run E-to-S in [56,86]% A or [50,79]% B, at least one extreme start and end unit, MI >=0.29 A or >=0.25 B, and shape other than Plateau. method.input: Synthetic data only; no manuscript file loaded. The four A/B ranges and MI minima are those printed in paper Tables 5 and 6.
method.pilot: 37000 tokens per run; baseline bridge_size=2; cross vocab_zipf_alpha [0.0,0.4,0.8,1.2] with top_k [5,30], seeds [301,438,575]; 3 shuffles in evaluate_corpus_fast.
method.reproduction: Import signatures_v27 as s. For each setting instantiate s.cfg_baseline(n_words=37000,bridge_size=2,top_k=k), set cfg.vocab_zipf_alpha=alpha, call s.evaluate_corpus_fast(cfg.generate(seed=seed),cfg.tokenizer,n_shuffles=3). Each run uses a new config or generates from the unchanged config and an independently seeded RNG.

detail.statement: An exploratory synthetic-only cross of the released Parisel baseline slot generator varied its vocabulary Zipf exponent and top-k successor count. At exponent 0.8 and top-k 30, all three exploratory seeds met each of the paper’s stated Currier A and B thresholds; the selected setting then met all four in 11/20 new seeds for each dialect (not necessarily the same seeds). On the 20 seeds, boundary end-to-start rate varied from 28.6% to 87.4%, MI from 0.335 to 0.492 bits, bilateral extremity was present in all runs, and boundary shape was Plateau in one, Intermediate in 13 and Zipfian in six. This is a noisy synthetic threshold check, not a held-out manuscript evaluation or a general refutation. The configuration was selected after inspecting eight settings; the fresh 20 seeds assess Monte Carlo stability, not an independent selection of model family or manuscript thresholds. The released generator’s tokenizer uses artificial units such as k2 and e2; at seed 1000, 7,441/37,000 generated words contain digits. Those outputs are not valid EVA submissions without a separately specified, validated encoding. Its explicit boundary-pair weighting also builds in directional structure, which must be disclosed and charged to model complexity.

check: Freeze the metric, sample, independent books and structured procedures before another evaluation. Test banks trained without access to target frequency tables, size and smoothing sensitivity, multiple latent processes and cipher models; report uncertainty at the work level, preserve bounded words and establish power and false-positive rates. Obtain the authors’ original implementation if possible, and implement a reviewed declarative primitive before pre-registering any manuscript claim. Do not interpret a nonzero score, a negative slope, or a match of means as evidence for language.

detail.check: Freeze the metric, sample, independent books and structured procedures before another evaluation. Test banks trained without access to target frequency tables, size and smoothing sensitivity, multiple latent processes and cipher models; report uncertainty at the work level, preserve bounded words and establish power and false-positive rates. Obtain the authors’ original implementation if possible, and implement a reviewed declarative primitive before pre-registering any manuscript claim. Do not interpret a nonzero score, a negative slope, or a match of means as evidence for language.
detail.generators: Seed a bank of 16 or 64 distinct two-character prefixes, then independently draw a prefix uniformly for each source type and complete it with random characters, rejecting spelling collisions. Repeat three seeds 4001–4003; add an alternative 16-prefix Zipf-weighted draw. After inspecting those outputs, add 96 and 128 uniform prefixes on the same samples and seeds. Finally sort source types of length at least four by descending observed frequency and assign contiguous equal-size rank groups to 96 or 128 random prefixes, completing unique random suffixes. The latter explicitly builds frequency-conditioned prefix clusters, so negative slopes are expected and the construction is an adversarial diagnostic, not evidence of a plausible historical process. It and the larger banks were added after observing the initial results.
detail.hand_validation: On the prefix tree cat:2, cats:1, dog:1 (N=4), C2=3,3,1 and scores are log2(3/2)=0.5849625007, log2(4/3)=0.4150374993, and log2(4)=2.0 respectively. The independent direct calculation agrees with the parent pilot; the cat prefix-of-another case retains cats as a competitor.
detail.limitations: Synthetic lexicons are fitted to each source’s own complete counts and length distribution; short words and the token-order pattern remain from the source. Uniform bank size strongly controls score means, and frequency-ranked assignments deliberately induce slope; no blindness, independent generator calibration, bootstrap, trained decoder or meaningful generation has been shown. Slopes are substantially more negative than the source and are not quantitatively matched. The three works are not independent manuscript witnesses and are too few to estimate general performance. No manuscript or season-heldout pages were measured.
detail.metric: For a sample of N tokens, word type w with frequency c(w), and token count C2(w) of all words beginning with the same first two normalized characters, define log2((N-c(w)+1)/(C2(w)-c(w)+1)). Compute the type-weighted mean and ordinary least squares slope against log2(c(w)/N) separately for lengths 4–8, requiring at least 100 types in each length group. Raw normalized Latin alphabet characters are used; no end marker is inserted. The add-one formula is an explicitly chosen competitor fraction, not the published authors’ implementation.
detail.sampling: Use first 30,000 normalized tokens of pinned Dante, Libro de Buen Amor and Paston Letters, verifying each SHA-256. These are three distinct works but were used in earlier related exploratory analyses and are not fresh confirmation. A source sample is transformed in full, preserving token sequence, every word length and the entire type-frequency multiset. Words shorter than four characters stay unchanged; their prefixes still contribute to all C2 counts. Every transformed type of length at least four is mapped injectively to an artificial ASCII spelling with the same length, and its occurrences use the same replacement.
detail.statement: On three 30,000-token historical samples, synthetic bijections preserving every type’s frequency and length generate fixed-prefix scores near historical means for some length groups. A frequency-ranked prefix bank also produces negative frequency slopes in all 15 book-by-length groups, generally much steeper than the historical slopes. These fitted controls show that the metric and slope sign alone are not language-specific; they are not independent random books or a test on the manuscript.

detail.statement: Pilot toward P-J-029, not its requested full validation: I compared the first four printed prose lines under ALTEA on PDF page 21 (https://archive.org/download/CAT31000255/cat31000255.pdf, page 21) with page 21 of the companion OCR. The page was chosen before viewing as an early body page; it is a convenience sample, not a random or representative sample. One reader, no independent second transcript, expanded the printed c-with-macron to cum, joined words hyphenated at printed line endings, rendered the long s as s, mapped ae/ligature to ae, and ignored marginalia and headings. After mapping ampersands to et and applying vs.refcorpus.normalize(..., 'latin'), the human line sequence is: 'altea calida et sicca cum equalitate opatio et proprietas ipsius est lenificare et maturare et mollificare et resoluere et abstergere semen et radix sunt maioris efficaciae notanter radix uiridis decoctio'. The matching OCR lines normalize to: 'altea calida et ficca cu xqualitate opatio et pro prietas ipfius eft lenificare maturare et mollifiz care et refoluere et abftergere semen et radix funt maiorisefficacia notanterradixuiridisdecoctio'. Standard Levenshtein distance on these strings is 19/204 reference characters (9.3%); on whitespace-separated tokens it is 19/30 reference words (63.3%). Long-s substitutions, a dropped conjunction, split line-end words, and fused adjacent words contribute. The comparison conflates transcription conventions and recognition errors; individual reference readings are not independently adjudicated, so the numbers are an indicative pilot, not an estimated book-wide error rate. No corrections, language-model or cipher-control tests were made. The source is public-domain and much later than the manuscript, as recorded in P-J-029.

check: Confirm the result on genuinely untouched folios chosen before model design, with independent training refits and jointly resampled evaluation folios. Evaluate effects of smoothing, exact line length, within-line position, paragraph position and page composition with controls capable of retaining latent line mixtures and overlapping word boundaries. Resolve uncertain or shifted alignment by direct line-level comparison and report inclusion bias. Obtain the original model and classes if possible; otherwise register this alternative separately only after review, without presenting it as the paper’s result.

detail.check: Confirm the result on genuinely untouched folios chosen before model design, with independent training refits and jointly resampled evaluation folios. Evaluate effects of smoothing, exact line length, within-line position, paragraph position and page composition with controls capable of retaining latent line mixtures and overlapping word boundaries. Resolve uncertain or shifted alignment by direct line-level comparison and report inclusion bias. Obtain the original model and classes if possible; otherwise register this alternative separately only after review, without presenting it as the paper’s result.
detail.limitations: The predictor and preprocessing are an explicit alternative, not the original author’s 18 classes or model. These are correlated transcriptions of the same folios, not two independent manuscripts. Folio bootstrap intervals and permutation tails answer different questions, and the training-refit intervals show sensitivity but do not alone prove population failure. Filtering to equal-length lines and mutually certain positions changes the target population; identical ordinal indices can still be shifted. Line-level latent effects and overlapping-pair dependence are uncontrolled by the null, and no season-heldout pages were accessed.
detail.model: Classify each target and immediate predecessor by the first character using acdefgiklmnopqrsy and OTHER (18 classes). Exclude the first line token and do not bridge uncertain tokens. Condition the baseline on target position bins 1, 2–3, 4–6, 7+ (zero indexed), line length bins <=6, 7–10, >10, and paragraph-first-line flag. The position-only class distribution has add-one smoothing. The alternative additionally conditions on predecessor class, with 18 pseudo-observations distributed according to the corresponding baseline. Both use only the fit folios of ZL and sum to one per context. Score each target’s natural-log probability improvement; IT shares the same fit.
detail.split_and_matching: Take the existing public practice-training folios in manuscript order and reserve each fifth folio (38 assigned); fit on the other 154. The original P-L2-031 pilot had used these folios to train its own model; the split is new, but that previous use prevents calling it untouched. For the reserved folios, match ZL and IT paragraph lines by folio and line ID and require equal raw token counts, retaining 538 lines from 737 per witness. Retain only positions present in both where the immediate predecessor and target in each witness are nonempty, certain, ASCII lowercase alphabetic tokens. The same 3,977 positions occur in both; previous and target first-character classes jointly agree in 3,832. Equal length and index do not prove segmentation is aligned; unmatched lines and uncertain words are excluded.
detail.statement: With a more strongly layout-conditioned first-glyph model, gains on a new folio split of the public practice-training data fall to 0.0041 nats per target for ZL and 0.0058 for IT; whole-evaluation-folio bootstrap intervals cross zero for both. All 99 within-folio exact-layout predecessor shuffles score lower, but 100 separately resampled training-folio fits have negative percentile intervals for the gain. The two uncertainty calculations condition on different things. These pages were used during the parent pilot’s training, so this is not an untouched research holdout or a replication of the paper’s unpublished classes.
detail.title: Layout conditioning weakens the public first-glyph gain and training refits are unstable
detail.uncertainty: Bootstrap evaluation folios together with all their rows 2,000 times, seed 31001, and report percentile entries 49 and 1949 for the original fixed fit. Separately draw 100 replacement samples of the training folios, seed 31002, refit both models for each and report sorted entries 2 and 97 against the fixed evaluation rows. The latter is a finite training-resampling sensitivity, not an independently collected model dataset or a joint train/evaluation confidence interval. detail.statement: Public-only partial investigation of K-048-open-1; this does not evaluate the hidden pages. Using the grapheme pool and longest-match tokenizer from the author's released grille.py/signatures_v27.py (https://github.com/labyrinthinesecurity/currier-signatures; token pool encoded in analysis_script), count certain alphabetic words of at least two EVA characters from paragraph lines shared by all three witnesses. Excluded words remain barriers, and words from different lines never form pairs. Fit each grapheme's class on ZL public practice-training pages: start if initial count > twice final, end if final > twice initial, else ambiguous; freeze these classes for all measurements. Restrict to loci common to ZL, IT and RF for both uncertain-space policies. The fixed class set has 22 start, 27 end and 13 ambiguous units; no evaluated boundary uses an unseen class. On public practice evaluation pages, end-to-start rates (and adjacent-pair counts) are ZL split 0.72335 (4475), ZL join 0.73639 (4298), IT split/join 0.71886 (4592), RF split 0.71663 (3723), and RF join 0.72103 (3685). Raw boundary mutual information in bits is 0.39556, 0.36607, 0.38100, 0.38100, 0.42186, 0.41794 respectively; mean MI under 100 fixed-seed whole-word shuffles within each complete eligible run is 0.20395, 0.20195, 0.19582, 0.19582, 0.23484, 0.23252. Shuffle residuals are biased positive, and these are not directly comparable to the paper's corpus-wide figures: the present sample, frozen classes, paragraph-only selection, uncertainty handling and line-local shuffles differ. The witnesses share manuscript pages and transcription conventions; common locus matching does not align each word. This demonstrates only public robustness of these particular descriptive quantities, not the paper's full joint signatures or a language comparison. Current trusted measurement language has no end/start-class statistic whose classes are fitted on training pages and frozen on evaluation pages; hidden evaluation and an independent implementation remain required.

import json, pathlib
import charter_context as c

 p=pathlib.Path('/tmp/voy-llct/corpus')/('book'+str(n)+'.conllu');p.write_bytes(pathlib.Path('/tmp/voy-llct/book'+str(n)+'.conllu').read_bytes());words,info=c.read_words('book'+str(n));rows=run_rows(words,[('us','um')],('internal','internal_same_morph','terminal_same_stem_case'),set());neg=negative_controls(words,thresholds);out[str(n)]={'source':info,'summary':summarized(rows,thresholds),'rows':rows,'negative_acceptances':{m:sum(x['acceptances'][m] for x in neg) for m in c.METHODS}};print(n,json.dumps(out[str(n)]['summary']),flush=True)

detail.statement: The P-L1-018 embedded implementation and SHA-verified LLCT files reproduce every stored calibration and held-apart row, summary, threshold and standalone-letter outcome. The reconstructed plan JSON has a different byte hash, so this is numerical reproduction rather than an exact-byte replay of the original plan or calibration artifact. The five us/um repeats contain 657–658 matched pairs, with only 31–32 unequal right contexts; all 626 terminal pairs tie. The ten standalone-letter tests accepted 7, 6 and 2 cases under unconditioned, position-all and position-info thresholds respectively. For a further exploratory source, the pinned UD Latin ITTB train file contains Aquinas Summa contra gentiles books II–IV. Using the original morphology/left matching and seed 66103, those individual books have respectively 28, 90 and 104 internal same-morphology pairs; books III and IV meet the frozen 40-site minimum. Applying the LLCT-frozen thresholds to each book after examining support, five pairing seeds per book give: position-aware scores rank the planted internal target before the paired alternative in all ten eligible runs, but both candidates fail both position-aware absolute thresholds in all ten. Unconditioned scoring ranks the alternative ahead in all ten and also accepts neither. The terminal same-stem/case arm ties in all fifteen book/seed runs; both position-aware methods accept both candidates in every tie. The standalone-letter acceptance counts in books II, III and IV are 7/10, 7/10, 7/10 unconditioned; 3/10, 4/10, 4/10 position-all; and 1/10 in each position-info. These three books share an author and work, and pairing seeds reuse the text. The exploratory source and matching were chosen after prior results and do not constitute independent manuscripts or confirmatory replication.
